title: Update IR V4 types to match latest finos/morphir spec
description:
The Classic ↔ V4 converter cannot be fully implemented until we update our IR V4 type definitions to match the most recent specification from finos/morphir.

## Background
The steel thread migrate command currently only supports same-format passthrough (V4→V4, Classic→Classic). Cross-format conversion is blocked because our IR V4 types are incomplete - they use `serde_json::Value` placeholders instead of typed expressions.

## References
- V4 Spec: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/
- What's New in V4: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/whats-new.md
- Complete Example: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/complete-example.json

## Current State (What Works)
- Distribution structure (Library/Specs/Application) - matches spec
- FormatVersion (string "4.0.0" or int 4)
- Wrapper object serialization in v4.rs
- TypeAttributes/ValueAttributes with source, constraints, extensions
- Core Type enum (7 variants) - Variable, Reference, Tuple, Record, ExtensibleRecord, Function, Unit
- Core Value enum (18+ variants) including V4-only Hole, Native, External
- Literal types with IntegerLiteral (alias WholeNumberLiteral)
- JSON-level converter works for Classic ↔ V4

## Tasks (Priority Order)

### Phase 1: Serde for Type<A>
- [ ] Implement Serialize for Type<A> with V4 wrapper object format
- [ ] Implement Deserialize for Type<A> with V4 format + shorthand support
- [ ] Add tests with sample V4 type expressions
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/type_expr.rs`, add `serde_v4.rs`

### Phase 2: Serde for Value<TA,VA>
- [ ] Implement Serialize for Value<TA,VA> with V4 wrapper object format
- [ ] Implement Deserialize for Value<TA,VA> with V4 format
- [ ] Add tests with sample V4 value expressions
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/value_expr.rs`

### Phase 3: Replace serde_json::Value placeholders
- [ ] Replace in TypeSpecification.type_expr
- [ ] Replace in ConstructorArgSpec.arg_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueSpecification.inputs/output
- [ ] Replace in TypeDefinition.type_expr
- [ ] Replace in ConstructorArg.arg_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueDefinition.output_type
- [ ] Replace in InputTypeEntry.input_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueBody::ExpressionBody.body
- [ ] Replace in ValueAttributes.inferred_type
- File: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/v4.rs`

### Phase 4: Add IncompleteTypeDefinition
- [ ] Add IncompleteTypeDefinition variant to TypeDefinition enum
- [ ] Include incompleteness reason (similar to HoleReason)
- [ ] Add serialization support
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/type_def.rs`, `v4.rs`

### Phase 5: Integration Tests
- [ ] Test with real V4 IR files from finos/morphir examples
- [ ] Test round-trip conversion: V4 JSON → typed IR → V4 JSON
- [ ] Test Classic → V4 conversion produces valid V4 JSON
- [ ] Add fixtures to integration-tests/fixtures/steel-thread/

## V4 Format Details

### Wrapper Object Format
```json
{"Variable": {"name": "a"}}
{"Reference": {"fqname": "morphir/sdk:list#map", "args": [...]}}
{"Tuple": {"elements": [...]}}
{"Record": {"field-name": type, ...}}
```

### Compact Shorthand (for deserialization)
- Type variable as bare string: `"a"` instead of `{"Variable": {"name": "a"}}`
- Simple reference as FQName: `"morphir/sdk:basics#int"` 
- Reference with args: `{"Reference": ["morphir/sdk:list#list", "a"]}`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Type<A> and Value<TA,VA> implement Serialize + Deserialize
- [ ] All serde_json::Value placeholders replaced with typed expressions
- [ ] Round-trip V4 JSON works (deserialize → serialize = same structure)
- [ ] Classic → V4 converter produces valid typed V4 IR
- [ ] Integration tests pass with real Morphir IR files

## Blocks
- Steel thread P0 completion (cross-format migration)
- morphir-rust-steel-thread

title: Add TOML workspace discovery and runnable pipeline CLI
description: Integrate moonbit-community/toml for Morphir workspace/project configuration. Support canonical TOML layouts, member globs/exclusions/default selection, shared workspace output, script configuration, and CLI filesystem execution across native, JavaScript, WASM and WASM-GC. Preserve legacy JSON inputs. Include manifest encoding/decoding and end-to-end workspace fixtures.
design:
# Morphir workspaces, pipeline execution and hosts

Status: approved and implemented. PR #23 squash-merged as b24d61e41cd7fbd1756b0f8a69908c2e869a3c3a.
Tracker: morphir-ukvn.5.12, under the MoonBit roadmap track morphir-ukvn.5.

## Purpose

Run the same Morphir pipeline against a workspace, project, directory or single file through the CLI or an embedding application. Discover Morphir configuration, apply Scheme configuration and transformations, and return or publish artifacts through explicit host capabilities.

Support native, JavaScript, WASM and WASM-GC builds without coupling the engine to npm, Node, the local filesystem or ambient process state. Runtime support requires a working host adapter as well as a successful compiler build.

## Proposed domain language

These definitions will replace the format-specific entries in CONTEXT.md after design approval.

- Project: a named unit of source, configuration and pipeline execution.
- Workspace: a root that defines project membership, shared configuration and output ownership. It may contain a root project.
- Host: the embedding environment that supplies external capabilities and controls their lifetime.
- Pipeline: a frontend, ordered IR transformations and a backend applied to selected inputs.
- Execution plan: the resolved projects, sources, configuration and stages for one invocation.
- Artifact: a named backend output ready for a host to consume or publish.
- Publication: making a completed set of artifacts available at its destination.

File formats describe projects and workspaces; they do not define those domain concepts.

## Responsibility boundaries

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Entry[CLI or embedding application] --> Runner[Host runner]
  Runner --> Host[Explicit host capabilities]
  Runner --> Discovery[Configuration and workspace discovery]
  Discovery --> Plan[Resolved execution plan]
  Plan --> Engine[Pipeline engine]
  Engine --> Frontend[Frontend to current IR]
  Frontend --> Scheme[Scheme IR transformations]
  Scheme --> Backend[Backend to artifacts]
  Backend --> Runner
  Runner --> Publish[Host publication]
```

Proposed package boundaries:

| Location | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `pkgs/morphir-engine/config` | TOML decoding/encoding, typed settings, merge rules and provenance |
| `pkgs/morphir-engine/workspace` | Portable discovery, member selection and workspace snapshots |
| `pkgs/morphir-engine` | Plans, stage execution, reports and existing frontend/backend registration |
| `pkgs/morphir-host` | Capability contracts, memory host and target-specific adapters/runner |
| `apps/morphir` | Arguments, command dispatch, console presentation and exit status |
| `pkgs/morphir-scheme` | Configuration language, IR transforms and runtime evaluation |

The engine has no dependency on morphir-host. The host runner depends on the engine and supplies snapshots. Shared portable request/result types live with the engine. Platform dependencies belong only in host adapter packages and target-specific files. No process-global registry is required.

## Host abstraction

The current `Host` provides synchronous `read`, `exists` and recursive `list` callbacks. Preserve this API as a compatibility adapter while introducing explicit preparation and publication around it.

Split the host into capabilities so an editor, browser or test can provide only what it supports:

| Capability | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Input access | Inspect entries, enumerate directories and read bounded content within a granted mount |
| Configuration inputs | Supply explicit system/user configuration mounts and an environment map |
| Publication | Stage artifacts, commit a publication and abort staged work; report guarantees |
| Execution control | Cancellation and resource limits checked between reads/stages and within Scheme evaluation |
| Events | Deliver structured progress/diagnostics to the embedding application |

A host mount is an opaque handle with a permitted root. Paths in domain requests are canonical relative paths within that mount. The CLI adapter resolves its working directory and platform configuration locations before entering the engine. The engine never calls cwd, getenv, stdout, filesystem or network APIs directly.

System and user configuration can live outside the workspace through separate read-only mounts. Output is a separate writable capability confined to the resolved workspace output directory. Validate output/source overlap before execution. Check symlink confinement at access time, including publication, rather than relying on string normalization alone.

Configuration discovery receives an immutable tree of directory entries and relevant configuration contents. Selected source contents are then materialized under configured file/byte limits. The first implementation uses bounded snapshots; it does not claim streaming or protection from concurrent source edits. An invocation records the contents it actually used. Source snapshots avoid time-of-check changes during execution.

### Synchronous core, asynchronous hosts

Keep configuration, discovery, planning and IR execution synchronous and deterministic over explicit inputs, following ADR 0002. The host runner may prepare inputs and publish outputs asynchronously when its environment supports that. Browser fetches and asynchronous Node I/O must not force asynchronous operations into every IR procedure.

Do not impose a cross-target MoonBit async dependency before proving its supported target/runtime combinations. Adapter APIs may use their environment's completion mechanism; the shared boundary remains snapshots, plans, artifacts and structured results. A later resumable runner can reduce memory use without changing workspace or IR models.

Scheme receives explicit configuration builders and IR transformation procedures. It receives no filesystem, process or network capabilities implicitly. Future runtime integrations can inject named, typed host procedures under a separate capability policy.

### Required adapters

| Adapter | Runtime contract |
| --- | --- |
| Memory | In-memory mounts, deterministic environment and captured artifacts; usable on all four compiler targets |
| Native | OS arguments, confined filesystem access, platform config discovery and console/exit integration |
| JavaScript | Node CLI adapter; separate injectable embedding API for environments without Node |
| WASM | A documented WASI runner with preopened directories and required imports, verified end to end |
| WASM-GC | Explicit embedding adapter and documented runner/import contract, verified end to end |

The current WASM CLI uses WASI output. Adding filesystem support must preserve a documented standalone WASI route. MoonBit filesystem helpers may introduce runtime-specific imports; a compile-only test cannot establish CLI portability. The first implementation milestone must prove argument, directory, read, write and exit behavior on each promised runtime. If a runtime cannot supply a capability, fail before execution with a structured unsupported-capability error.

Process execution, package downloading and network access are future capabilities. The initial pipeline uses registered in-process frontends/backends.

## Workspace discovery and compatibility

Follow the upstream Morphir discovery contract and reuse its protocol-v1 fixture shapes where possible: development-root FileTree, optional configuration trees, environment and CLI overlay in; WorkspaceSnapshot, sorted ProjectSnapshots and diagnostics out. Unresolved symlink entries are rejected by the pure protocol; adapters may materialize confined targets with cycle/depth/file/byte limits.

At each discovery directory, detect all six primary candidates:

- `morphir.toml`, `morphir.yaml`
- `.morphir/morphir.toml`, `.morphir/morphir.yaml`
- `.config/morphir/config.toml`, `.config/morphir/config.yaml`

More than one candidate is an ambiguity error naming all conflicts. This slice decodes TOML. A sole YAML candidate produces an explicit unsupported-format error; YAML parsing is a follow-up. This is therefore a TOML subset of the upstream configuration contract.

The logical project/workspace root is independent of a configuration file's hidden directory. Resolve `[workspace].root` from the logical discovery root, validate confinement, then expand `members` and apply `exclude` using upstream glob semantics. Deduplicate and sort canonical member paths. Invalid patterns, escaping paths, missing explicit members and invalid default members receive diagnostics. A root `[project]` participates alongside members.

Support selection by canonical member path or project name. Duplicate names make name-based selection ambiguous; path selection remains available. Explicit `--project` wins. From a member directory, choose its owning project. At the workspace root, use `default_member`, then the root project or sole member; otherwise require an explicit selection or `--all`. This fallback is a proposal to check against upstream CLI selection fixtures before implementation.

Keep adapters for existing `morphir.json` and `morphir-workspace.json`. Use legacy manifests only when there is no canonical primary configuration at that logical root. When both exist, use canonical configuration and emit a compatibility warning. This precedence is a proposed MoonBit migration policy, not a claim about upstream behavior.

Directory/file inputs use the same plan and execution types. Without a discovered project, construct an explicit ad hoc project with deterministic defaults. A file invocation selects only that file. Discovery of an enclosing workspace may inherit configuration but must not broaden the requested source selection.

## TOML and configuration resolution

Use `moonbit-community/toml`, initially the inspected version 0.5.0, through a small codec adapter. Preserve the generic TOML document alongside decoded typed settings. Encoding promises semantic round trips, including unknown fields, without preserving comments or layout. Keep TOML numeric/date values intact in retained documents.

Initially consume workspace membership/root/output, project metadata/source/module settings, frontend language, and supported IR settings. Unknown extension sections remain available for round trips. Unsupported requested execution features, such as an unavailable frontend or IR layout, must fail validation rather than silently change behavior.

Apply upstream layers in order:

1. Built-in defaults.
2. System configuration supplied by the host.
3. Global user configuration supplied by the host.
4. Workspace or project primary configuration.
5. Selected member primary configuration.
6. Adjacent workspace then member user overrides.
7. Explicit environment configuration.
8. Explicit CLI overlay for supported options, matching the discovery request contract.

Deep-merge tables, replace arrays, ignore null overlays where representable, and treat secret references as leaves. Retain provenance for winning leaves and arrays so diagnostics can name the declaring file or environment key. Do not resolve secret commands or read secret files in this slice.

Enforce ambiguity checks for global candidates and adjacent TOML/YAML user overrides. Use upstream environment key/value conversion, including double-underscore nesting and operational exclusions such as MORPHIR_HOME. Platform path resolution belongs to host adapters.

Configuration resolution precedes Scheme configuration. Apply workspace script, member script and explicit invocation script in that order. Preserve the existing scalar override and ordered transform composition behavior, then reapply explicit CLI choices as the final override. Validate again before freezing the plan. Transform composition is a language rule distinct from TOML array replacement.

Scripts may configure frontend, backend, source and project metadata before planning. They may not change resolved workspace membership or escape the granted input/output mounts. Existing per-project Scheme sessions retain deterministic sorted-source execution. Script failures identify the script and stage and prevent publication.

## Planning, execution and publication

Run these phases explicitly:

1. Prepare host mounts and configuration snapshot.
2. Discover workspace/project metadata and select inputs.
3. Resolve configuration and evaluate configuration scripts.
4. Validate a fixed execution plan, capabilities and output paths.
5. Materialize selected sources and execute frontend, transforms and backend.
6. Stage and publish successful artifacts under the declared publication policy.

Use the workspace-owned `workspace.out_dir`, default `.morphir/out`. A member's own `out_dir` is ignored with a warning, following upstream rules. Allocate destinations by member path and task, for example `.morphir/out/packages/core/compile.dest/`. The root project's task destination is `.morphir/out/compile.dest/`.

The current engine produces one independent IR distribution per source. Preserve relative source names inside a task destination, for example `compile.dest/src-name.ir.json`. Do not describe these outputs as a linked project distribution. A frontend that supplies a project-wide distribution can produce `morphir-ir.json` through a future project frontend contract. Cross-file linking and dependency resolution require separate compiler work.

For `--all`, finish transformations for every selected project before publication begins. Any configuration or transformation error leaves existing published outputs untouched. Check path collisions before staging and bound staged artifact bytes.

Publication declares its guarantees. A filesystem adapter may provide atomic replacement per task where its runtime supports it. Whole-workspace atomic replacement is not assumed. If a later publication fails, report which task destinations committed and which did not. The command fails and no overall success record is published. Abort removes only the invocation's own staging data; never delete unrelated files. Concurrent writes to the same destination must be serialized or rejected by the adapter.

Return structured diagnostics and publication results. CLI stdout carries requested machine-readable results; progress and errors go to stderr. Proposed statuses: 0 success, 2 invalid invocation/configuration, 1 execution/publication failure, 130 cancellation. Embedding APIs return values without exiting the process.

## Review scenarios and acceptance

- Two members share defaults but override frontend settings independently; provenance explains each effective setting.
- A hidden-layout workspace resolves the same logical root and member destinations as a root-layout workspace.
- Both TOML and YAML exist at a discovery location; the diagnostic lists both and nothing runs.
- Two projects share a name; selecting by path succeeds and selecting by name fails clearly.
- One project's transform fails during `--all`; no new outputs are published.
- Publication fails after an earlier task committed; the report states the actual partial publication.
- A symlink escapes a granted root or forms a cycle; the adapter rejects it deterministically.
- A browser host supplies in-memory files and receives artifacts without filesystem or process APIs.
- Native, Node, WASI and WASM-GC runner fixtures produce equivalent IR and failure diagnostics.
- TOML decode/encode retains known and unknown values semantically; merge tests exercise replacement, provenance and environment rules.
- Legacy manifest and existing memory-host fixtures continue to work.

Use compiler checks and focused conformance/integration tests. Add actual packaged CLI smoke tests on promised runtimes; existing build-only checks are insufficient for host I/O.

## Implementation sequence after approval

1. Prove target host I/O and exit contracts with a tiny disposable fixture. Record exact runtime/import requirements.
2. Add portable configuration codecs and workspace discovery with upstream fixtures.
3. Add capability contracts, memory/native/JavaScript/WASM adapters and publication tests.
4. Connect plans, Scheme configuration and artifact paths while keeping legacy engine calls compatible.
5. Add CLI workspace/project/file/directory selection and end-to-end fixtures; document runner commands.
6. Update CONTEXT.md and ADR 0002 to reflect the approved boundaries, then complete normal review and PR checks.

No implementation commits precede approval of this design. Package boundaries, selection fallback and publication guarantees are proposed decisions for that review.

## Sources inspected

- Existing engine types, discovery/configuration code and ADR 0002 at this repository's merged baseline eb30ebe.
- finos/morphir checkout 5c5307d89f34d876e8f1ebf561ec55efbadf9fa0: `docs/spec/morphir-toml/morphir-toml-specification.md`, `morphir-toml-merge-rules.md`, workspace protocol models and native discovery implementation under `ecosystem/morphir-rust`.
- https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/morphir-toml/morphir-toml-specification.md
- https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/morphir-toml/morphir-toml-merge-rules.md
- https://mooncakes.io/docs/moonbit-community/toml and the installed 0.5.0 package interface inspected during research.
- https://github.com/moonbit-community/toml-parser


## Implementation clarifications

- Upstream fixtures establish that system/global layers and workspace defaults shared with members exclude project identity and workspace-root sections. Member user metadata is inspected for discovery; Scheme scripts only run for selected projects.
- Filesystem publication advertises recoverable task replacement, not atomic directory exchange. Failed rollback preserves its backup and lock for recovery.
- WASI uses only Preview 1 imports with development fd 3. Optional confined system/user config mounts are documented; WASM-GC uses an explicit morphir_host_v1 interface.
- IR output versions 1 through 4 use existing lossless migrations. Unsupported downgrades prevent publication, including absent Scheme member documentation that classic encodings cannot retain.
- Execution plans own Scheme sessions and are single-use. Exposed source/destination arrays are copies.

- Review corrections enforce nested project ownership and honor an explicit MORPHIR_HOME in minimal environments. Both findings have regression tests and answered/resolved review threads.

title: M5: Morphir SDK in MoonBit
description: Fill the morphir-sdk MoonBit package (an 8-line placeholder today): Basics, String (lexical order), List, Maybe, Result, Dict (Elm union semantics), Set, Char, Int (no silent overflow), Decimal, with Elm semantics for modBy, division by zero and ordering, as the E0 spike listed. This is the runtime layer the Morphir-to-MoonBit backend targets. Done when a test suite pins each function's semantics against the Elm SDK behaviour. Spec: design of morphir-ukvn. Reprioritized by Damian 2026-09-26: MoonBit first, basics before the backend.
design:
# Morphir SDK in MoonBit

Status: implemented and merged. M5 completed by PR #26 as 3cabebc011bc52b4d6b008ba3afa36e84349eea4, following initial SDK/hybrid execution in PR #25. Arbitrary-precision integers, truncation toward zero and structured DivisionByZero errors were approved by the maintainer.
Tracker: morphir-ukvn.5.11, under morphir-ukvn.5.
Baseline: 657facc, with M0-M4 and workspace/host support merged.

## Purpose and scope

Implement the reusable runtime library that generated MoonBit programs and the Morphir Scheme backend can call. M5 covers Basics, String, List, Maybe, Result, Dict, Set, Char, Int and Decimal. The pinned upstream IR specifications declare 248 named values across these modules, plus their types and constructors. Inventory every value, its canonical FQName, type/signature, MoonBit binding, semantic source and tests. Do not claim M5 complete with a partial function set.

Dates/times, regex, JSON SDK modules, aggregates, a general evaluator, IR type inference, project linking and the MoonBit code generator remain separate work. Supporting tuples as values does not imply implementing the separate Tuple SDK module.

## Authority and compatibility

Use finos/morphir-elm commit bc99af69a8b24d391311fae3822a87eafef3c334 for Morphir.IR.SDK module signatures and Morphir.SDK source behavior. Use elm/core 1.0.5 and chain-partners/elm-bignum 1.0.1 as pinned behavioral references where the SDK delegates to them. Record source path and version for each fixture. The existing IR fixture pin is compatible with this source pin.

Match Elm behavior in its valid representable domain. General Integer arithmetic must remain exact beyond JavaScript safe integers and machine integers; do not reproduce JavaScript overflow or 32-bit coercion. Keep an explicit compatibility-exceptions list for integer zero divisors, invalid numeric conversions and runtime-specific locale behavior. Exceptions must be resolved and covered by tests before the corresponding implementation is accepted.

Preserve the difference between IR literal representation and runtime values. IR codecs retain decimal lexemes and scale; SDK Decimal operations follow their own numerical and formatting contract and must not rewrite IR literals implicitly.

## Boundaries and package layout

finos/morphir-sdk is a pure, synchronous library usable on native, js, wasm and wasm-gc. It has no dependency on morphir-host, filesystem, environment, process, network, or the Scheme evaluator. Remove the unused morphir-core dependency if compiler inspection confirms it remains unnecessary.

- Root package: shared Order and structured SDK errors; documentation of conventions.
- /integer: the exact integer representation and checked platform conversions, backed by moonbitlang/core/bigint.
- /basics: arithmetic, booleans, comparison and functional helpers. Integer and Float implementations have explicit typed bindings for the future backend's specialization of polymorphic SDK functions.
- /int: opaque Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64 values and checked conversions to/from general Integer.
- /decimal: decimal representation, parsing, arithmetic, rounding and formatting.
- /char and /string: explicit Elm-compatible character/string operations.
- /list, /maybe, /result: immutable functional collections and combinators.
- /dict and /set: ordered immutable collections, with explicit Morphir comparison semantics.
- /conformance: portable fixtures, binding coverage and test helpers.

The canonical IR names remain morphir/SDK module names. MoonBit package names do not change IR names. Record a static binding inventory for future code generation, without introducing a dynamic universal value type into the SDK.

Adapters translate values and errors at the runtime boundary. Scheme backend integration depends on this library; the library does not depend on Scheme. The host can attach source/FQName context to an SDK error and choose how to report it. No SDK function exits the process or writes output.

### Hybrid runtime bindings

Morphir values may be implemented by a portable IR expression, a runtime binding, or both. Bindings may work on all targets or only one. This is a language-independent execution rule. The current `ExpressionBody`, `NativeBody`, and `ExternalBody` with optional fallback can represent these cases without a new IR wire variant. A direct IR evaluator and the Scheme backend must use the same binding resolution contract.

Resolve a matching binding only when the selected target and host have registered it. `ExternalBody` uses the binding or its portable fallback. `NativeBody` requires a binding. `ExpressionBody` evaluates its IR expression unless an explicitly registered, semantically equivalent native accelerator replaces it; the expression remains the fallback. Missing required bindings are reported before invocation. Failure inside an invoked binding propagates; it does not retry the fallback.

The SDK installs default native bindings. A host may register additional builtins and explicitly replace defaults under a documented conflict policy. Bindings carry canonical value identity, target, arity and type information. Resolve and check them before evaluation where possible, while preserving currying, typed values, cancellation, limits, and host capability boundaries in both execution paths. Test native selection, fallback, missing and conflicting bindings, callback behavior, and error propagation through direct IR and Scheme evaluation.

## Representation and semantics

### Integers and floats

Decision approved: general Integer is arbitrary precision. Reuse MoonBit core BigInt behind a Morphir API; check conversion bounds before any machine-sized conversion. Int8-Int64 constructors enforce signed ranges, and narrowing returns Maybe/Option as upstream specifies. Negative values and exact 64-bit boundaries need fixtures.

Integer division truncates toward zero for nonzero divisors. remainderBy retains the dividend sign; modBy retains the divisor sign, with upstream argument order. Approved zero-divisor policy: integerDivide, remainderBy and modBy raise the structured SDK error DivisionByZero. This deliberately replaces Elm JavaScript's 0/NaN outcomes for the first two with a representable error. The runtime or pipeline host catches the error and can attach operation and source context. Float division retains IEEE behavior; Decimal division retains its upstream Maybe return type.

Required examples: integerDivide(-7, 3) = -2; remainderBy(3, -7) = -1; modBy(3, -7) = 2. Test positive and negative dividends/divisors, zero dividends, and zero-divisor errors across all four targets. Do not use a process abort or change canonical SDK results to Result merely to report these errors.

Float operations use Double with IEEE behavior, including NaN and infinity for floating division. Numeric conversion and rounding behavior must be specified per operation; nonfinite Float-to-Integer conversion must not silently yield a machine integer. Finite rounding fixtures include negative halves and values outside 32-bit range. Integer exponentiation rejects a negative exponent where an exact integer result is undefined. Do not route SDK Basics.divide through Scheme rational division.

### Decimal

Use an arbitrary-precision significand and a decimal exponent, with validated public construction. Reuse an existing package only after verifying the required arithmetic, rounding, parsing and all-target behavior. Do not convert exact arithmetic through Double.

Mirror the pinned Decimal reference: round uses half-to-even, truncate uses toward-zero, div returns Maybe and divWithDefault supplies the caller's fallback. The reference defaults to minimum exponent -32 for relevant parsing/division paths; capture its exact behavior with fixtures before encoding a policy. Test 1/3, negative ties, zero divisors, exponent shifts, scientific notation, normalization and fromFloat/toFloat explicitly. Treat nonfinite conversion and locale-independent formatting as deliberate cases.

### Ordering and text

Use lexical string ordering compatible with Elm's UTF-16 comparison, including supplementary characters versus BMP characters. Do not assume MoonBit's default String ordering matches it. The same ordering must drive Basics comparison, List sorting and Dict/Set traversal.

Pin each string operation's indexing unit. Elm String.length and slice count UTF-16 units, while map/toList/uncons handle characters. Test supplementary characters, combining characters, empty separators, negative indices, trimming and case expansion. Host locale must not make behavior differ across targets; specify and test a deterministic policy for toLocaleUpper/toLocaleLower before claiming coverage.

Structural equality must be consistent for supported data values. Callable values are not generally comparable. Keep invalid comparison errors explicit. Dict/Set keys need a coherent comparator; resolve unsupported key cases such as NaN in the binding contract.

### Collections and higher-order calls

List, Dict and Set APIs expose immutable results. Preserve input collections across insert/remove/map/union. Dict.union keeps the left value for duplicate keys, fromList duplicate-key behavior follows Elm, and folds/traversal use the prescribed order. Sorting must preserve upstream stability. Maybe and Result combinators preserve error/default propagation and callback evaluation order. List.innerJoin and leftJoin are part of the inspected Morphir contract.

Native MoonBit APIs use typed callbacks and the upstream argument order. Scheme adapters preserve currying and dispatch higher-order callbacks through the runtime so cancellation, errors and existing execution limits remain effective. Avoid cyclic dependencies between generic comparison helpers and collection packages.

## Dependency reuse

Consult moonrockz packages before introducing an equivalent utility. Inspected registry/organization candidates include expect, moonspec, ion and directories. moonrockz/expect 0.2.0 has only a core/debug package import and is a candidate for test assertions, subject to a four-target compiler check. Moonspec adds a broader dependency graph and is optional for this unit-level corpus. Directories belongs in host adapters and is not needed by the pure SDK. Ion is a serialization package and is not yet verified as a reusable Decimal arithmetic implementation.

Use the pinned MoonBit core BigInt and suitable immutable collection internals where their behavior fits. Keep Morphir semantics in wrappers. Do not add dependencies solely because they are available. Dependency choices and licenses must be recorded when adopted.

## Conformance and acceptance

1. Generate a binding inventory from all ten pinned upstream module specifications. Every one of the 248 values must map to implemented typed functions/adapters and behavioral tests. Constants and nonreturning never also need an explicit mapping.
2. Generate Elm oracle fixtures for normal and boundary inputs and commit their pinned provenance and generation recipe. Execute the upstream SDK where possible, with explicit exceptional-value encoding rather than lossy JSON numbers.
3. Use a separate exact-integer oracle or mathematical fixtures beyond Elm JavaScript's exact range. Classify these as the approved integer extension instead of claiming Elm produced them.
4. Embed fixtures in MoonBit tests so all four targets run identical cases without host I/O. Add algebraic and immutability checks that catch errors beyond examples.
5. Exercise SDK references through actual IR -> Scheme -> runtime calls and compare with direct SDK results. Include curried and higher-order calls, constructor shape, error translation and cancellation. Preserve ordinary Scheme language arithmetic separately from SDK semantics.
6. Run the compiler, focused tests and final existing four-target CI. Verify there are no host-specific imports in the portable SDK. Publish an honest coverage/exception matrix.

## Proposed implementation slices

A. Pin sources, create the complete binding inventory and oracle fixture recipe; establish shared Order/error and exact Integer types.
B. Implement integer arithmetic, Basics numeric operations and fixed-width conversions; verify edge cases across targets.
C. Implement immutable List/Maybe/Result and higher-order conventions.
D. Implement Char/String and comparison; verify Unicode and lexical ordering.
E. Implement Dict/Set using the shared ordering contract and immutable operations.
F. Implement Decimal against the pinned reference corpus.
G. Integrate the Scheme SDK bridge, finish remaining Basics polymorphic/functions, verify all inventory entries, document the package and run full CI.

Each implementation slice records its commit range and tests in beads. Keep plans/designs in beads and ignored .dev renders. No source implementation is included in this design draft.

## Sources inspected

- Local finos/morphir-elm checkout at bc99af69a8b24d391311fae3822a87eafef3c334: src/Morphir/IR/SDK/{Basics,String,List,Maybe,Result,Dict,Set,Char,Int,Decimal}.elm and src/Morphir/SDK/{Int,Decimal}.elm.
- Local elm/core 1.0.5: Elm/Kernel/Basics.js, Elm/Kernel/Utils.js, Elm/Kernel/String.js.
- Local chain-partners/elm-bignum 1.0.1: src/Decimal.elm.
- pkgs/morphir-scheme/{numbers.mbt,backend/runtime.mbt}; docs/adr/0002-scheme-and-engine.md.
- Mooncakes registry entries for moonrockz packages and https://api.github.com/orgs/moonrockz/repos.
- https://github.com/moonrockz/expect ; https://mooncakes.io/docs/moonbitlang/core/bigint.

## Pinned value inventory

### Basics: 53 values

add, subtract, multiply, divide, integerDivide, power, toFloat, round, floor, ceiling, truncate, modBy, remainderBy, negate, abs, clamp, isNaN, isInfinite, sqrt, logBase, e, pi, cos, sin, tan, acos, asin, atan, atan2, degrees, radians, turns, toPolar, fromPolar, equal, notEqual, lessThan, greaterThan, lessThanOrEqual, greaterThanOrEqual, max, min, compare, not, and, or, xor, append, identity, always, composeLeft, composeRight, never

### String: 44 values

isEmpty, length, reverse, repeat, replace, append, concat, split, join, words, lines, slice, left, right, dropLeft, dropRight, contains, startsWith, endsWith, indexes, indices, toInt, fromInt, toFloat, fromFloat, fromChar, cons, uncons, toList, fromList, toUpper, toLower, pad, padLeft, padRight, trim, trimLeft, trimRight, map, filter, foldl, foldr, any, all

### List: 39 values

singleton, repeat, range, cons, map, indexedMap, foldl, foldr, filter, filterMap, length, reverse, member, all, any, maximum, minimum, sum, product, append, concat, concatMap, intersperse, map2, map3, map4, map5, sort, sortBy, sortWith, isEmpty, head, tail, take, drop, partition, unzip, innerJoin, leftJoin

### Maybe: 8 values

andThen, map, map2, map3, map4, map5, withDefault, hasValue

### Result: 10 values

andThen, map, map2, map3, map4, map5, withDefault, toMaybe, fromMaybe, mapError

### Dict: 22 values

empty, singleton, insert, update, remove, isEmpty, member, get, size, keys, values, toList, fromList, map, foldl, foldr, filter, partition, union, intersect, diff, merge

### Set: 17 values

# Morphir SDK in MoonBit

Status: design draft. Arbitrary-precision integers approved by Damian in this conversation. Integer zero-divisor policy is pending confirmation. Implementation has not started.
Tracker: morphir-ukvn.5.11, under morphir-ukvn.5.
Baseline: 657facc, with M0-M4 and workspace/host support merged.

## Purpose and scope

Implement the reusable runtime library that generated MoonBit programs and the Morphir Scheme backend can call. M5 covers Basics, String, List, Maybe, Result, Dict, Set, Char, Int and Decimal. The pinned upstream IR specifications declare 248 named values across these modules, plus their types and constructors. Inventory every value, its canonical FQName, type/signature, MoonBit binding, semantic source and tests. Do not claim M5 complete with a partial function set.

Dates/times, regex, JSON SDK modules, aggregates, a general evaluator, IR type inference, project linking and the MoonBit code generator remain separate work. Supporting tuples as values does not imply implementing the separate Tuple SDK module.

## Authority and compatibility

Use finos/morphir-elm commit bc99af69a8b24d391311fae3822a87eafef3c334 for Morphir.IR.SDK module signatures and Morphir.SDK source behavior. Use elm/core 1.0.5 and chain-partners/elm-bignum 1.0.1 as pinned behavioral references where the SDK delegates to them. Record source path and version for each fixture. The existing IR fixture pin is compatible with this source pin.

Match Elm behavior in its valid representable domain. General Integer arithmetic must remain exact beyond JavaScript safe integers and machine integers; do not reproduce JavaScript overflow or 32-bit coercion. Keep an explicit compatibility-exceptions list for integer zero divisors, invalid numeric conversions and runtime-specific locale behavior. Exceptions must be resolved and covered by tests before the corresponding implementation is accepted.

Preserve the difference between IR literal representation and runtime values. IR codecs retain decimal lexemes and scale; SDK Decimal operations follow their own numerical and formatting contract and must not rewrite IR literals implicitly.

## Boundaries and package layout

finos/morphir-sdk is a pure, synchronous library usable on native, js, wasm and wasm-gc. It has no dependency on morphir-host, filesystem, environment, process, network, or the Scheme evaluator. Remove the unused morphir-core dependency if compiler inspection confirms it remains unnecessary.

- Root package: shared Order and structured SDK errors; documentation of conventions.
- /integer: the exact integer representation and checked platform conversions, backed by moonbitlang/core/bigint.
- /basics: arithmetic, booleans, comparison and functional helpers. Integer and Float implementations have explicit typed bindings for the future backend's specialization of polymorphic SDK functions.
- /int: opaque Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64 values and checked conversions to/from general Integer.
- /decimal: decimal representation, parsing, arithmetic, rounding and formatting.
- /char and /string: explicit Elm-compatible character/string operations.
- /list, /maybe, /result: immutable functional collections and combinators.
- /dict and /set: ordered immutable collections, with explicit Morphir comparison semantics.
- /conformance: portable fixtures, binding coverage and test helpers.

The canonical IR names remain morphir/SDK module names. MoonBit package names do not change IR names. Record a static binding inventory for future code generation, without introducing a dynamic universal value type into the SDK.

Adapters translate values and errors at the runtime boundary. Scheme backend integration depends on this library; the library does not depend on Scheme. The host can attach source/FQName context to an SDK error and choose how to report it. No SDK function exits the process or writes output.

## Representation and semantics

### Integers and floats

Decision approved: general Integer is arbitrary precision. Reuse MoonBit core BigInt behind a Morphir API; check conversion bounds before any machine-sized conversion. Int8-Int64 constructors enforce signed ranges, and narrowing returns Maybe/Option as upstream specifies. Negative values and exact 64-bit boundaries need fixtures.

Integer division truncates toward zero for nonzero divisors. remainderBy retains the dividend sign; modBy retains the divisor sign, with upstream argument order. Proposed zero-divisor policy: a structured error for integerDivide, remainderBy and modBy. This deliberately replaces Elm JavaScript's 0/NaN outcomes for the first two with a representable error; user confirmation is pending.

Float operations use Double with IEEE behavior, including NaN and infinity for floating division. Numeric conversion and rounding behavior must be specified per operation; nonfinite Float-to-Integer conversion must not silently yield a machine integer. Finite rounding fixtures include negative halves and values outside 32-bit range. Integer exponentiation rejects a negative exponent where an exact integer result is undefined. Do not route SDK Basics.divide through Scheme rational division.

### Decimal

Use an arbitrary-precision significand and a decimal exponent, with validated public construction. Reuse an existing package only after verifying the required arithmetic, rounding, parsing and all-target behavior. Do not convert exact arithmetic through Double.

Mirror the pinned Decimal reference: round uses half-to-even, truncate uses toward-zero, div returns Maybe and divWithDefault supplies the caller's fallback. The reference defaults to minimum exponent -32 for relevant parsing/division paths; capture its exact behavior with fixtures before encoding a policy. Test 1/3, negative ties, zero divisors, exponent shifts, scientific notation, normalization and fromFloat/toFloat explicitly. Treat nonfinite conversion and locale-independent formatting as deliberate cases.

### Ordering and text

Use lexical string ordering compatible with Elm's UTF-16 comparison, including supplementary characters versus BMP characters. Do not assume MoonBit's default String ordering matches it. The same ordering must drive Basics comparison, List sorting and Dict/Set traversal.

Pin each string operation's indexing unit. Elm String.length and slice count UTF-16 units, while map/toList/uncons handle characters. Test supplementary characters, combining characters, empty separators, negative indices, trimming and case expansion. Host locale must not make behavior differ across targets; specify and test a deterministic policy for toLocaleUpper/toLocaleLower before claiming coverage.

Structural equality must be consistent for supported data values. Callable values are not generally comparable. Keep invalid comparison errors explicit. Dict/Set keys need a coherent comparator; resolve unsupported key cases such as NaN in the binding contract.

### Collections and higher-order calls

List, Dict and Set APIs expose immutable results. Preserve input collections across insert/remove/map/union. Dict.union keeps the left value for duplicate keys, fromList duplicate-key behavior follows Elm, and folds/traversal use the prescribed order. Sorting must preserve upstream stability. Maybe and Result combinators preserve error/default propagation and callback evaluation order. List.innerJoin and leftJoin are part of the inspected Morphir contract.

Native MoonBit APIs use typed callbacks and the upstream argument order. Scheme adapters preserve currying and dispatch higher-order callbacks through the runtime so cancellation, errors and existing execution limits remain effective. Avoid cyclic dependencies between generic comparison helpers and collection packages.

## Dependency reuse

Consult moonrockz packages before introducing an equivalent utility. Inspected registry/organization candidates include expect, moonspec, ion and directories. moonrockz/expect 0.2.0 has only a core/debug package import and is a candidate for test assertions, subject to a four-target compiler check. Moonspec adds a broader dependency graph and is optional for this unit-level corpus. Directories belongs in host adapters and is not needed by the pure SDK. Ion is a serialization package and is not yet verified as a reusable Decimal arithmetic implementation.

Use the pinned MoonBit core BigInt and suitable immutable collection internals where their behavior fits. Keep Morphir semantics in wrappers. Do not add dependencies solely because they are available. Dependency choices and licenses must be recorded when adopted.

## Conformance and acceptance

1. Generate a binding inventory from all ten pinned upstream module specifications. Every one of the 248 values must map to implemented typed functions/adapters and behavioral tests. Constants and nonreturning never also need an explicit mapping.
2. Generate Elm oracle fixtures for normal and boundary inputs and commit their pinned provenance and generation recipe. Execute the upstream SDK where possible, with explicit exceptional-value encoding rather than lossy JSON numbers.
3. Use a separate exact-integer oracle or mathematical fixtures beyond Elm JavaScript's exact range. Classify these as the approved integer extension instead of claiming Elm produced them.
4. Embed fixtures in MoonBit tests so all four targets run identical cases without host I/O. Add algebraic and immutability checks that catch errors beyond examples.
5. Exercise SDK references through actual IR -> Scheme -> runtime calls and compare with direct SDK results. Include curried and higher-order calls, constructor shape, error translation and cancellation. Preserve ordinary Scheme language arithmetic separately from SDK semantics.
6. Run the compiler, focused tests and final existing four-target CI. Verify there are no host-specific imports in the portable SDK. Publish an honest coverage/exception matrix.

## Proposed implementation slices

A. Pin sources, create the complete binding inventory and oracle fixture recipe; establish shared Order/error and exact Integer types.
B. Implement integer arithmetic, Basics numeric operations and fixed-width conversions; verify edge cases across targets.
C. Implement immutable List/Maybe/Result and higher-order conventions.
D. Implement Char/String and comparison; verify Unicode and lexical ordering.
E. Implement Dict/Set using the shared ordering contract and immutable operations.
F. Implement Decimal against the pinned reference corpus.
G. Integrate the Scheme SDK bridge, finish remaining Basics polymorphic/functions, verify all inventory entries, document the package and run full CI.

Each implementation slice records its commit range and tests in beads. Keep plans/designs in beads and ignored .dev renders. No source implementation is included in this design draft.

finos/morphir-sdk is a pure, synchronous library usable on native, js, wasm and wasm-gc. It has no dependency on morphir-host, filesystem, environment, process, network, or the Scheme evaluator. Remove the unused morphir-core dependency if compiler inspection confirms it remains unnecessary.

- Root package: shared Order and structured SDK errors; documentation of conventions.
- /integer: the exact integer representation and checked platform conversions, backed by moonbitlang/core/bigint.
- /basics: arithmetic, booleans, comparison and functional helpers. Integer and Float implementations have explicit typed bindings for the future backend's specialization of polymorphic SDK functions.
- /int: opaque Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64 values and checked conversions to/from general Integer.
- /decimal: decimal representation, parsing, arithmetic, rounding and formatting.
- /char and /string: explicit Elm-compatible character/string operations.
- /list, /maybe, /result: immutable functional collections and combinators.
- /dict and /set: ordered immutable collections, with explicit Morphir comparison semantics.
- /conformance: portable fixtures, binding coverage and test helpers.

The canonical IR names remain morphir/SDK module names. MoonBit package names do not change IR names. Record a static binding inventory for future code generation, without introducing a dynamic universal value type into the SDK.

Adapters translate values and errors at the runtime boundary. Scheme backend integration depends on this library; the library does not depend on Scheme. The host can attach source/FQName context to an SDK error and choose how to report it. No SDK function exits the process or writes output.

### Hybrid runtime bindings

Morphir values may be implemented by a portable IR expression, a target-specific runtime binding, or both. This is a language-independent execution rule. The current `ExpressionBody`, `NativeBody`, and `ExternalBody` with optional fallback can represent these cases without a new IR wire variant. A direct IR evaluator and the Scheme backend must use the same binding resolution contract.

Resolve a matching binding only when the selected target and host have registered it. A hybrid value uses the registered binding; otherwise it evaluates its portable fallback. Missing bindings without a fallback are reported before invocation. Failure inside an invoked binding propagates; it does not retry the fallback. `NativeBody` requires a binding. `ExpressionBody` evaluates its IR expression.

The SDK installs default native bindings. A host may register additional builtins and explicitly replace defaults under a documented conflict policy. Bindings carry canonical value identity, target, arity and type information. Resolve and check them before evaluation where possible, while preserving currying, typed values, cancellation, limits, and host capability boundaries in both execution paths. Test native selection, fallback, missing and conflicting bindings, callback behavior, and error propagation through direct IR and Scheme evaluation.

## Representation and semantics

### Integers and floats

Decision approved: general Integer is arbitrary precision. Reuse MoonBit core BigInt behind a Morphir API; check conversion bounds before any machine-sized conversion. Int8-Int64 constructors enforce signed ranges, and narrowing returns Maybe/Option as upstream specifies. Negative values and exact 64-bit boundaries need fixtures.

Integer division truncates toward zero for nonzero divisors. remainderBy retains the dividend sign; modBy retains the divisor sign, with upstream argument order. Approved zero-divisor policy: integerDivide, remainderBy and modBy raise the structured SDK error DivisionByZero. This deliberately replaces Elm JavaScript's 0/NaN outcomes for the first two with a representable error. The runtime or pipeline host catches the error and can attach operation and source context. Float division retains IEEE behavior; Decimal division retains its upstream Maybe return type.

Required examples: integerDivide(-7, 3) = -2; remainderBy(3, -7) = -1; modBy(3, -7) = 2. Test positive and negative dividends/divisors, zero dividends, and zero-divisor errors across all four targets. Do not use a process abort or change canonical SDK results to Result merely to report these errors.

Float operations use Double with IEEE behavior, including NaN and infinity for floating division. Numeric conversion and rounding behavior must be specified per operation; nonfinite Float-to-Integer conversion must not silently yield a machine integer. Finite rounding fixtures include negative halves and values outside 32-bit range. Integer exponentiation rejects a negative exponent where an exact integer result is undefined. Do not route SDK Basics.divide through Scheme rational division.

### Decimal

Use an arbitrary-precision significand and a decimal exponent, with validated public construction. Reuse an existing package only after verifying the required arithmetic, rounding, parsing and all-target behavior. Do not convert exact arithmetic through Double.

Mirror the pinned Decimal reference: round uses half-to-even, truncate uses toward-zero, div returns Maybe and divWithDefault supplies the caller's fallback. The reference defaults to minimum exponent -32 for relevant parsing/division paths; capture its exact behavior with fixtures before encoding a policy. Test 1/3, negative ties, zero divisors, exponent shifts, scientific notation, normalization and fromFloat/toFloat explicitly. Treat nonfinite conversion and locale-independent formatting as deliberate cases.

### Ordering and text

Use lexical string ordering compatible with Elm's UTF-16 comparison, including supplementary characters versus BMP characters. Do not assume MoonBit's default String ordering matches it. The same ordering must drive Basics comparison, List sorting and Dict/Set traversal.

Pin each string operation's indexing unit. Elm String.length and slice count UTF-16 units, while map/toList/uncons handle characters. Test supplementary characters, combining characters, empty separators, negative indices, trimming and case expansion. Host locale must not make behavior differ across targets; specify and test a deterministic policy for toLocaleUpper/toLocaleLower before claiming coverage.

Structural equality must be consistent for supported data values. Callable values are not generally comparable. Keep invalid comparison errors explicit. Dict/Set keys need a coherent comparator; resolve unsupported key cases such as NaN in the binding contract.

### Collections and higher-order calls

List, Dict and Set APIs expose immutable results. Preserve input collections across insert/remove/map/union. Dict.union keeps the left value for duplicate keys, fromList duplicate-key behavior follows Elm, and folds/traversal use the prescribed order. Sorting must preserve upstream stability. Maybe and Result combinators preserve error/default propagation and callback evaluation order. List.innerJoin and leftJoin are part of the inspected Morphir contract.

Native MoonBit APIs use typed callbacks and the upstream argument order. Scheme adapters preserve currying and dispatch higher-order callbacks through the runtime so cancellation, errors and existing execution limits remain effective. Avoid cyclic dependencies between generic comparison helpers and collection packages.

## Dependency reuse

Consult moonrockz packages before introducing an equivalent utility. Inspected registry/organization candidates include expect, moonspec, ion and directories. moonrockz/expect 0.2.0 has only a core/debug package import and is a candidate for test assertions, subject to a four-target compiler check. Moonspec adds a broader dependency graph and is optional for this unit-level corpus. Directories belongs in host adapters and is not needed by the pure SDK. Ion is a serialization package and is not yet verified as a reusable Decimal arithmetic implementation.

Use the pinned MoonBit core BigInt and suitable immutable collection internals where their behavior fits. Keep Morphir semantics in wrappers. Do not add dependencies solely because they are available. Dependency choices and licenses must be recorded when adopted.

## Conformance and acceptance

1. Generate a binding inventory from all ten pinned upstream module specifications. Every one of the 248 values must map to implemented typed functions/adapters and behavioral tests. Constants and nonreturning never also need an explicit mapping.
2. Generate Elm oracle fixtures for normal and boundary inputs and commit their pinned provenance and generation recipe. Execute the upstream SDK where possible, with explicit exceptional-value encoding rather than lossy JSON numbers.
3. Use a separate exact-integer oracle or mathematical fixtures beyond Elm JavaScript's exact range. Classify these as the approved integer extension instead of claiming Elm produced them.
4. Embed fixtures in MoonBit tests so all four targets run identical cases without host I/O. Add algebraic and immutability checks that catch errors beyond examples.
5. Exercise SDK references through actual IR -> Scheme -> runtime calls and compare with direct SDK results. Include curried and higher-order calls, constructor shape, error translation and cancellation. Preserve ordinary Scheme language arithmetic separately from SDK semantics.
6. Run the compiler, focused tests and final existing four-target CI. Verify there are no host-specific imports in the portable SDK. Publish an honest coverage/exception matrix.

## Proposed implementation slices

A. Pin sources, create the complete binding inventory and oracle fixture recipe; establish shared Order/error and exact Integer types.
B. Implement integer arithmetic, Basics numeric operations and fixed-width conversions; verify edge cases across targets.
C. Implement immutable List/Maybe/Result and higher-order conventions.
D. Implement Char/String and comparison; verify Unicode and lexical ordering.
E. Implement Dict/Set using the shared ordering contract and immutable operations.
F. Implement Decimal against the pinned reference corpus.
G. Integrate the Scheme SDK bridge, finish remaining Basics polymorphic/functions, verify all inventory entries, document the package and run full CI.

Each implementation slice records its commit range and tests in beads. Keep plans/designs in beads and ignored .dev renders. No source implementation is included in this design draft.

design:
# MoonBit tooling acquisition and embedding

Status: implemented and squash merged in PR #28 as 6cedfbe8eebbddc3fabb75ad3133a1c977c35d03, 2026-09-30. Scope: finos/morphir-moonbit only. The Rust CLI in finos/morphir has
independent implementation and acceptance evidence.

## Contract and hosts

Provide a portable MoonBit toolchain service under morphir-host/toolchain. A host
supplies argument-based process execution, filesystem operations, environment and
cancellation. Process execution returns exit status, stdout and stderr, with a
timeout. The service owns tool selection, version validation and orchestration;
the engine does not acquire global filesystem/process dependencies.

Use the pinned compiler 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9 and its matching core. Explicit selection
uses --home or MORPHIR_MOON_HOME; otherwise prefer the managed version, then a
system installation. An invalid explicit installation must fail rather than fall
back silently. Validation checks compiler identity and runs a compilation and
execution smoke fixture against the selected core. MOON_HOME and executable paths
are set for each child, without changing the caller environment or shell profiles.

Native and Node hosts provide process execution. WASM-GC hosts can provide it
through the existing host ABI; the Node runner supplies the adapter. Plain WASI
Preview 1 does not provide subprocess/download capabilities and returns an
explicit unsupported-capability diagnostic. Hosts can use the portable service
with their own adapters. JSON and JSON Lines are available on every CLI command,
including unsupported cases.

## CLI acquisition

Commands: toolchain info, setup, build, run, and exec. --home selects a toolchain,
--target selects a compiler target, run --package selects a package, and arguments
after -- go only to the program. setup requires --yes before network acquisition.
Existing matching installations are reused without network access. Managed
installations live under MORPHIR_HOME/toolchains or the user Morphir directory.

Download native tools and core from version-specific official URLs. Extract in a
new staging directory under an exclusive installation lock; bundle core, validate,
then rename to publish. Failures remove task-owned staging data and release the
lock. Existing installations are never overwritten. Support official native
archives for macOS arm64 and Linux x64 initially; unsupported installation
platforms are explicit. Existing toolchains and injectable hosts remain usable on
other platforms. All child commands use argv, never interpolated shell commands.
Archive selection is pinned and HTTPS-only; record archive integrity in the managed
receipt. Network acquisition tests use isolated installation roots.

## Embedding

Expose an asynchronous JS embedding API for browser and non-browser applications.
Pin @moonbit/moonc-worker to 0.1.202609203, whose compiler identifies revision
7d59c7ec9. Keep it optional and outside the CLI's startup path. An embedding host
supplies the compiler adapter, interfaces/core dependencies, runtime imports and
asset loading. Provide a worker transport with request IDs, disposal, error
propagation and cancellation by terminating the worker. Calls serialize compiler
access because the upstream compiler has mutable state.

Compilation accepts in-memory source files, package metadata, .mi interfaces and
.core dependencies; links Wasm with explicit exports. Execution instantiates with
host-provided imports and calls a selected export. Full moon build/package-manager
semantics are not implied by this package compiler API. Browser and Node worker
tests must compile real source, execute its result and exercise diagnostics and
termination. Browser execution uses a real headless browser, not a simulated DOM.
Non-browser embedding must work without an installed CLI.

## Delivery and evidence

1. Host/process contract, acquisition service and structured CLI commands.
2. Embedded compiler/runtime API and worker transports with real Node/browser tests.
3. Required repository gates, four-target CLI checks, installed npm checks and PR
   review. Squash merge under the existing authorization, then close beads with
   commit/test evidence and remove branches and temporary assets.

E1 remains separate and can proceed through acquisition. Embedding is a general
host integration mode; browsers motivate it where CLI acquisition is unavailable.
The feasibility bead closes on demonstrated browser/non-browser compilation and
execution, with documented capability limits and remaining integration work.
acceptance_criteria: On a supported machine without MoonBit, the MoonBit CLI can acquire a pinned, version-matched toolchain and demonstrate compilation and the supported execution workflow. Repeated setup reuses the installation; explicit and existing system installations are discoverable and validated. All new CLI commands support JSON and JSON Lines. Host boundaries and unsupported capabilities are explicit.
notes:
Completed 2026-09-30 in finos/morphir-moonbit PR #28, squash merged as 6cedfbe8eebbddc3fabb75ad3133a1c977c35d03. Implementation range 9581fcf..6820756. Full local check and hosted CI pass: 553 tests on each native/JS/Wasm/Wasm GC target, all-target CLI integrations and installed npm CLI. Nine embedding tests plus real Chromium pass. Production npm dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities. All three automated review findings were verified, fixed, answered and resolved. MoonBit maintainer permission was reported by Damian on Discord on 2026-09-30. Completion is specific to this repository and does not complete the independent Rust CLI in finos/morphir.

The CLI implements toolchain info/setup/build/run/exec with JSON and JSON Lines. Host callbacks own process/filesystem effects, explicit argv, child-only environment, cancellation and timeouts. Setup validates the compiler and matching core with compilation/execution, acquires official pinned macOS arm64 and Linux x64 archives with SHA-256 checks and consent, stages publication under an exclusive lock, writes a receipt and reuses installations. Actual acquisition/reuse/execution from empty isolated directories passed on macOS locally and Linux in CI. Unsupported acquisition hosts and missing moonx are reflected in capabilities. Existing installations remain usable where process adapters support them. WASI and native Windows process limits are documented. Official archive retention can require a reviewed pin refresh; fetched binary archives are not redistributed by this change.

E1 (.5.2), the Morphir-to-MoonBit backend, is now unblocked. Existing CLI target tests do not complete E2 or finos/morphir Rust CLI integration.

Review findings answered and resolved. Scope: morphir-moonbit only; capability limits and remaining integrations documented in notes.

comments.text: Maintainer report, 2026-09-30: Damian received approval from MoonBit maintainers on Discord to use the MoonBit compiler and execution tooling, including moonc and the moon run/moonx paths. Support two distribution modes: tooling acquisition through our CLI and embedding, with embedding especially relevant for browser scenarios. comments.author: Damian Reeves
comments.text: Maintainer clarification, 2026-09-30: embedding is a general distribution/integration mode for MoonBit compiler and execution tooling across hosts. Browsers are a motivating use case because our CLI acquisition path is unavailable there, not the boundary of embedding support. The design must also address embedding in non-browser applications and hosts through the same host abstraction. Keep supported host capabilities and completion evidence explicit; acquisition and embedding remain separate modes.
