Design before bd-plan stored .dev/designs/morphir-moonbit-backend.html:

# Morphir-to-MoonBit backend

Status: draft under discussion, 2026-09-30. The build/publication boundary is pending Damian's selection; do not treat this draft as approved. Damian selected a MoonBit generator and integration with the MoonBit CLI. Tracker: morphir-ukvn.5.2. Baseline: 6cedfbe. Authority: roadmap morphir-ukvn and the reconciled Track 5 handoff.

## Outcome and boundaries

Add the `moonbit` backend to finos/morphir-moonbit. A user supplies a versioned IR library document, selects the IR JSON frontend and MoonBit backend, and receives a MoonBit library project that the pinned compiler builds against finos/morphir-sdk. Generation is portable and returns artifacts; publication and tool execution remain host responsibilities. The generator is MoonBit, as requested by Damian. It does not wait for A2 or A7.

E1 establishes source generation and compilation acceptance here. E2 owns execution across targets and evaluator equivalence. The umbrella Rust CLI and released MEP extension installation require separate work and evidence. A MoonBit package is not itself a released MEP component, and this implementation must not claim that integration is complete.

## First delivery contract

Start with complete, nongeneric library definitions. Support scalar SDK types, closed records, tuples, lists, Maybe and Result, custom types, aliases, ordinary functions and top-level recursion. Support literals, variables, local and cross-module references, applications, closures with binding/wildcard parameters, local nonrecursive definitions, conditionals, tuples/lists/records, field access and record updates, and custom/SDK constructors. The SDK binding allowlist is explicit and documents which typed calls are emitted. Arithmetic uses the existing exact Integer implementation and Float specialization; strings and characters use SDK Text and Character. Supported SDK errors propagate rather than becoming target-specific traps.

Reject unsupported constructs with a backend diagnostic before publication: generic definitions, extensible records, holes/incomplete definitions, document literals, pattern matching/destructuring beyond supported lambda patterns, local mutual recursion, unresolved dependencies, opaque implementations, and native/external definitions without a supported portable fallback. Do not erase type information, guess a numeric specialization, or generate placeholder bodies. Initial unsupported features remain visible follow-up capabilities, not claims of complete IR or SDK code generation.

The public generator entry accepts current v4 semantic IR. The existing IR JSON frontend reads versions 1-4 and explicitly migrates through morphir-ir/migration. A library API accepting versioned IR performs that same explicit migration. The generator is not a general IR type inferencer. Use declared signatures, local binding types, referenced definitions, expression structure and consistent inferred-type annotations to determine the types needed for emission. Ambiguous unsupported cases fail explicitly. The MoonBit compiler is the source of truth for generated language typing.

## Portable package and artifacts

Create finos/morphir-moonbit in pkgs/morphir-moonbit, depending on morphir-ir. It has no filesystem, process, network, host, engine, Scheme evaluator or compiler dependency. An artifact has a portable relative path and text content. Generation returns the entire artifact set only on success.

Emit moon.mod, moon.pkg, model.mbt and a machine-readable symbol manifest. The module imports finos/morphir-sdk at its current exact module version. Do not vendor a compiler or embed absolute checkout paths. Consumers resolve the SDK using MoonBit's normal module facilities; offline acceptance supplies the local SDK in an isolated moon.work. Acceptance must build the actual published CLI output, not a manually reconstructed source file. Registry availability and SDK release publication are separate from local compilation acceptance.

Flatten IR modules into one MoonBit package initially. This avoids imposing MoonBit package-cycle restrictions on legal Morphir module references and recursive types. Names encode canonical FQNames injectively with explicit symbol prefixes. Local variables and fields also use injective canonical-name encoding, avoiding keywords, initialism collisions and generated-name capture. The manifest records canonical Morphir names, generated names and accessibility. Private modules/values remain private; custom-type constructor access follows the IR access controls. Do not advertise source mapping beyond these symbol names.

Closed record shapes are interned structurally and emitted as nominal MoonBit structs. Canonical ordering makes artifact content stable regardless of map insertion order. Resolve aliases when matching a shape. Unsupported recursive alias expansion fails with context. Custom types become enums. Preserve parameter and constructor argument order. Never infer semantics from documentation or annotations.

Functions use unary curried closures, including higher-order values. Zero-input definitions are functions evaluated when referenced, avoiding eager global initialization. SDK calls use typed adapters to bridge curried Morphir functions and uncurried SDK APIs. Backend numeric specialization follows concrete resolved argument/result types. Preserve conditional and boolean short-circuit evaluation. Generation never executes a model.

## Engine integration

Keep Engine::register_backend compatible for existing one-file backends. Add register_artifact_backend for backends emitting multiple relative paths beneath a per-source output directory. Represent backend output explicitly rather than overloading a filename or embedding a project in JSON.

For source src/model.json, the moonbit backend owns model.moonbit/ under the existing task output directory. Separate IR documents generate separate projects; cross-document linking is outside this slice. Nested source paths retain their hierarchy. The engine validates every returned artifact path before appending any output from that source. Reject empty, absolute, traversal, backslash, drive, duplicate and file/directory-overlap paths, including normalization collisions. Backend output never chooses a host root. Plans check duplicate per-source roots. Execute and legacy run enforce the same path rules.

`processed` retains its current meaning of emitted artifacts. Reports retain provenance on every file. Host staging, destination replacement, limits and failure behavior remain unchanged. Any selected transformation diagnostic prevents publication. The new backend participates in source discovery, transforms, dry runs, JSON and JSON Lines through the existing pipeline.

## Pending engine integration decision

Damian asked how buildable library projects integrate into the engine. The initial proposal generates one project per complete IR library document, not a merged project assembled from multiple source files. The engine currently compiles each source individually. Multi-source library assembly needs a distinct project-level linking design.

The initial proposal uses a separate explicit toolchain build command. The alternative under discussion adds an explicit build stage before publication, so compiler failure preserves the previous output. In that case, multi-artifact output alone is insufficient: backend results need project/build metadata, and a host capability must build staged or in-memory inputs without leaking publication paths into the engine. The current Publication contract has only stage/commit/abort, and its filesystem staging directory is private. The generic build contract and SDK resolution must be settled before implementing this part. Compile validation of generated source also differs from publication of compiled binary artifacts, which the current text Artifact cannot represent.

## CLI and toolchain

Use `morphir run <model.json> --frontend ir-json --backend moonbit`. Configuration may set pipeline.backend='moonbit'. Generation never downloads or runs tools implicitly. Users can build the resulting project with the existing `morphir toolchain build <project>` provider or with their version-matched MoonBit installation. Preserve explicit --home, cancellation and acquisition behavior.

The first acceptance fixture is a typed pricing library with records, an enum, a cross-module function, a conditional and exact integer SDK arithmetic. Include another historical v3 input and a failure fixture. Pin moonc 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9 and matching core. Compile the generated project through moon build and the existing toolchain build command. Do not interpret the current SDK or CLI target suites as generated-model acceptance.

## Validation

Focused portable tests verify representative code generation, deterministic content, scoped references, accessibility, arbitrary-precision literals, unsupported constructs and versioned input. Engine tests exercise both APIs, safe relative paths, duplicate outputs and all-or-nothing per-source output. Host tests preserve previous publications when a later source fails and replace stale project files on success.

A Node acceptance script invokes the actual CLI, checks structured output, materializes generated projects, supplies only the pinned local SDK dependency through moon.work, and builds with the real compiler. Include it in existing CLI CI rather than relying on unrun examples. Existing four-target tests, CLI packaging checks, lint, formatting and package validation must pass before any push.

## References

- Current IR: pkgs/morphir-ir/versions/v4/{types,values,packages}.mbt.
- SDK binding inventory: pkgs/morphir-sdk/conformance/bindings.json.
- Existing engine backend API: pkgs/morphir-engine/types.mbt and engine.mbt.
- Host publication contract: pkgs/morphir-host/README.md.
- MoonBit error/effect rules: https://docs.moonbitlang.com/en/latest/language/error-handling.html.
- MoonBit module configuration: https://docs.moonbitlang.com/en/latest/toolchain/moon/module.html.

Pinned compiler experiments and generated-project compilation take precedence over nightly documentation when syntax differs.

Morphir / MoonBit
E1 design · Revision 0.1
September 30, 2026
01 · Intent and scope02 · Current architecture03 · Domain terms04 · Pipeline walkthrough05 · Component boundaries06 · Stage graph07 · Data contracts08 · Library assembly09 · MoonBit generation10 · Dependency resolution11 · Build and host lifecycle12 · Publication and failure13 · Configuration14 · Pluggability and transports15 · Diagnostics and limits16 · Compatibility and migration17 · Acceptance and delivery18 · Decisions to iterate19 · Evidence and references
Contents

Local review document.
Contract sketches are proposals.

Track 5 · Morphir to WASM · E1

Buildable libraries in a pluggable pipeline

A MoonBit backend that returns a complete library project. A configurable build stage that validates it through an explicit host provider. Publication happens only after the selected stages succeed.

Draft for iterationmorphir-ukvn.5.2Baseline 6cedfbeMoonBit implementation
Direction agreed; contracts still under design.

Damian selected a MoonBit generator and CLI integration and endorsed the modular stage boundaries. This revision develops the full design before implementation. Build-before-publication is the recommended configured path, with source-only generation also available. The precise contracts, delivery scope, and decision list remain proposals.

Self-contained HTML. No external assets, network requests, or account connections. The interactive walkthrough illustrates proposed behavior; it does not run a compiler.

01 / Outcome

Make the library project a first-class output

The user-facing result is a generated MoonBit library with enough source, manifests, and dependency information to build through a chosen host. The engine coordinates typed stages and output ownership. Language-specific generation and compilation live in replaceable components.

E1 owns

  • A portable MoonBit generator using the current Morphir IR and SDK.
  • Multiple artifacts and generated-project metadata from a backend.
  • An explicit library build-validation stage and host adapter.
  • Source-only and generate-and-build pipeline configurations.
  • Real CLI, compiler, failure, and publication acceptance in this repository.

Separate completion evidence

  • E2 executes generated models across targets and compares evaluator results.
  • A7 owns the MoonBit source frontend and broader extension work.
  • The Rust CLI in finos/morphir needs its own integration and tests.
  • A released MEP/WIT component requires protocol, packaging, and release evidence.
  • Publishing SDK or compiler releases remains separate from local build validation.

Architecture requirements

  1. Frontends, assembly, transforms, backends, build providers, and publishers have distinct contracts.
  2. Pipeline configuration selects components and stages without embedding MoonBit rules in the engine.
  3. Pure stages can execute without filesystem, network, process, or compiler access.
  4. Host effects are explicit, capability checked, cancellable, and bounded.
  5. A failed generation, dependency resolution, or build does not replace previously published output.
  6. Unsupported IR, bindings, or host capabilities produce diagnostics, never placeholder output.
02 / Existing code

Extend the current separation of engine and host

Verified against the working tree at 6cedfbe. None of the new contracts below are implemented yet.
AreaCurrent behaviorDesign change
FrontendSource → IRFile. Each source produces a separate distribution.Adapt results into a collection of IR units with stable identities and provenance.
TransformsScheme transforms accept and return current IR per source.Keep package transforms; make their placement and order explicit.
BackendIRFile → String, with one filename suffix.Return artifact sets and generated-project descriptions.
PlanningResolves configuration, registered components, sources, and task destinations. Plans are single-use.Also validate stage connections, provider requirements, and output ownership rules.
Host runnerSnapshots source contents, runs the engine, then publishes successful artifacts.Orchestrate materialization, dependency resolution, and build validation before publication.
Publicationstage / commit / abort; recoverable replacement per task with an exclusive filesystem lock.Keep replacement semantics. Acquire the publication lock after builds succeed.
ToolchainOptional provider with describe / request. Acquired tools build on-disk projects; embedded tools compile in-memory packages.Add a project-build adapter and precise capability requirements. Preserve existing operations.
ArtifactsPaths, one source path, and text content. processed counts successful artifacts.A new typed result adds multiple-source provenance, projects, and build receipts. Legacy reports remain compatible.

The native baseline suite passed all 553 tests before this design work. That establishes the starting point; it is not evidence that E1 works.

Embedded package compilation is not a complete project builder.

The embedded adapter needs host-supplied interfaces and core dependencies. It does not resolve a moon.mod dependency graph, and the synchronous MoonBit boundary does not automatically bridge an asynchronous JavaScript worker. Both gaps must remain explicit.

03 / Vocabulary

Keep Morphir projects and generated projects distinct

Existing definitions in CONTEXT.md continue to apply. The following additions are proposed for the glossary after the design settles.

TermMeaning
Morphir projectA named unit of source, configuration, and pipeline execution discovered in a Morphir workspace.
IR unitAn independently identified IR distribution with provenance. It may already contain a complete library package.
Library assemblyCombining compatible IR units into one package while retaining identities, access, and references. It is distinct from resolving external implementations.
Generated projectA backend output whose source and manifests form a build unit for a particular toolchain. One Morphir project may produce several generated projects.
Build validationCompiling a generated project to establish that the selected compiler accepts it. E1 validates a library; it does not execute that library's model.
Build receiptEvidence that a particular input set and dependency set passed a build with an identified toolchain and target.
Build workspaceHost-owned temporary storage or an in-memory session used to resolve and compile one generated project.
Stage componentA registered implementation of one typed pipeline operation. Its transport and host requirements are separate from its pipeline role.
PublicationMaking a completed output set available at its destination. A compiler accepting a scratch copy is not publication.
04 / End-to-end behavior

Follow one library through the pipeline

Choose a scenario to see the stage boundary and publication result. All four paths use the same generation contract.

1 · Pure stageFrontendSnapshot → current IR units
2 · Pure stageAssemble + transformIndependent or assembled libraries
3 · Pure stageBackendIR → files + project descriptions
4 · EngineValidate outputsOwnership, paths, identities
5 · Host effectPrepare build workspaceCopy inputs; resolve dependencies
6 · Provider effectValidate buildCompiler + core + dependency set
7 · HostCollect accepted outputsSources + build receipts
8 · Publisher effectPublish taskStage → replace → cleanup

Build before publication

Generation returns an immutable source set. The host builds a private copy with explicitly resolved dependencies. If every required build succeeds, it publishes the sources and receipt together. Compiler caches and incidental files stay in the private build workspace.

A concrete input and output

Input snapshot
  morphir.toml
  src/pricing.ir.json       # one complete multi-module library

Published task after successful build
  .morphir/out/compile.dest/
    dist/pricing.ir.moonbit/
      moon.mod
      moon.pkg
      model.mbt
      symbols.json
      morphir-build.json    # emitted only after verified build success

Private host state, never published by E1
  build workspace / provider handle
  resolved SDK and matching core
  compiler outputs, caches, temporary logs

The .moonbit suffix is an output-layout convention selected by the registered backend adapter. The generic engine does not special-case that suffix or the filenames inside it.

05 / Ownership

Put each decision in the component that owns it

Portable semantics

Engine + stage components

  • Resolve effective configuration and a typed stage graph.
  • Decode, migrate, assemble, transform, and generate IR.
  • Validate identities, paths, references, and declared output ownership.
  • Describe build requirements without invoking host effects.
  • Produce diagnostics and immutable results.
External capabilities

Host runner + providers

  • Snapshot and materialize files.
  • Select installed or embedded tools.
  • Resolve dependency assets under an explicit policy.
  • Perform asynchronous or process compilation.
  • Enforce deadlines, cancellation, and workspace cleanup.
Visibility and recovery

Publisher

  • Receive the final accepted artifact set.
  • Enforce destination confinement.
  • Stage files and replace task destinations.
  • Report actual committed destinations.
  • Preserve backups if rollback fails.

Proposed package placement

morphir-ir
  current and versioned IR, explicit migrations

morphir-engine
  typed result contracts, stage catalog, planner, pure executor
  no dependency on morphir-host

morphir-moonbit                          # new portable module
  symbol/type lowering, SDK adapters, source/project emission
  depends on morphir-ir; no engine/host/compiler dependency

morphir-host
  runner, build workspace leases, provider selection, publication
  adapts generated projects to toolchain/provider requests

morphir-host/toolchain
  acquired MoonBit compiler selection and process execution

morphir-host/embedding
  asynchronous embedded package compilation and host-supplied dependencies

apps/morphir
  component registration, CLI flags, host wiring, structured reports

The generator has its own lightweight output type so it does not depend on the engine. A registration adapter translates it to the shared pipeline contracts. This avoids a dependency cycle and makes the generator directly usable by other hosts.

Start shared stage contracts inside morphir-engine. Extract a transport-neutral contract package only when a second transport needs it; do not create a broad plugin SDK speculatively.

06 / Configurable execution

A typed stage graph, not an arbitrary shell workflow

The planner expands a preset or explicit stage list into a directed acyclic graph. Each node names a registered component, its scope, typed input connections, and immutable options. Edges carry named values; they do not refer to whatever files happen to exist in a directory.

RoleInput → outputScope and effect
FrontendSource snapshot → IR unitsSource or project scope, according to declared capability. Existing callbacks remain source-scoped.
AssemblyIR units → library unitsProject scope, pure. Identity assembly supports complete library documents.
TransformLibrary units → library unitsPackage scope, pure except explicitly supplied runtime capabilities. Existing Scheme adapters remain supported.
BackendLibrary units → generation batchPackage or project scope, pure. Language-specific manifests remain opaque to the engine.
Build validationGeneration batch → validated batch + receiptsGenerated-project scope, host effect through a selected provider.
PublicationAccepted batch → publication reportTask scope, host effect. Depends on every required stage for that task.

Planning rules

  • Reject cycles, duplicate node IDs, unknown components, incompatible ports, unsupported options, and outputs with no ownership rule.
  • Every required build must have a compatible provider. A generation-only plan needs no toolchain.
  • Track backend language separately from compiler target: moonbit is a backend; wasm is a build target.
  • Configuration can choose a direct generation-to-publication edge or insert build validation.
  • Publication receives one explicit output selection. A future fan-out must merge through a collision-checking stage before publication.
  • Execution is sequential and deterministic initially. The graph permits future independent scheduling without making concurrency an E1 acceptance requirement.
Dry run resolves structure, not model semantics.

It shows sources, destinations, stage connections, provider requirements, and unresolved capability checks. It does not read source bodies, compile, acquire tools, or promise that a model is supported. Checks requiring generated manifests or IR semantics run during execution.

Runner and synchronous core

The engine owns graph validation and pure stage execution. The host runner drives the plan and awaits effect stages. A native synchronous runner can use the same stage order; a JavaScript runner awaits workers and I/O between pure calls. A provider-owned Promise is never hidden inside a synchronous MoonBit callback.

The first implementation can split the plan into a pure generation phase and a host build/publication phase. Preserve explicit graph identities and contracts now; a general resumable interpreter is a later implementation choice if additional mixed-effect stages justify it.

07 / Proposed contracts

Carry artifacts, projects, and evidence separately

These sketches define semantics, not final MoonBit field names or a published wire protocol. IDs and relative paths are validated value types rather than unvalidated strings.

IRUnit {
  id: UnitId
  distribution: CurrentIR
  provenance: SourceProvenance[]
}

Artifact {
  id: ArtifactId
  path: RelativePath
  content: Utf8Text | BinaryBytes
  media_type: String
  provenance: SourceProvenance[]
}

GeneratedProject {
  id: GeneratedProjectId
  root: RelativePath
  kind: Library
  toolchain_family: ComponentId
  artifact_ids: ArtifactId[]
  dependency_requirements: DependencyRequirement[]
  backend_metadata: VersionedData
}

GenerationBatch {
  artifacts: Artifact[]
  projects: GeneratedProject[]
}

BuildRequest {
  project_id: GeneratedProjectId
  provider_id: ComponentId
  operation: ValidateLibrary
  target: String
  dependency_policy: DependencyPolicy
  options: VersionedData
}

BuildReceipt {
  project_id: GeneratedProjectId
  input_digest: Digest
  resolved_dependencies: DependencyIdentity[]
  toolchain_identity: ToolchainIdentity
  target: String
  successful: Bool
  diagnostics: Diagnostic[]
}

ValidatedBatch {
  generation: GenerationBatch
  receipts: BuildReceipt[]
}

Contract invariants

  1. A backend returns its entire batch or a failed result. Partial file lists never become successful projects.
  2. Every project member references exactly one artifact in the batch, beneath the project's declared root. Overlapping project roots are rejected initially.
  3. The engine assigns task-relative ownership. A backend cannot select an absolute host destination.
  4. Validate all paths and file/directory conflicts before accepting the batch. Reject traversal, drive paths, NUL, duplicate IDs, normalized collisions, and ancestor overlaps. Filesystem publication also detects case-insensitive collisions.
  5. The runner supplies the build policy. A backend describes compatibility requirements; it cannot silently request acquisition, execution, or network access.
  6. A build receipt is bound to the exact source and resolved dependency identities. It is invalid if those inputs change.
  7. Successful generation without a build has no successful build receipt. Reports identify generated, validated, and published separately.

Binary data and compatibility

E1 publishes text source, manifests, and receipts. The new artifact contract should permit bytes so later compiled outputs do not need to masquerade as text. An in-process adapter can carry bytes directly; component/process transports use bounded attachments or a versioned encoding. Opaque native pointers are never portable references.

The existing Artifact and Report APIs remain available through a text-only adapter. A new result version carries projects and receipts. Legacy callers receive an explicit incompatibility diagnostic if they request a result they cannot represent.

Why a file list alone is insufficient

A file list tells the publisher what to write, but not which files form a build unit, which compiler family is required, which dependencies were used, or whether the source has been validated. Project metadata and build receipts let the pipeline answer those questions without teaching the engine to interpret moon.mod.

08 / Source and library boundaries

Model assembly independently of emission

A JSON IR input may already contain several modules and their library dependencies. In that case, identity assembly passes the complete library to the backend. Several JSON files are not automatically fragments of one package.

E1 default: independent libraries

One complete library IR document yields one generated project. Preserve source-relative hierarchy, giving src/pricing.ir.json the root pricing.ir.moonbit/ under the adapter's output naming rule. A backend-specific option can instead select an explicitly configured stable root; naming collisions still fail validation.

No cross-document linking is implied. References must resolve inside the library or through explicitly supported dependencies.

Optional future: assembled library

A registered assembly component combines compatible module units. It checks package identity, module uniqueness, dependencies, visibility, signatures, and duplicate definitions. It preserves canonical FQNames and many-source provenance.

This is a separate capability with its own acceptance. The pipeline includes the stage boundary now without claiming a linker has been implemented.

Assembly rules when enabled

  • Inputs must explicitly declare they are fragments of the same package or be mapped by a supported assembly contract. Configuration does not arbitrarily rewrite FQNames.
  • Duplicate modules or values are errors unless a separately designed merge operation explains how they combine.
  • External dependency specifications with incompatible identities or signatures are errors.
  • Private implementation details stay private. Project exposed_modules is applied at a documented point after assembly and before package transforms.
  • Reference checking and dependency resolution remain distinct. Finding a specification does not manufacture an implementation.
  • Top-level mutual recursion and module cycles remain semantic IR concerns; flattening the generated MoonBit package can avoid imposing new package cycles.
Scope proposal, not an approved reduction.

Ship identity assembly with E1's complete-library path first. If project-level multi-source assembly is required for E1 itself, give it a separate design slice and tests before source generation. The broader pipeline supports either choice.

09 / Backend internals

Generate typed MoonBit without changing Morphir semantics

Current IR library
  → index declarations and signatures
  → resolve references, access, aliases, and supported bindings
  → check required type information and backend capabilities
  → lower types, effects, currying, and record shapes
  → emit deterministic source and MoonBit manifests
  → return project description, symbols, and artifacts

Versioned input

The ir-json frontend decodes a versioned document and uses existing explicit migrations to current v4 IR. The generator accepts current IR. A direct versioned API can reuse the same migration path and must preserve migration diagnostics. IR v4 support follows this repository's semantic model; it is not a claim of complete upstream YAML or document-tree protocol support.

Symbols and access

Use stable injective encodings of canonical FQNames for top-level symbols, plus separate prefixes for locals, fields, constructors, and generated temporaries. Preserve distinctions such as initialisms and word segments. Emit symbols.json linking Morphir names to generated declarations and access. Strings in code, comments, filenames, and manifests use the correct escaping for their destination.

The initial layout is one MoonBit module containing one flattened package. That permits Morphir cross-module references without introducing MoonBit package cycles. Private values remain private. Public signatures depending on inaccessible types and constructor visibility require explicit validation; nominal enum syntax must not accidentally expose private constructors. Full line-level source maps are a later capability.

Types and functions

Morphir conceptMoonBit lowering and checks
General IntSDK Integer with arbitrary precision. Parse the original lexeme; never coerce through a host Number or machine Int.
Float / Bool / UnitDouble / Bool / Unit with literal validation and documented Float edge behavior.
String / CharSDK Text / Character, retaining UTF-16 behavior and SDK comparison rules.
DecimalSDK Decimal operations. Preserve IR literal lexemes until explicit construction; do not rewrite wire data.
Tuple, Maybe, Result, ListMoonBit tuples and SDK-compatible Option, Result and immutable List mappings. Preserve Result type parameter order.
Closed recordsIntern canonical structural shapes as nominal structs. Resolve aliases, retain field identity, and unify equivalent shapes across modules.
Aliases / custom typesValidated aliases and enums. Detect unsupported alias cycles; preserve constructor parameter order and access.
FunctionsUnary curried functions/closures. Adapt uncurried SDK callbacks explicitly. Preserve evaluation order and captured bindings.
Zero-input definitionsAccessor functions evaluate on reference rather than introducing eager global initialization.
Native / external bodiesResolve only explicitly registered target-compatible implementations. Missing required bindings fail. Use a portable fallback only when no binding is selected, never after an invoked binding fails.

Type information and effect handling

The generator is not a general type inference engine. Use declared inputs/outputs, indexed reference signatures, bound variables, expected types, and consistent inferred-type annotations. Reject ambiguous numeric specialization or contradictory information with symbol and expression context. The compiler determines generated MoonBit language typing; semantic mapping and compatibility still require backend validation and focused tests.

Raising SDK calls must propagate structured SDK errors through generated function and callback effects. Conditional branches remain conditional. Fully applied boolean and/or retain short-circuit behavior. Equality, ordering, partial application, and higher-order callbacks must use the Morphir SDK rules rather than accidentally inheriting host rules.

Coverage ladder

Delivery sliceProposed coverageEvidence required
First buildable libraryComplete nongeneric libraries; scalar types, closed records, aliases, custom types, tuples and basic collections; references, calls, closures, lets, conditionals, fields and updates; audited SDK allowlist.Typed pricing fixture with multiple modules, constructors, exact arithmetic, higher-order behavior, and real compiler acceptance.
Expression coveragePattern matching/destructuring, local recursion, constructor/list/literal patterns, and remaining supported expressions.Independent fixtures and evaluator comparisons when E2 begins; diagnostics for unsupported cases until supported.
Generic and constrained coverageGeneric public declarations, comparable/number constraints, generic records and recursive structures.Explicit strategy for constraints and exported generics. Monomorphization alone cannot implement an arbitrary public generic library API.
Binding coverageEach SDK value classified as direct call, adapter, specialization, or unsupported. Target-specific external implementations require registration.Audit all 248 SDK inventory entries; every claimed generated binding has compilation and semantic evidence.

Extensible records, holes, incomplete bodies, document literals, unsupported SDK modules, unresolved external implementations, and unsupported distributions fail explicitly until their semantics are designed. A limited first release is labeled as such; it does not claim complete IR or SDK generation.

10 / Build inputs

Make dependency resolution explicit and reproducible

The backend names semantic dependencies and emits language manifests. A provider-specific resolver maps them to concrete packages, interfaces, and compiled assets. The engine carries dependency identities without implementing MoonBit's package resolver.

  1. The generated project requires an identified Morphir SDK release or source snapshot, not merely whichever local module happens to have version 0.1.0.
  2. The host configuration selects a dependency policy and approved sources. A provider reports which operations and policies it can enforce.
  3. The resolver freezes actual dependency identities and compiler/core compatibility before compilation. Reject mismatched SDK bindings, interfaces, or core assets.
  4. The receipt records resolved identities and content digests. Stable source output contains no absolute checkout paths or temporary build handles.
PolicyBehaviorAcceptance boundary
Offline / suppliedUse an explicit cache, local module map, or supplied interfaces/cores. Missing dependencies fail; no network fallback.Primary E1 acceptance uses an isolated local SDK mapping and pinned matching core.
Locked networkResolve only approved pinned identities, verifying supplied integrity information. Network access must be authorized by configuration and provider capability.Requires tests proving the actual MoonBit resolver behavior and available integrity contracts. A raw moon build subprocess does not establish this guarantee.
Unresolved source exportEmit portable manifests and dependency requirements without claiming resolution or compilation.Valid for source-only output. The report says generated, not validated.

SDK and compiler pins

The current acquisition service pins moonc 0.10.14+7d59c7ec9 and matching core. The embedded package uses @moonbit/moonc-worker 0.1.202609203, identifying the same revision. Select and verify the pair through the provider, not a literal embedded in generic engine logic.

The SDK inventory's semantic reference is Morphir Elm commit bc99af69a8b24d391311fae3822a87eafef3c334. That semantic pin is not the identity of a published MoonBit SDK package. Acceptance must record the actual MoonBit SDK source digest or release used.

Standalone distribution still needs release evidence.

A local moon.work proving compilation against this checkout does not prove that a user can fetch the SDK from a public registry. Verify the registry/release path separately before advertising a standalone install-and-build experience. Release publication remains subject to maintainer approval.

11 / Effects and lifecycle

Build in a private workspace, then publish

The build-stage adapter consumes a generated project and build request. The host creates an isolated workspace lease, resolves dependencies, and invokes the selected provider. The engine never sees the physical scratch path. A process adapter translates the lease to an on-disk directory; an embedded adapter can keep inputs and dependencies in memory.

runner:
  generation = execute_pure_stages(plan, source_snapshot)
  require_generation_success(generation)

  for required_project in selected_builds:
    with host.prepare_build_workspace(project, policy) as lease:
      resolved_inputs = host.resolve_dependencies(lease, project)
      result = await provider.validate_library(lease, request)
      receipt = verify_result_matches_inputs(result, resolved_inputs)
      collect_receipt(receipt)
      # cleanup the lease on success, error, or cancellation

  require_all_required_builds_successful()
  final_outputs = select_sources_and_verified_receipts()
  publish_task_destinations(final_outputs)

Conceptual pseudocode. Native callers use a synchronous adapter. JavaScript hosts await real asynchronous effects. Existing provider requests need an adapter; this is not a new supported method today.

Lease responsibilities

  • Give each invocation its own workspace. Prevent two providers from mutating the same source tree concurrently.
  • Bind a lease to its host, invocation, project, and allowed operations. Release is idempotent; reuse after disposal fails.
  • Keep generated inputs immutable in the accepted batch. Build a private copy and verify its source identity. Reject unexpected manifest/source rewrites or record an explicit transformation as a new artifact set.
  • Separate compiler output/cache directories from publication input. Copy only declared, validated outputs back into the accepted batch.
  • On cleanup failure, report the retained workspace location or host handle for recovery. Never remove unrelated caches or other invocations' files.

What does build success mean?

A receipt requires the selected compiler to report success for the declared library build, the correct compiler/core pair, the frozen dependency set, and the required project/package checks. Where a provider contract promises build products, verify their presence and identity. An exit code of zero from the wrong directory, an old artifact, or an info probe is not acceptance.

E1 publishes generated source and receipt. Compiled binaries, interfaces, and target-specific runtime bundles remain private build products unless a later output-selection contract explicitly includes them. Executing the model is not part of build validation.

Capability selection

A requested build is required, not opportunistic. Missing provider, incompatible compiler, unsupported target, absent dependency resolver, or absent workspace capability causes a diagnostic before publication. There is no silent fallback to source-only success. Source-only mode succeeds without any provider because that mode does not request compilation.

Toolchain setup is a separate explicit operation. Build never installs tooling implicitly. Preserve existing configured-home precedence and diagnostics rather than adding another compiler discovery path.

Embedded execution

A full generated module build may need a dependency graph, interfaces, core linking, and manifest interpretation. The current embedded compiler provides package compilation, not all of those services. Advertise package-compile and project-build separately. A host can satisfy the latter with its own project adapter and supplied dependency graph; until then a requested project build fails capability negotiation.

A future resumable engine can suspend at a host-effect node and consume a correlated result. The first JS host can instead orchestrate the explicit pure-generation/build/publication phases. Both require per-invocation state, cancellation, and stale-response rejection; neither blocks the worker inside the synchronous engine.

12 / Transaction boundary

Preserve the last successful task output

Complete generation, dependency resolution, and every required build before opening the publication transaction. Then stage the final sources and verified receipts through the existing publisher. The build scratch workspace is separate from the publisher's locked staging directory.

Failure pointEffect on publicationRecovery/report
Invalid configuration or graphNo source execution or publication.Configuration/plan diagnostic with component and connection.
IR migration, assembly, transform, generationNo replacement for any selected task.Relevant source/symbol diagnostics; scratch cleanup if allocated.
Dependency resolution or compiler failureNo publication transaction begins.Build diagnostic and failed receipt/result; previous output remains.
Cancellation before commitDo not start the next commit. Clean invocation-owned scratch/staging.Cancelled outcome. A provider that cannot interrupt must disclose its boundary.
Task commit failureFilesystem publisher attempts to restore that task's backup.Publication error; report actual committed task destinations.
Rollback or cleanup failureKeep required backup/lock for recovery.Report retained recovery state. Do not claim a successful cleanup.
Task replacement is recoverable, not workspace-atomic.

All selected builds finish before any task is published. A later publication I/O failure can still occur after an earlier task has committed. Preserve the current committed reporting and publisher guarantee. Do not describe several task replacements as one atomic transaction.

Stale outputs and incomplete success

A successful task replacement removes old generated files and old build receipts. Source-only publication replaces the destination with source-only output, so a previous receipt cannot survive and imply a new build succeeded. If a required build fails, the previous successful directory may remain on disk, but this invocation's report explicitly says it did not publish.

The final output selection excludes compiler caches, downloaded dependency directories, temporary logs, and undeclared files. Protect destinations and task ownership at both engine and host boundaries.

13 / Public configuration proposal

Choose stages, providers, and build policy independently

The shorthand below preserves frontend.language and pipeline.backend. New fields are illustrative and require validation, precedence, help, and structured-output support before they become supported syntax.

[project]
name = "Pricing"
source_directory = "src"

[frontend]
language = "ir-json"

[pipeline]
backend = "moonbit"
mode = "generate-and-build"       # or "generate"
assembly = "independent-library"

[pipeline.output]
root_naming = "source-stem"        # one independent library per IR document

[pipeline.build]
provider = "moonbit-process"
target = "wasm"
operation = "validate-library"
dependencies = "offline-supplied"
timeout_ms = 120000

[toolchains.moonbit]
# Host resolves an explicit home, managed installation, or system toolchain.
# No absolute host path is written into the generated project.

[backend.moonbit]
layout = "flat-package"
sdk = "finos/morphir-sdk"
# The supported schema defines an exact release/source identity.

Explicit graph form

An explicit graph lets an embedding host replace assembly, add transforms, select a different backend, or omit build validation. Stage IDs and roles remain stable even when implementations change. The shorthand expands into this same internal model.

[[pipeline.stages]]
id = "read-ir"
role = "frontend"
uses = "ir-json"

[[pipeline.stages]]
id = "library"
role = "assembly"
uses = "independent-library"
needs = ["read-ir"]

[[pipeline.stages]]
id = "source"
role = "backend"
uses = "moonbit"
needs = ["library"]

[[pipeline.stages]]
id = "check"
role = "build"
uses = "moonbit-project-build"
needs = ["source"]
provider = "moonbit-process"
target = "wasm"

[[pipeline.stages]]
id = "publish"
role = "publication"
uses = "host-publisher"
needs = ["check"]

For source-only output, omit check and connect publication to source. Selecting a preset and an explicit graph simultaneously is an error. Role-specific schemas reject unknown settings; provider IDs are registered capabilities, not executable names or arbitrary shell commands.

Precedence and scripts

Preserve the current project resolver's system/global/environment, workspace/project manifest, Scheme script, and explicit override behavior. Normalize the resulting settings once into the stage graph. Existing Scheme transform order is retained. For explicit graphs, replace the graph as a whole rather than deep-merging stage arrays by accident. Component options use their declared merge/validation rules.

CLI proposal

# Existing flags, new backend. Source-only preset remains possible.
morphir run src/pricing.ir.json --frontend ir-json --backend moonbit

# Proposed flags, not implemented yet.
morphir run . --pipeline-mode generate-and-build --build-target wasm --json
morphir run . --pipeline-mode generate --json-lines
morphir run . --dry-run --json

# Existing explicit tooling remains supported.
morphir toolchain setup --yes
morphir toolchain build path/to/generated/project --target wasm

Do not overload --target: project listing currently uses it to filter backend names, while toolchain commands use it for compiler targets. A new pipeline build option should be explicit and reflected in configuration provenance.

14 / Components and transport

Register by capability; keep transport replaceable

The component catalog describes stable IDs, contract versions, roles, input/output types, execution scope, supported IR families, component-specific option schemas, and required host capabilities. Runtime compatibility is checked before a stage receives inputs. Registration conflicts fail unless an explicit override policy is selected.

TransportHow it fitsBoundary
In-process MoonBitDirect typed callbacks behind the catalog. E1's first generator implementation.Pure generator receives no ambient host capabilities. Not a claim of OS isolation.
Process extensionAdapter encodes requests/results with contract versions and bounded attachments.Host owns process lifecycle, paths, cancellation, protocol errors, and limits.
WIT/WASM componentFuture adapter maps typed stage contracts to approved Morphir interfaces/worlds.Use approved WIT/MEP authority. Do not invent an unrelated release protocol or claim an internal package is a component release.
Async JS embeddingHost runner awaits provider requests around portable stages.Workers, dependency assets, binary transfers, disposal, and concurrency remain explicit.

Provider manifest

A build provider advertises operation kind, input mode, target support, toolchain identity, dependency-resolution policy support, cancellation behavior, and limits. Existing protocolVersion / operations / targets / mode fields remain available. New project-level claims need their own versioned capability description; compile capability alone is insufficient.

Two providers may satisfy the same build-stage contract. Their receipts must expose what was actually used. The host chooses one through configuration; the engine does not silently swap process and embedded modes after failure.

A deliberately small first catalog

Register existing Scheme and IR JSON adapters, identity assembly, the MoonBit backend, a MoonBit project-build adapter, and the host publisher. Do not add a plugin downloader, arbitrary workflow language, or universal dynamic value runtime merely to make these stages pluggable.

15 / Observable behavior

Report the stage and the affected library

Diagnostics have stable codes, severity, stage/component IDs, project/unit IDs, source provenance, optional Morphir FQName/expression location, a message, and structured details. Preserve the original compiler diagnostics and streams even when an adapter can extract richer locations. Only map a compiler location back to IR when a verified mapping exists.

code:        "build.compiler_failed"
stage:       "check"
component:   "moonbit-project-build"
project:     "Pricing"
generated:   "pricing-library"
source:      "src/pricing.ir.json"
message:     "The selected MoonBit compiler rejected the generated library."
details:     { target, toolchain_identity, exit_code, compiler_diagnostics }
published:   false

Events and reports

Retain human, JSON, and JSON Lines output for every invocation, including help, dry run, failure, and cancellation. Add schema-versioned stage start/finish, dependency resolution, build result, and publication events. Correlate each event with the invocation and generated project. Diagnostics on stderr do not corrupt structured stdout.

The legacy processed count keeps its artifact meaning. New reports give separate source/unit, generated-project, validated-project, artifact, and committed-task counts. Never count a failed or merely generated library as built.

Limits and cancellation

  • Enforce source and output budgets, file counts, dependency depth/bytes, expression traversal depth, manifest size, and compiler-output limits.
  • Use a total build deadline as well as bounded individual process calls; per-call timeouts alone do not bound a resolver/build sequence.
  • Check cancellation between stages, within long generator traversals, before effects, after provider completion, and before publication commits.
  • Process interruption and worker termination are adapter capabilities. In-process embedded compilation cannot promise interruption while executing synchronous compiler code.
  • Correlate responses to stage/invocation IDs. A late result after cancellation or disposal cannot resume another run or publish stale outputs.
16 / Migration strategy

Keep existing callers working while adding richer results

  1. Add new typed backend/project results and adapters without changing the behavior of register_backend.
  2. Wrap existing one-string backends as a one-artifact generation result with no generated project or required build.
  3. Keep current Engine::run and Engine::execute available for pure generation. Introduce a richer graph execution result rather than making them acquire compilers.
  4. Extend Host::run or add a versioned runner to execute required build stages. Plain generation plans still work with existing publishers and no provider.
  5. Use additive provider capability negotiation. Do not reinterpret an old compile request as a new arbitrary project/attachment protocol.
  6. Preserve current single-use plans and isolated Scheme sessions. Do not reuse closure state across retries; create a fresh invocation.
  7. Version new structured CLI report schemas while retaining existing fields where their meaning remains valid.

Output ownership and legacy paths

Existing single-file paths stay unchanged. Generated projects use distinct per-input roots inside the same task destination. Both pure execution APIs use shared output-path validation. Default source-derived naming strips only the final extension, with configuration available for a stable logical project root; duplicate or ambiguous roots are errors.

The local HTML is a review surface. Beads remains the canonical design/decision record. After design agreement, update beads and regenerate an implementation plan; the earlier five-task draft has not been imported and does not authorize an implementation scope.

17 / Verification and delivery

Prove the contracts and the actual generated project

ConcernFocused acceptance
Stage graphUnknown roles, bad connections, cycles, conflicting configuration, omitted provider, unsupported target, and source-only mode.
GenerationDeterministic content, injective symbols, access, type lowering, currying, conditional evaluation, SDK errors, unsupported constructs, and explicit migration.
Artifact ownershipTraversal, normalized/case collisions, ancestor overlaps, duplicate IDs, invalid project membership, nested source roots, and many-source provenance.
Build identityCompiler/core mismatch, unresolved SDK, wrong dependency digest, stale build products, manifest mutation, and a provider returning success for the wrong project.
PublicationFailed build preserves previous output; successful replacement removes stale files/receipts; source-only removes old receipt; later commit failure reports earlier commits.
LifecycleCancellation, deadlines, disposed leases, late worker replies, cleanup failure, and no acquisition in a build invocation.
Real CLITyped multi-module pricing library and historical v3 fixture generate through the actual CLI, build with pinned moonc/core against an explicitly supplied SDK, and report success in JSON and JSON Lines.
ModularityReplace the MoonBit provider with a test provider through the same registry/configuration. Generate with a memory host and no compiler. Unsupported embedded project builds fail explicitly.

Delivery sequence

  1. Settle the decisions below and store the agreed contracts in beads.
  2. Introduce multi-artifact/project contracts, shared path validation, and legacy adapters.
  3. Implement the portable generator and its audited initial coverage.
  4. Add configured build validation, dependency identities, workspace leases, and provider adapters.
  5. Connect CLI configuration, events, source-only mode, and publication gating.
  6. Run real generated-library acceptance and existing four-target, CLI/npm, lint, formatting, and package validation gates before any push.

The existing E1 minimum is a model generating MoonBit accepted by moon build. The proposed engine-integrated build path adds required failure/publication behavior. Completion is measured against the agreed supported scope, with remaining coverage clearly tracked. E2 and upstream CLI/extension completion remain separate.

Compilers, formatters, and focused tests determine language/mechanical correctness. Review concentrates on semantics, stage boundaries, dependency authority, concurrency, recovery, and what the evidence actually proves.

18 / Review agenda

Decisions for the next iteration

Each item has a proposed direction and the question it settles. These are design choices, not requests to approve implementation or a release.

D1

Default pipeline mode

Proposal: existing pipelines retain generation-only behavior. A configured MoonBit library-build preset requires compilation before publication; explicit source-only mode remains available.

Settle whether choosing the MoonBit backend alone selects generation or also selects a build preset. Avoid surprising compiler requirements for portable callers.

D2

Assembly scope for E1

Proposal: identity assembly for complete IR library documents. Add multi-source library assembly as a separate component/capability.

Settle whether multiple source files must form one library in the first delivery. This changes provenance, project roots, and reference validation.

D3

Graph surface and runner depth

Proposal: typed internal stage graph with shorthand presets. Design the explicit configuration now; implement only the stage combinations E1 validates. The host orchestrates pure generation, build, and publication without a general resumable VM initially.

Settle whether public arbitrary stage lists and a resumable engine are needed immediately or can follow the proven contracts.

D4

Source and compiled output

Proposal: publish source projects and verified receipts. Keep binary build products private in E1, with a byte-capable contract for later selection.

Settle whether reusable .mi/core or target binaries must be E1 publication outputs. That requires provider product manifests and binary transport acceptance.

D5

SDK source and distribution

Proposal: explicit offline source mapping with content identity for local acceptance; separately verify an exact SDK release for standalone consumption.

Settle the published dependency identity and provider enforcement. Module version alone does not prove source identity.

D6

First backend coverage

Proposal: a useful typed nongeneric library slice first, with audited binding support and explicit diagnostics. Follow with patterns, generics, and wider SDK coverage.

Settle the minimum representative model and which language constructs must be supported before E1 can close. Avoid making a small fixture imply universal code generation.

D7

Generated layout and public API

Proposal: one flattened MoonBit package with stable symbols and a manifest. Preserve access and keep record-shape helpers private unless public signatures require them.

Settle readability/ergonomics versus injective naming and module-cycle freedom. Private constructors and public opaque types need compiler-backed prototypes before final syntax is chosen.

D8

Embedded project-building claims

Proposal: acquired process provider establishes E1 project-build acceptance first. Embedded package compilation remains separately advertised until a project adapter resolves the full graph.

Settle whether browser project-build acceptance is required now. It needs additional dependency and asynchronous host orchestration work.

19 / Traceability

Evidence and authoritative sources

Repository links are relative to this local document. Beads IDs identify the shared Morphir tracker, not a local issue database.

  • morphir-ukvn: approved ecosystem roadmap. morphir-ukvn.5: reconciled Track 5 handoff. morphir-ukvn.5.2: E1 and its draft design.
  • Repository work tracking and local artifact guidance; agent configuration and pre-push requirements.
  • Domain glossary; ADR 0002: Scheme and engine separation; ADR 0003: hybrid value execution.
  • Current engine types; planning and pure execution; configuration resolver; engine contract and per-source behavior.
  • host runner and publication contract; filesystem replacement and recovery; host limits and guarantees.
  • existing provider boundary; process request implementation; acquired toolchain capabilities; embedded capabilities and current limitations.
  • current type vocabulary; value/body vocabulary; distributions and dependencies; 248-value SDK binding inventory.
  • CLI flags and structured output; current CI target and CLI gates.
  • MoonBit official documentation for errors and function effects and module configuration. Nightly documentation informs the design; pinned compiler evidence decides actual syntax support.

Revision history

Adds typed stages, generated-project contracts, build leases, dependency policy, publication guarantees, capability negotiation, and an explicit review agenda. Contents

Local review document.
Contract sketches are proposals.

Track 5 · Morphir to WASM · E1

Buildable libraries in a pluggable pipeline

A MoonBit backend that returns a complete library project. Ion carries pipeline data and annotations across persistence and transport boundaries. A configurable build stage validates the project through an explicit host provider. Publication happens only after the selected stages succeed.

Draft for iterationmorphir-ukvn.5.2Baseline 6cedfbeMoonBit implementation
Direction agreed; contracts still under design.

Damian selected a MoonBit generator and CLI integration and endorsed the modular stage boundaries. This revision develops the full design before implementation. Build-before-publication is the recommended configured path, with source-only generation also available. Amazon Ion is the agreed primary pipeline and intermediate-data format, with explicit opt-outs such as JSON or TOML. Ion binary is proposed for machine storage, and Ion text for readable documents. The precise contracts, encoding defaults, delivery scope, and remaining decision list are proposals.

Local HTML with locally bundled Mermaid rendering. No network requests or account connections. Diagrams render as SVG and include readable source descriptions. The interactive walkthrough illustrates proposed behavior; it does not run a compiler.

01 / Outcome

Make the library project a first-class output

The user-facing result is a generated MoonBit library with enough source, manifests, and dependency information to build through a chosen host. The engine coordinates typed stages and output ownership. Language-specific generation and compilation live in replaceable components.

E1 owns

  • A portable MoonBit generator using the current Morphir IR and SDK.
  • Multiple artifacts and generated-project metadata from a backend.
  • Ion-first serialization, annotation preservation, and byte-capable I/O at pipeline boundaries.
  • An explicit library build-validation stage and host adapter.
  • Source-only and generate-and-build pipeline configurations.
  • Real CLI, compiler, failure, and publication acceptance in this repository.

Separate completion evidence

  • E2 executes generated models across targets and compares evaluator results.
  • A7 owns the MoonBit source frontend and broader extension work.
  • The Rust CLI in finos/morphir needs its own integration and tests.
  • A released MEP/WIT component requires protocol, packaging, and release evidence.
  • Publishing SDK or compiler releases remains separate from local build validation.

Architecture requirements

  1. Frontends, assembly, transforms, backends, build providers, and publishers have distinct contracts.
  2. Pipeline configuration selects components and stages without embedding MoonBit rules in the engine.
  3. Pure stages can execute without filesystem, network, process, or compiler access.
  4. Host effects are explicit, capability checked, cancellable, and bounded.
  5. A failed generation, dependency resolution, or build does not replace previously published output.
  6. Unsupported IR, bindings, or host capabilities produce diagnostics, never placeholder output.
  7. Pipeline data defaults to Ion. Alternate formats require explicit selection and checked conversion; no boundary silently drops annotations or narrows values.

05 / Ownership

Put each decision in the component that owns it

Portable semantics

  • Enforce destination confinement.

  • Report actual committed destinations.

06 / Configurable execution

A typed stage graph, not an arbitrary shell workflow

The planner expands a preset or explicit stage list into a directed acyclic graph. Each node names a registered component, its scope, typed input connections, and immutable options. Edges carry named values; they do not refer to whatever files happen to exist in a directory.

RoleInput → outputScope and effect
FrontendSource snapshot → IR unitsSource or project scope, according to declared capability. Existing callbacks remain source-scoped.
AssemblyIR units → library unitsProject scope, pure. Identity assembly supports complete library documents.
TransformLibrary units → library unitsPackage scope, pure except explicitly supplied runtime capabilities. Existing Scheme adapters remain supported.
BackendLibrary units → generation batchPackage or project scope, pure. Language-specific manifests remain opaque to the engine.
Build validationGeneration batch → validated batch + receiptsGenerated-project scope, host effect through a selected provider.
PublicationAccepted batch → publication reportTask scope, host effect. Depends on every required stage for that task.

Planning rules

  • Reject cycles, duplicate node IDs, unknown components, incompatible ports, unsupported options, and outputs with no ownership rule.
  • Every required build must have a compatible provider. A generation-only plan needs no toolchain.
  • Track backend language separately from compiler target: moonbit is a backend; wasm is a build target.
  • Configuration can choose a direct generation-to-publication edge or insert build validation.
  • Publication receives one explicit output selection. A future fan-out must merge through a collision-checking stage before publication.
  • Serialized edges and checkpoints default to Ion; direct in-process edges carry typed values without needless encode/decode cycles. Validate each selected codec/profile against both port capabilities and host byte-I/O support.
  • Execution is sequential and deterministic initially. The graph permits future independent scheduling without making concurrency an E1 acceptance requirement.
Dry run resolves structure, not model semantics.

It shows sources, destinations, stage connections, provider requirements, and unresolved capability checks. It does not read source bodies, compile, acquire tools, or promise that a model is supported. Checks requiring generated manifests or IR semantics run during execution.

Runner and synchronous core

The engine owns graph validation and pure stage execution. The host runner drives the plan and awaits effect stages. A native synchronous runner can use the same stage order; a JavaScript runner awaits workers and I/O between pure calls. A provider-owned Promise is never hidden inside a synchronous MoonBit callback.

The first implementation can split the plan into a pure generation phase and a host build/publication phase. Preserve explicit graph identities and contracts now; a general resumable interpreter is a later implementation choice if additional mixed-effect stages justify it.

07 / Primary data format

Ion is the common data boundary

Settled requirement: Ion first, explicit format opt-outs.

The pipeline uses Amazon Ion for its data envelopes and intermediate files unless the caller explicitly selects another format. The remaining choices concern the Morphir profile, encoding defaults, and compatibility rules. Ion does not require serializing every in-process function call or changing the syntax of generated source.

Ion has a shared data model for text and binary representations, including annotations and types beyond JSON. That makes it suitable for retaining metadata and exact values while selecting binary storage. It does not itself add new types to Morphir IR or provide a type inference or optimizer implementation. Define morphir-pipeline-v1 for envelopes and an explicit IR profile mapping to current IR. The codec maps semantic enums and identities by the profile, with explicit symbol/string rules. A native Ion integer retains arbitrary magnitude; any IR literal whose original lexeme matters also retains that lexeme separately. Rich metadata uses Ion values directly, not the current JSON-shaped Data enum. A validated schema is a wire contract; generator checks still determine whether the decoded IR is supported.

Preserve annotations through changes to IR

Ion annotations are ordered symbol metadata attached to values. Morphir semantic annotations and inferred-type attributes are separately defined IR concepts; the profile states how each is represented. Decoding retains unknown annotations and rich extension values on stable node IDs. These values must survive assembly, migrations, transforms, checkpoints, and symbol/metadata emission when their nodes survive.

  1. A preserving stage returns its typed result plus node lineage: retained, derived, or removed identities. Retained nodes keep annotations and extension values.
  2. A rewrite declares how metadata moves to derived nodes. An optimizer interprets only registered annotation meanings; unknown annotations remain opaque.
  3. Removed nodes have recorded lineage. Metadata is not silently reassigned to an unrelated array position, nor is annotation order normalized away.
  4. A legacy transform can pass through unchanged nodes when preservation is demonstrable. If it changes annotated structure without a valid metadata mapping, fail with data.annotation_preservation_unsupported. Any requested destructive conversion is explicit and reports the affected paths.

The exact node-identity and rewrite rules need an agreed profile before structural optimization is enabled. This is part of the first serialization slice, not a promise that existing Scheme transforms already preserve Ion metadata.

Exact values and safe opt-outs

Preserve the Ion data model

Keep arbitrary integers, decimal coefficient/exponent and negative zero, timestamp precision/offset, typed nulls, symbol versus string, ordered annotations, lists versus s-expressions, blobs/clobs, and struct field multiplicity within configured limits. Unresolved symbols require a usable catalog or an explicit failure wherever semantic text identity is required.

Use self-contained local symbol tables by default; shared tables require declared catalog identities. Symbol-table numeric IDs are encoding details, never Morphir identities. Ion symbol handling.

Check JSON and TOML conversion

Plain JSON/TOML cannot represent all Ion values and annotations. A selected codec validates representability first and rejects loss by default. A versioned tagged lossless JSON profile can be an explicit alternative; an intentionally lossy report/export view must declare its projection and report what it omits.

Do not route internal Ion values through the package's generic JSON conversion: its JSON projection drops annotations and narrows several kinds, including duplicate struct fields. Inspected conversion implementation.

Ion strings are Unicode data. Morphir SDK text can contain UTF-16 code units requiring a profile-defined tagged byte representation when they are not valid Unicode scalars. Likewise, if a semantic contract needs exact floating NaN payload bits, encode those bits explicitly. Neither value may be silently replaced by a convenient text or numeric approximation.

Use moonrockz/ion through narrow adapters

The inspected 0.2.0 source at cc3bbc10e1565613e3bdd0bec8dd0a5c1175a3c9 provides immutable annotated values, synchronous text and binary readers/writers, Ion Hash, schema validation, and separate streaming packages. Start with its synchronous value/codecs behind the registry. Keep async streaming in optional host adapters; verify the needed packages on native, JS, WASM, and WASM-GC before claiming portable support. Pin the selected release/source and transitive dependencies in implementation. Inspected package documentation.

The package's decimal exponent uses a machine Int; acceptance must establish and bound that range. Ion arithmetic helpers do not replace Morphir SDK arithmetic semantics. Parse and validate budgets for nesting, digits/exponents, symbol tables, annotations, scalar lengths, bytes, and value counts before accepting untrusted data.

Identity and storage optimization

Build receipts hash the exact source/artifact bytes. A future semantic cache can additionally use Ion Hash with explicit algorithm/profile versions and the relevant IR, compiler, SDK, and stage-option identities. Annotations contribute to semantic identity; values with unresolved symbol text cannot be assumed hashable. Keep byte identity and semantic identity distinct. Ion Hash specification.

Binary Ion and symbol-table reuse offer storage choices; measure actual size, encode/decode cost, and memory with representative IR before making performance claims. Binary envelopes and checkpoints require byte-capable source reads, publication, and transport in E1. A missing byte capability is a planning/execution diagnostic, never permission to substitute JSON. Ion binary format.

Contract invariants

  1. A backend returns its entire batch or a failed result. Partial file lists never become successful projects.
  2. Every project member references exactly one artifact in the batch, beneath the project's declared root. Overlapping project roots are rejected initially.
  3. The engine assigns task-relative ownership. A backend cannot select an absolute host destination.
  4. Validate all paths and file/directory conflicts before accepting the batch. Reject traversal, drive paths, NUL, duplicate IDs, normalized collisions, and ancestor overlaps. Filesystem publication also detects case-insensitive collisions.
  5. The runner supplies the build policy. A backend describes compatibility requirements; it cannot silently request acquisition, execution, or network access.
  6. A build receipt is bound to the exact source and resolved dependency identities. It is invalid if those inputs change.
  7. Successful generation without a build has no successful build receipt. Reports identify generated, validated, and published separately.

Byte-capable I/O is an immediate requirement

E1 publishes native text source/manifests and binary Ion metadata/receipts. Source snapshots need Utf8Text | BinaryBytes, a declared codec/media type, and exact byte identity. Extend host reads and publication writes with explicit byte operations; never decode binary Ion as UTF-8. In-process adapters carry bytes directly; component/process transports use bounded attachments or a negotiated versioned encoding. Opaque native pointers are never portable references.

ProfiledData is a validated typed-contract projection with an Ion-preserving extension model. The current JSON-shaped Data is insufficient for richer metadata and cannot be the intermediate bridge. Serialize using the selected profile only at transport or storage boundaries.

The existing Artifact and Report APIs remain available through a text-only adapter. A new result version carries projects and receipts. Legacy callers receive an explicit incompatibility diagnostic if they request a result they cannot represent.

Why a file list alone is insufficient

A file list tells the publisher what to write, but not which files form a build unit, which compiler family is required, which dependencies were used, or whether the source has been validated. Project metadata and build receipts let the pipeline answer those questions without teaching the engine to interpret moon.mod.

09 / Source and library boundaries

Model assembly independently of emission

An Ion or explicitly selected JSON IR input may already contain several modules and their library dependencies. In that case, identity assembly passes the complete library to the backend. Several IR documents are not automatically fragments of one package.

E1 default: independent libraries

One complete library IR document yields one generated project. Preserve source-relative hierarchy, giving src/pricing.ir.10n the root pricing.ir.moonbit/ under the adapter's output naming rule. A backend-specific option can instead select an explicitly configured stable root; naming collisions still fail validation.

No cross-document linking is implied. References must resolve inside the library or through explicitly supported dependencies.

Optional future: assembled library

A registered assembly component combines compatible module units. It checks package identity, module uniqueness, dependencies, visibility, signatures, and duplicate definitions. It preserves canonical FQNames and many-source provenance.

This is a separate capability with its own acceptance. The pipeline includes the stage boundary now without claiming a linker has been implemented.

Assembly rules when enabled

  • Inputs must explicitly declare they are fragments of the same package or be mapped by a supported assembly contract. Configuration does not arbitrarily rewrite FQNames.
  • Duplicate modules or values are errors unless a separately designed merge operation explains how they combine.
  • External dependency specifications with incompatible identities or signatures are errors.
  • Private implementation details stay private. Project exposed_modules is applied at a documented point after assembly and before package transforms.
  • Reference checking and dependency resolution remain distinct. Finding a specification does not manufacture an implementation.
  • Top-level mutual recursion and module cycles remain semantic IR concerns; flattening the generated MoonBit package can avoid imposing new package cycles.
Scope proposal, not an approved reduction.

Ship identity assembly with E1's complete-library path first. If project-level multi-source assembly is required for E1 itself, give it a separate design slice and tests before source generation. The broader pipeline supports either choice.

10 / Backend internals

Generate typed MoonBit without changing Morphir semantics

Current IR library
  → index declarations and signatures
  → resolve references, access, aliases, and supported bindings
  → check required type information and backend capabilities
  → lower types, effects, currying, and record shapes
  → emit deterministic source and MoonBit manifests
  → return project description, symbols, and artifacts

Versioned input

The proposed ir-ion frontend decodes and validates the Ion IR profile, then uses explicit migrations to current v4 IR with metadata lineage. The existing ir-json frontend remains a selected compatibility path for historical JSON documents; it must not be used as an internal Ion-to-JSON bridge. The generator accepts current IR. A direct versioned API can reuse the same migration path and must preserve migration diagnostics. IR v4 support follows this repository's semantic model; it is not a claim of complete upstream YAML or document-tree protocol support.

Symbols and access

Use stable injective encodings of canonical FQNames for top-level symbols, plus separate prefixes for locals, fields, constructors, and generated temporaries. Preserve distinctions such as initialisms and word segments. Emit symbols.10n linking Morphir names to generated declarations, access, source-node lineage, and retained metadata. The compiler consumes generated source; the Ion symbol/metadata artifact retains annotations that have no MoonBit syntax equivalent. Strings in code, comments, filenames, and manifests use the correct escaping for their destination.

The initial layout is one MoonBit module containing one flattened package. That permits Morphir cross-module references without introducing MoonBit package cycles. Private values remain private. Public signatures depending on inaccessible types and constructor visibility require explicit validation; nominal enum syntax must not accidentally expose private constructors. Full line-level source maps are a later capability.
