09 / E2

Keep artifacts alive only while needed

Session states are acquired → prepared → built → running → completed → disposed, with failed/cancelled transitions into disposal from every effectful state. Reject invoking before build, use after disposal, reused lease IDs and replies for another artifact, target, suite or call.

Use fresh compiler output directories and private result paths. Hash compiled artifacts before invocation and verify identity after execution. Bound input bytes, result bytes, diagnostics, number/depth of values, per-call time, overall time and evaluator fuel. Deadlines include queue/build/run time where applicable.

Cancel child process trees and await termination before removing their workspace. Unix commands run in an owned process group; the supervisor confirms that no live group members remain. Windows executable commands start suspended, join a private Job Object with breakaway disabled, then resume. A Windows PowerShell 5.1 worker monitors cancellation, deadline and owner exit, terminates the job and waits for its active-process count to reach zero before writing a private completion receipt. Abrupt worker termination closes its non-inherited job handle and kills associated processes; the absent receipt still prevents a completion claim. The Windows worker inherits the host environment for its own runtime, while an explicit Unicode environment block carries the caller-selected variables into the model process. Private JSON requests and receipts are an explicit control-plane opt-out; model and telemetry payloads remain Ion. This supervision controls ordinary descendants and is not an OS sandbox. Aggregate cleanup errors with the original cause. A killed process, stale file or partial report never becomes a successful outcome.

No compilation, run or evaluator call occurs while holding the publication lock. Ordinary invocation returns outcomes without replacing E1 output. Verification with explicit publication commits the entire accepted task; failed attempt diagnostics remain available to the caller without replacing previously verified evidence.

12 / E2

Observe the pipeline without changing its result

Instrumentation is part of E2 from the first slice. It must answer which stage is slow, which target or provider failed, what a run produced, and whether execution resources were cleaned up. It also applies to the existing E1 generation/build/publication path. Keep a versioned observation contract portable across native, JS, Wasm and Wasm GC; the host selects sinks, clocks, sampling and exporters.

Three distinct outputs

Execution outcomes and verification receipts are required evidence. Progress events drive the CLI and embedding host. Telemetry consists of diagnostic logs, traces and metrics and can be filtered or dropped under an explicit bounded policy. Sampling telemetry never samples results, terminal statuses or receipts.

The current host already exposes Event variants for phases, diagnostics, generation, validation and publication through an optional callback. Adapt those typed events into observations and retain callback compatibility. Add structured start/end events at the owning stage; do not recover stage identity by parsing today's phase strings.

Portable contracts

ContractResponsibility
ObservationContextRun ID, trace/span/parent IDs, component scope and optional call/project/lease correlation. Pass explicitly across callbacks, processes and workers. Generate IDs with a host capability; do not derive them from model contents.
ObservationVersioned event name, signal kind, severity, stage, outcome/error code, bounded attributes, sequence number, optional wall time and monotonic duration. Ion-rich extension metadata is separate from portable scalar attributes.
ObserverA cheap enabled guard and non-blocking try_record returning accepted, filtered, dropped or unavailable. A no-op implementation is the default for library users. Avoid value formatting, clock reads and allocation when disabled.
TelemetrySessionHost-owned filter/redaction rules, bounded buffering, metric aggregation, sink health, deadline-bounded drain/flush and idempotent shutdown. No process-wide provider installation from library code.
TelemetrySinkExplicit supported signals, encodings, target/host requirements and sync/async drain behavior. Native OpenTelemetry, in-memory capture, Ion file, stderr and JSON Lines adapters implement this boundary.

Instrument pure generation/codec/comparison calls at their orchestration boundaries. The generator continues to return deterministic artifacts and diagnostics; it does not read a clock or write logs. Optional fine-grained semantic observations can be returned as data under a configured limit. Generated model bodies have no logging dependency by default; their driver and supervisor own invocation spans and mapped failures.

Trace structure and correlation

morphir.verify
  plan → snapshot → decode → transform → generate
  target[js | wasm-gc | native | llvm]
    dependencies → build → invoke[call] → cleanup
  evaluate[call] → compare[call,target]
  publish

Every started scope has one logical terminal transition: success, failure or cancellation. Close scopes in cleanup paths. Parent spans contain their children; evaluator work that runs alongside target work is a sibling, with links at comparison. Repeated attempts get a new attempt ID and span while retaining the run/call correlation.

Transport validated W3C-compatible trace context in the provider request envelope, separately from semantic invocation data. Keep trace IDs out of source, suite, build and semantic cache hashes. Reject malformed or oversize context; allowlist baggage rather than propagating arbitrary environment or user data. Each process measures its own duration with a monotonic clock. Wall-clock timestamps support correlation; they do not define duration across hosts.

Logging and Ion

Define morphir-observation-v1 for structured local telemetry. When file logging is enabled, default to a binary Ion stream of self-contained records with bounded rotation and retention; offer readable Ion text. Keep unknown annotations and exact rich values in an explicit extension field. Human stderr and JSON Lines are supported projections, chosen independently of the model format.

OTLP has its own attribute/log value model. Project a documented subset; encode out-of-range integers/decimals as tagged exact strings when explicitly allowed, and omit or reject unsupported rich metadata with a conversion count. Do not silently stringify an arbitrary Ion object or pretend that OTLP preserves Ion annotations. The full local Ion record can retain rich metadata without exporting it.

Default fields are stage, target, timing, counts, stable diagnostic code and correlation IDs. Model arguments, result values, source text, environment values, credentials and absolute local paths are excluded unless a host explicitly opts in. Apply redaction before records reach any queue or sink. Debug level alone does not enable sensitive payload capture.

Lifecycle and failure policy

Synchronous engine callbacks enqueue bounded immutable records and return. Async exporters drain at host-controlled boundaries or in a host-owned task; they never block a pure stage or hold the publication lock. Completed spans retain their original timestamps and context when drained. Reserve bounded capacity for completion summaries and account for every dropped record; traces may be incomplete under pressure and must not masquerade as complete receipts.

Capture/queue/export failures do not change a model outcome or invalidate an otherwise valid receipt. Report telemetry health and a bounded warning through a separate non-recursive path. A sink must not report its own failure through itself. Essential execution diagnostics remain in the required result path. If durable audit evidence is later required, give it an explicit required-artifact policy rather than relying on best-effort telemetry.

End the root execution span before draining telemetry. Flush with a separate bounded shutdown allowance after execution cleanup and publication. Measure flush health locally with exporter self-instrumentation suppressed; do not create new spans in the queue being drained. Cancellation ends work and still attempts bounded telemetry shutdown; a stuck exporter cannot keep the CLI alive indefinitely. Hosts own and reuse providers across runs when appropriate, and library disposal must not shut down another host's provider.

Current host implementation: TelemetrySession.flush_to_process sends an immutable native Ion batch to an explicitly supplied exporter command through the shipped Node worker. Its stdin transport is process-isolated and supervised. File preparation and exporter execution share a host-selected flush budget of at most five seconds, with an additional 500 ms worker termination allowance. Call it after execution and publication lock release. The default local file sink remains available. This is a host export boundary; it does not declare the native OpenTelemetry adapter or collector acceptance complete.

Evidence that can be checked later

An Ion execution receipt records the schema/profile version; original and normalized model identities; suite and call identities; generated library/export-manifest/driver identities; compiler, core and every dependency identity; executable digests; runtime versions/binary identities and platform; evaluator identity/profile; build mode; comparison policy; outcomes; limit settings and actual completion status.

Semantic reuse keys include every behavior-relevant identity. Timing, temporary paths and diagnostic ordering stay outside semantic hashes. This leaves room for Ion binary and symbol-table optimizations without making byte layout part of semantic equality.

16 / E2

Defaults and boundaries to keep explicit

D1

Use a separate public consumer driver

It proves exported access and keeps library generation reusable. The first ABI is an internal Ion file protocol; stable host-language library ABIs remain separate capabilities.

D2

Keep build, execution, comparison and publication distinct

Reuse E1 preparation/identity rules through a session. Build-only callers dispose immediately; execution callers retain the verified artifact until their calls finish.

D3

Use Scheme for the always-available live evaluator

Record shared SDK limitations and independently derived cases. Rust support needs a proven pin; do not silently make an unavailable external checkout a required default for ordinary users.

D4

Include LLVM explicitly

The roadmap names C and LLVM. Treat them as separate native backends. The pinned compiler reports “LLVM backend is disabled” even with a freshly built matching core. Select and verify a separate LLVM-capable compiler/core pin through explicit provider configuration, retaining the existing pin for the other lanes until compatibility is proven. Keep that toolchain identity in the receipt; any deferral of LLVM requires an explicit scope decision.

D5

Preserve rich values with Ion

Use typed in-process contracts, binary Ion intermediates and explicit JSON projection where required. Preserve exact numerics, annotations and UTF-16 semantics.

D6

Portable instrumentation, host-owned telemetry

Extend the existing event seam with typed observations, context and bounded lifecycle hooks. Prefer moonbit-community/opentelemetry for a native exporter adapter and moonrockz/ion for local records. Required outcomes and receipts bypass sampling and telemetry delivery. Package choice remains conditional on target-specific integration checks.

What E2 completion does not claim

Full generic IR/SDK coverage; stable C/JS/WIT library packaging; multi-document linking; embedded project resolution; browser parity; upstream Rust CLI extension integration; or a published release. Each needs its own acceptance evidence.

design:
# Morphir Ecosystem Model and Roadmap Status: approved design (Damian, 2026-09-26). Each capability below gets its own design and plan when its turn comes; this document is what those designs argue from. ## 1. Purpose **Intent.** Turn the Morphir plans into small capabilities that a user can see, that ship on their own, and that are not tied to one another more than they must be. Free finos/morphir-rust from being the one place every extension is built, so each language ecosystem can be served on its own. **Who it is for.** Extension authors first, then Morphir CLI users, then contributors to a language ecosystem. **Success looks like.** - A contributor can build, test and release the Python extension from finos/morphir-python without touching morphir-rust. The same holds for every language repo. - A new ecosystem repo starts from one common layout. - A PR that touches only docs, or only one extension, runs only its own CI jobs. - The roadmap is a list of capabilities, each with a user-visible result and no more than one or two dependencies. - Any capability can be taken by another engineer, agent or machine. ## 2. The repository model ### 2.1 Two halves Every ecosystem repository has two halves and follows one layout. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph repo["finos/morphir-"] native["Native half
IR support and Morphir SDK
in the language itself"] rust["Extension half
the language's MEP extension
(Rust today; a component in the language later)"] docs["Docs"] end rust -->|"cargo add"| crates["Published core crates
(from morphir-rust)"] rust -->|"release: bundle + release.json"| bundle["Extension release
(installable by the CLI)"] umbrella["finos/morphir
CLI, specs, MCK"] -->|"pins by checksum or submodule"| bundle ``` - **Native half.** The language's own reading and writing of Morphir IR, and its Morphir SDK (the standard library a generated model runs against). - **Extension half.** The language's MEP extension: frontend, backend, workspace discovery. Written in Rust today against the published core crates. Later it can be a component written in the language itself, where the language compiles to WASM (TypeScript through jco componentize, MoonBit natively). - **Docs.** The repo's own docs site or docs folder. - A repo can have an empty extension half. finos/morphir-moonbit today and finos/morphir-scala after its restructure are native-only repos in the same layout. ### 2.2 finos/morphir-rust is the special case In morphir-rust both halves are Rust. Its native half is the Rust IR (`morphir-core`), the Rust SDK, and the core crates every other repo's extension half depends on: `morphir-extension-sdk`, `morphir-host`, `morphir-host-native`, `morphir-workspace`, `morphir-common`, `morphir-projection`. Its extension half is `morphir-rust-binding`, `morphir-elm-binding` until it moves (A6), and the Morphir Scheme reference extension (D1). What follows: the core crates are published from morphir-rust, and it is the one repo where a core change fans out to its own extensions. Everywhere else a core change arrives as a crate version bump. ### 2.3 finos/morphir holds the extensions with no language home The umbrella keeps the CLI (`crates/morphir`), the specs (`spec/`), and the MCK. It gains the format extensions: Avro and OpenAPI (A5) and the WIT backend (B1). They are extensions like any other, with bundle releases, but they live next to the CLI because no language repo owns them. ### 2.4 Built into the CLI, or installed A language is **built into the CLI** when the umbrella pins its ecosystem repo as a submodule and `crates/morphir` lists it as a built-in, depending on the extension crate by path through that pin. Gleam keeps this route after it moves (A3): `morphir compile` handles Gleam with no install, and the only coupling is the pin. Every other language is **installed**: `morphir extension install ` fetches the bundle from the language repo's release. Which languages are built in is an umbrella decision, and each language repo has its own pipeline either way. A built-in language still ships a bundle, so older CLIs and non-Rust hosts can install it. A project whose `morphir.toml` names a language the CLI does not have gets a clear message with the install command. ### 2.5 Published core crates The core crates are published to crates.io on each morphir-rust release. Versions are `0.x.y`, with prereleases such as `0.5.0-beta.1` allowed. Cargo treats `x` as the breaking number of a `0.x.y` version, so a breaking change bumps `x` and an additive change bumps `y`. No crate reaches 1.0 before Morphir 1.0.0. Until the first publish, an extension repo may use a git dependency on morphir-rust pinned to a tag, as a stopgap. ### 2.6 Packaging is a CLI command, not a script to copy Today the bundle packaging is Python under morphir-rust `scripts/extension_packaging`, and it needs `morphir-host-native` in the same workspace. It becomes a command of the CLI (for example `morphir extension bundle`), so an ecosystem repo needs only the released CLI to package, verify claims, and publish. The release workflow in the common layout calls that command. ### 2.7 Change-scoped CI Each repo builds only what a change affects: the native half, the extension half, or docs, and, in a repo with more than one extension, only the extensions touched. A core crate change is the only change that fans out, and only inside morphir-rust. The umbrella's `changes` filter gets one path set per extension it holds. Every repo pins its filters with a test, as the umbrella's `tests/ci` does today. Measure: a docs-only PR or a single-extension PR runs only its own jobs. ### 2.8 Incremental delivery per extension An extension ships with the capabilities it has, and its claim set tells the host. Each extension's roadmap is a ladder, and a repo can release at any rung: 1. types-only frontend 2. values in the frontend 3. backend 4. workspace discovery (`morphir compile` with no `morphir.toml`) 5. incremental and multi-document compile No rung waits for another extension, and no capability in the map requires a whole ladder. ### 2.9 Parallel work Every capability in the map is an independent unit of work with its own bead. The dependencies in the map are the only ordering. A capability can be claimed (`bd update --claim`) by any engineer, agent or machine. ## 3. Extension direction: WIT first, components first - **Target hosts** are component-model hosts: the Rust CLI through wasmtime, and JavaScript runtimes through jco. Elixir through Gleam is possible later, not a focus now. - **Contracts are WIT.** The extension contracts are written as WIT interfaces and worlds (`morphir:mep`, `morphir:host`), with WAC where composition helps. WIT is the source of truth for worlds and functions. The Gleam model in `spec/mep` stays the source of truth for the message types, and the WIT type package is generated from it by the WIT backend (B1). Until B1 exists, a hand-written type package is checked against the model by a test. - **WASM extensions are components**, not Extism plugins. Extism is maintained, not extended, so existing installs keep working; it may be retired as component-model support matures. - **Process and native extensions stay fully supported.** They are not the focus of this push. - **The runtime is different from extensions.** The evaluator keeps a core WASM target for browsers and hosts without component-model support (D3), next to its component target (D2). ## 4. The map Five tracks. Tracks run side by side; arrows are the only dependencies. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph T1["Track 1: repos and pipelines"] A1a["A1a crate publish proof (0.0.1)"] --> A1b["A1b core crates on crates.io"] A1b --> A2["A2 layout, packaging command, scoped CI"] A2 --> A3["A3 Gleam to morphir-gleam (built in by pin)"] A2 --> A10["A10 TypeScript extension in morphir-typescript"] A2 --> A4["A4 Python to morphir-python"] A2 --> A5["A5 Avro, OpenAPI to finos/morphir"] A3 --> A6["A6 Elm-native to morphir-elm"] A3 --> A9["A9 Scala restructure, scala-elm retired"] A2 --> A7["A7 MoonBit extension"] A2 --> A8["A8 .NET extension (C#, F#)"] A2 --> A11["A11 JVM extension (Java, Kotlin)"] end subgraph T2["Track 2: WIT contract and components"] B1["B1 WIT backend, types only"] --> B2["B2 MEP contract as WIT"] B2 --> B3["B3 component extensions end to end"] B3 --> B4["B4 host as a component, JS wrapper"] B3 --> B5["B5 MCK and itest adapters as components"] end subgraph T3["Track 3: MEP model follow-ups"] C1["C1 Rust MEP types from the model"] C2["C2 MEP conformance suite"] C3["C3 guest SDK (morphir-opua.2)"] end subgraph T4["Track 4: evaluation"] D1["D1 Morphir Scheme reference extension"] --> D2["D2 runtime as a component"] D1 --> D3["D3 runtime as core WASM"] D2 --> D4["D4 language-native runtime hosts"] end subgraph T5["Track 5: Morphir to WASM"] E0["E0 spike: MoonBit route"] --> E1["E1 Morphir to MoonBit backend"] E1 --> E2["E2 wasm, native and JS targets"] end A1b -.-> B3 B2 -.-> C2 A7 -.-> E1 E1 -.-> D2 ``` ### Track 1: repos and pipelines | Id | Capability | Repo | Depends on | User result | Wave | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | A1a | Publish one leaf crate (`morphir-common`) at `0.0.1` through `release.yml` to prove the pipeline, trusted publishing and organization secrets | morphir-rust | none | The publish job works end to end | now | | A1b | Publish `morphir-core`, `morphir-extension-sdk`, `morphir-workspace`, `morphir-projection` at `0.x.y` in dependency order; metadata, dry run in CI, bump rule in docs | morphir-rust | A1a | `cargo add morphir-extension-sdk` works outside the workspace | now | | A2 | The common layout: a documented repo layout and template with two halves, mise tasks, release workflow, change-scoped CI with a filter test, and `morphir extension bundle` replacing the Python packaging scripts | finos/morphir, morphir-rust | A1b | A contributor starts a language repo and releases an extension from it | 1 | | A3 | Gleam extension moves to finos/morphir-gleam; umbrella pins the repo; Gleam stays built in; bundle released from morphir-gleam | morphir-gleam, finos/morphir | A2 | No change for users; Gleam contention leaves morphir-rust | 1 | | A10 | TypeScript extension in finos/morphir-typescript, first rung types-only | morphir-typescript | A2 | `morphir extension install morphir-typescript` | 1 | | A4 | Python extension moves to finos/morphir-python, installable | morphir-python | A2 | `morphir extension install morphir-python` fetches from its own repo | 1 | | A5 | Avro and OpenAPI extensions move to finos/morphir with scoped CI | finos/morphir | A2 | Same bundles, released from the umbrella | 1 | | A6 | Elm-native (`morphir-elm-binding`) moves to finos/morphir-elm as its Rust half, next to the TypeScript extension | morphir-elm | A3 | Two Elm providers, one repo | 2 | | A9 | morphir-scala restructure: drop build cruft, keep IR, SDK and langkit as the native half, decommission `morphir-scala-elm` (umbrella pin, `scala_elm` compatibility case, CLI tests, kb decision 0001 updated) | morphir-scala, finos/morphir | A3 | Two Elm frontends, not three | 2 | | A7 | MoonBit extension in finos/morphir-moonbit (frontend and backend; possibly a MoonBit-written component, no Rust) | morphir-moonbit | A2 | MoonBit models compile; the Morphir-to-MoonBit backend feeds Track 5 | later | | A8 | finos/morphir-dotnet joins `ecosystem/`, gets the layout, and builds one extension serving C# and F# (provider shape decided in its design) | morphir-dotnet | A2 | .NET models compile | later | | A11 | finos/morphir-jvm joins `ecosystem/` and builds a Java and Kotlin extension | morphir-jvm | A2 | JVM models compile | later | Wave 1 order: A3, then A10 and A4 close together, then A5. ### Track 2: WIT contract and components | Id | Capability | Repo | Depends on | User result | |---|---|---|---|---| | B1 | WIT backend extension, types only: `morphir generate --target wit` emits a WIT type package; rules for generics and recursive types settled here | finos/morphir | none | Any types-only Morphir model becomes a WIT package | | B2 | MEP contract as WIT: hand-written `morphir:mep` worlds, generated type package in `spec/mep/generated/wit/`, drift check | finos/morphir | B1 | Extension authors get a WIT contract | | B3 | Component extensions end to end: a component guest target in `morphir-extension-sdk`, `ComponentConnection` in `morphir-host` (wasmtime), one extension (Avro) shipped as a component and run by the CLI | morphir-rust, finos/morphir | B2, A1b | The first component extension installs and runs | | B4 | Host as a component (`morphir:host` worlds) with a JavaScript wrapper in morphir-typescript | morphir-rust, morphir-typescript | B3 | A JavaScript runtime drives Morphir extensions | | B5 | MCK and itest adapters as WIT components: one `morphir:mck/adapter` world, each implementation exports it, the kit runs any adapter in wasmtime or jco | finos/morphir, each repo | B3 | One conformance runner for every language | ### Track 3: MEP model follow-ups | Id | Capability | Existing bead | Depends on | |---|---|---|---| | C1 | Rust MEP protocol types generated from `spec/mep/generated/mep.ir.json` | `morphir-opua.1.2.2` | none | | C2 | MEP conformance suite in `spec/mep/mck` | `morphir-opua.1.2.7` | none; B2 extends it | | C3 | Guest SDK and shared discovery rules | `morphir-opua.2` | as recorded in that epic | The other Phase B, C and D beads under `morphir-opua.1` keep their places; B3 and B4 are the new homes of `morphir-opua.1.4.1` and `.1.4.2`. ### Track 4: evaluation | Id | Capability | Repo | Depends on | User result | |---|---|---|---|---| | D1 | Morphir Scheme dialect: a reference frontend and backend whose syntax mirrors IR, no external toolchain, published with the core crates; used by core tests and as the runtime's input language | morphir-rust | none | A readable form of IR that round-trips exactly | | D2 | The runtime (`morphir-runtime`) as a WASM component for the CLI and JavaScript hosts | morphir-rust | D1, shares B3 work | Evaluate a model from any component host | | D3 | The runtime as core WASM for browsers and hosts without component-model support | morphir-rust | D1 | Evaluate a model in a browser | | D4 | Language-native runtime hosts: the evaluator embedded through bindings in JVM, .NET, Python and others | each repo | D2 | Evaluate a model from the host language | Track 4 links to the evaluation epic `morphir-o6vm.9`. Ordering inside the track is decided in its own design. ### Track 5: Morphir to WASM | Id | Capability | Repo | Depends on | User result | |---|---|---|---|---| | E0 | Spike: compile two or three small models to MoonBit by hand or with a minimal generator, build with `moon build --target wasm-gc`, run in wasmtime, compare with `morphir-runtime`; measure SDK mapping, currying and closures, whether `moonc` runs as WASM, debuggability, build time. Output is a recommendation; everything built is thrown away | morphir-moonbit | none | Route decided | | E1 | Morphir-to-MoonBit backend (in the morphir-moonbit extension) | morphir-moonbit | E0, A7 | A model compiles to MoonBit | | E2 | wasm-gc, native (C, LLVM) and JavaScript targets through MoonBit's toolchain | morphir-moonbit | E1 | A model compiles to WASM, native or JS | Routes not chosen: route 0, direct emission with `wasm-encoder` (`morphir-wasm-binding`, kept as the Extism conformance guest); route 1, a Cranelift backend (the fallback if the spike fails). ## 5. Decisions | # | Decision | Date | |---|---|---| | 1 | Core crates are published to crates.io; git dependencies pinned to a tag are the stopgap | 2026-09-25 | | 2 | Crate versions are `0.x.y` with prereleases; no 1.0 before Morphir 1.0.0 | 2026-09-25 | | 3 | morphir-rust is core plus the Rust ecosystem repo, the special case of the model | 2026-09-25 | | 4 | Gleam stays built into the CLI through the umbrella's submodule pin; built in versus installed is an umbrella decision | 2026-09-25 | | 5 | Target hosts are component-model hosts; contracts are WIT; WASM extensions are components; Extism maintained, not extended; process and native fully supported | 2026-09-25 | | 6 | WIT is the source of truth for worlds and functions; the Gleam model for types; the WIT type package is generated by the WIT backend | 2026-09-25 | | 7 | Avro, OpenAPI and the WIT backend live in finos/morphir | 2026-09-25 | | 8 | Change-scoped CI is a rule of the model | 2026-09-25 | | 9 | Elm-native moves to morphir-elm in wave 2; the Morphir Scheme dialect is the reference extension in morphir-rust | 2026-09-25 | | 10 | Two Elm frontends: the TypeScript extension and Elm-native; `morphir-scala-elm` is decommissioned | 2026-09-25 | | 11 | Incremental delivery per extension, by claim set, is a rule of the model | 2026-09-26 | | 12 | The runtime targets components, core WASM and language-native hosts, as slices | 2026-09-26 | | 13 | Morphir to WASM goes through MoonBit as the main bet, proved by a spike; Cranelift is the fallback | 2026-09-26 | | 14 | A1 starts with a `0.0.1` publish of one leaf crate to prove the pipeline | 2026-09-26 | | 15 | MCK and itest adapters become WIT components (B5) | 2026-09-26 | ## 6. Not decided here Each of these belongs to its capability's own design: - The exact directory layout and template contents (A2). - The Morphir Scheme dialect's syntax, IR coverage and name (D1). - One provider or two for .NET (C#, F#) and for JVM (Java, Kotlin) (A8, A11). - The WIT rules for generics and recursive types, including the MEP `Json` type (B1). - The `morphir:mck/adapter` world (B5). - Whether `morphir-host` and `morphir-host-native` are published crates (A2). - Ordering inside Track 4. ## 7. How work proceeds - This spec is the design of the epic "Morphir ecosystem model and roadmap". Its five tracks are child epics, and each capability is a bead under its track. The existing epics `morphir-opua.1` (host library and MEP contract) and `morphir-opua.2` (guest SDK) are linked into Tracks 2 and 3, not moved. - Each capability gets its own design and plan, stored in beads (`bd-plan spec`, `bd-plan import`), and is executed from the rendered plan. - First three items, in parallel: A1a, B1, E0.

title: Deliver native V4 linked metadata independently
description: Deliver native V4 linked metadata independently of Morphir-in-Morphir dogfooding. Preview MVP is morphir-uqub.11 / #999: authored facts, query, export, focused MCK, docs and a qualified CLI prerelease. Trusted semantic validation is morphir-d7e8.2 / #1001 and can ship with the preview if ready, without gating it. Broader conformance and graph interoperability remain follow-ups.

title: Host library and MEP contract (finos/morphir#958)
description: The design is finos/morphir discussion 949, checkpoints 1-17. Tracking of this work now lives in beads, under this epic. The GitHub issues under finos/morphir#958 (phases #959-#962 and their sub-issues) stay open as mirrors and link back to their matching bead.
design:
# Morphir host library and MEP contract: design Status: design approved on 2026-09-23. This spec is waiting for review. Record: https://github.com/finos/morphir/discussions/949 (checkpoints 1 to 17). Beads: `morphir-opua` (extension SDK). This design is its host piece. Code blocks marked "sketch" show the shape of an idea. They are not the final API. ## 1. Goal Give every Morphir client one host library. The library finds the project, builds the MEP request, and talks to an extension guest. The same library serves the CLI, the desktop workbench, servers, and browsers. It also serves TypeScript and Python callers through the WASM component model. The MEP contract becomes a Morphir model. A Gleam module defines it. Morphir backends generate each binding and each language's types from it. Success looks like this: - `morphir compile`, `morphir generate`, and `morphir extension install` call `morphir-host`. The CLI no longer builds MEP requests or hardcodes `morphir-cli` as the peer name. - The web workbench uses the host pool. `crates/morphir/src/commands/ui/provider/sessions.rs` is gone. - `spec/mep/contract/mep.gleam` is the single source of the contract. CI fails when generated files drift. - A component guest and a process guest answer the same `Session::compile` call. - A TypeScript caller and a Python caller open a session through the host compiled to a component. They pass the same MEP conformance suite as the Rust host. ## 2. Terms - **Host library.** `morphir-host`. The in-process library that discovers a project, builds the guest request, and talks to the guest. - **CLI client.** The `morphir` command. It parses arguments, calls the host library, writes files, and prints diagnostics. - **Guest.** An extension that answers MEP calls: a native Rust guest, a process, or a WASM component. - **Session.** One live guest after the handshake. - **MEP.** The Morphir Extension Protocol, with its methods, capability statement, and version handshake. - **Binding.** One wire form of MEP: JSON-RPC, or a typed WIT world. ## 3. Scope In scope: - The host library in Rust (`morphir-host`) and its component form. - The MEP contract as a Gleam model, its bindings, and its versioning rule. - How the contract is published, downloaded, and checked. - The CLI, the workbench, and `morphir-daemon` as clients. - The TypeScript and Python host wrappers. Out of scope: - Moving the session host out of the CLI as its own project. - The public compile entry points in finos/morphir#897 (beads `morphir-t9cg`). This design gives those callers types they can use. - Moving the Elm package-name rule (kb `morphir-extensions` decision 0005) into the SDK. That is a later piece of `morphir-opua`. - The guest-authoring API. ## 4. Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph U["finos/morphir (umbrella)"] G["spec/mep/contract/mep.gleam"] -->|"morphir-gleam"| IR["MEP Library IR
(published model)"] K["spec/mep/mck
host and guest suites"] end IR -->|"backends"| B["Rust types, WIT morphir:mep, JSON Schema, TS, Python"] subgraph H["finos/morphir-rust: morphir-host"] CORE["sans-IO core: handshake, codec, version negotiation"] S["Session, one-shot helpers, Pool, Registry"] GC["GuestConnection: Native | JsonRpc over Channel | Component"] CORE --> S --> GC end B --> H CLI["morphir CLI"] --> S WB["web workbench"] --> S D["morphir-daemon"] --> S H -->|"morphir:host (async)"| TS["TypeScript wrapper (jco)"] H -->|"morphir:host-sync"| PY["Python wrapper (wasmtime-py)"] K -.->|"checks"| H K -.->|"checks"| TS K -.->|"checks"| PY ``` ### 4.1 The CLI and the host library (checkpoints 3 and 4) The host is a library linked into the `morphir` binary. There is no separate host program. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor User participant CLI as CLI client participant HL as Host library participant G as Elm guest User->>CLI: morphir compile src/Foo.elm --package-name My.Package CLI->>CLI: check compile cache CLI->>HL: compile(files, language = elm, package = My.Package, peer) HL->>HL: discover project, normalize name to my/package HL->>G: initialize, then compile request G-->>HL: IR and diagnostics HL-->>CLI: result CLI->>CLI: write IR to output path, update cache CLI-->>User: print diagnostics ``` The work splits like this: | Operation | CLI client owns | Host library owns | | --- | --- | --- | | compile | output paths, compile cache, configuration warnings | project discovery, request building, frontend guest call | | generate | finding IR on disk, output directory, writing files | backend selection, backend guest call | | probe (install) | copying files, updating the catalog | handshake, `describe`, session fallback, `check_statement` | - The client passes its peer name and version. The library never hardcodes `morphir-cli`. - Compile, generate, and probe advertise one list of supported MEP versions. - `ConnectedDaemonSession` stays a way to reach an extension over HTTP. The CLI does not use it to reach the host library. ### 4.2 Layers (checkpoint 5) ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph clients["Clients"] CLI["morphir compile / generate / install"] WB["web workbench"] SRV["server"] BR["browser (WASM + JS)"] end subgraph HL["morphir-host"] OS["One-shot helpers
compile, generate, probe"] POOL["Pool (optional)
reuse per key, evict a stopped guest, retry once"] S["Session
handshake, capabilities, compile, generate, describe"] OS --> S POOL --> S end CLI --> OS WB --> POOL SRV --> POOL SRV --> S BR --> S ``` 1. **Session.** `open(guest, peer)` starts the guest, negotiates the version, and stores the capabilities. The client owns the session's lifetime. 2. **One-shot helpers.** These open a session, make one call, and close it. `morphir compile`, `morphir generate`, and install use them. Probe opens a session, reads the capabilities, checks the statement, and closes the session. 3. **Pool.** An optional helper on top of sessions. It keeps one guest for each key, removes a guest that stopped, and retries a request once on a new guest. This is the logic of `sessions.rs` today. The library keeps no hidden global state. The client decides pool size, idle time, and tenant limits. ```rust // sketch impl Session { pub async fn open(guest: GuestSource, peer: PeerInfo) -> Result; pub fn capabilities(&self) -> &Capabilities; pub async fn compile(&mut self, request: CompileRequest) -> Result; pub async fn generate(&mut self, request: GenerateRequest) -> Result; pub async fn describe(&mut self) -> Result; pub async fn close(self) -> Result<()>; } pub async fn compile_once(guest: GuestSource, peer: PeerInfo, request: CompileRequest) -> Result; impl Pool { pub async fn compile(&self, key: K, request: CompileRequest) -> Result; pub async fn generate(&self, key: K, request: GenerateRequest) -> Result; pub async fn abandon(&self, key: &K); } ``` ### 4.3 Crates (checkpoint 6) ```mermaid flowchart TB CLI["morphir CLI"] --> HN D["morphir-daemon"] --> HN JS["browser JS"] --> HW HN["native transports
(crate or feature)
process stdio, Extism, wasmtime"] --> H HW["morphir-host-wasm
(later)"] --> H H["morphir-host
portable core, compiles for wasm32"] H --> SDK["morphir-extension-sdk
protocol types, check_statement"] H --> WS["morphir-workspace
discover_with_identity"] ``` - `morphir-host` has no tokio process code and compiles for `wasm32`. It does not depend on any language binding. - Process stdio and Extism transports move out of `morphir-daemon` into a native crate or a feature. - `morphir-daemon` becomes one more client of `morphir-host`. - The name `morphir-runtime` stays reserved, because elsewhere in the ecosystem "runtime" means the IR evaluator. ### 4.4 Transport (checkpoint 10) ```mermaid flowchart TB S["Session and Pool"] --> C{"GuestConnection
typed calls"} C --> N["NativeConnection
in-process Rust guest"] C --> JR["JsonRpcConnection
MEP codec, written once"] C --> CM["ComponentConnection
WIT exports"] JR --> CH{"Channel
messages"} CH --> ST["process stdio"] CH --> HT["HTTP"] CH --> WW["Web Worker postMessage"] CM --> WT["wasmtime (native)"] CM --> JCO["jco (browser)"] HS["HostServices
log, progress, read-file"] -.->|"guest calls back"| C ``` ```rust // sketch #[cfg_attr(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), async_trait)] #[cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", async_trait(?Send))] pub trait GuestConnection { async fn initialize(&mut self, params: InitializeParams) -> Result; async fn describe(&mut self) -> Result; async fn compile(&mut self, request: CompileRequest) -> Result; async fn generate(&mut self, request: GenerateRequest) -> Result; async fn close(&mut self) -> Result<()>; } #[cfg_attr(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), async_trait)] #[cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", async_trait(?Send))] pub trait Channel { async fn send(&mut self, message: JsonRpcMessage) -> Result<()>; async fn receive(&mut self) -> Result; } pub trait HostServices { fn log(&self, level: LogLevel, message: &str); fn read_file(&self, path: &str) -> Result; } ``` - `JsonRpcConnection` owns the MEP codec. It matches request ids, maps RPC errors such as `-32014` to Rust errors, uses must-ignore readers, and normalizes legacy request shapes. - A `Channel` moves messages only. It contains no MEP method names. - `ComponentConnection` calls WIT exports with typed records and builds no JSON. - Each client supplies `HostServices`. The JSON-RPC connection routes guest requests to it. The component connection wires it as the WIT `host` imports. - `MepTransport` requires `Send`. The new traits drop `Send` on `wasm32`. ### 4.5 Registry (checkpoint 14) `morphir-host` defines `Registry` and `GuestSource`. Each client registers its own guests. ```rust // sketch: CLI let mut registry = Registry::new(); registry.register(GuestSource::native(gleam_guest()))?; if elm_requested { registry.register(GuestSource::native(elm_guest()))?; } for snapshot in catalog.installed() { registry.register(GuestSource::from_installed(snapshot))?; } ``` The CLI keeps today's rules from `crates/morphir/src/extensions.rs`. A browser client registers only component guests. When a second client needs the same default set, a small composition crate takes over the list at that time. ### 4.6 Sans-IO core and the component worlds (checkpoints 16 and 17) The protocol logic lives in a sans-IO core. An async shell and a sync world both drive it. ```rust // sketch pub enum Event { Opened, Received(JsonRpcMessage), Call(Request), Closed } pub enum Action { Send(JsonRpcMessage), Complete(RequestId, Response), Fail(RequestId, Error), Close } impl SessionCore { pub fn handle(&mut self, event: Event) -> Vec; } ``` ```mermaid flowchart TB CORE["SessionCore (sans-IO)"] CORE --> ASYNC["async shell
world morphir:host"] CORE --> SYNC["sync world
morphir:host-sync"] ASYNC --> RS["native Rust (Wasmtime 46+)"] ASYNC --> JS["Node and browsers (jco, JSPI)"] SYNC --> PY["Python (wasmtime-py)"] ``` - `morphir:host` exports `Session`, `Pool`, the one-shot calls, and `Registry` as `async func`. It imports async `send` and `receive`. - `morphir:host-sync` exports the core's `handle` function. The embedder runs the event loop. - The embedder supplies `Channel` and `HostServices` as imports, because a Wasm component cannot start processes. - The TypeScript wrapper uses `morphir:host` through jco. It falls back to `morphir:host-sync` if jco P3 is not stable enough for a release. - The Python wrapper uses `morphir:host-sync` with an asyncio loop. It moves to `morphir:host` when wasmtime-py supports component model async. - The WIT does not use `error-context`. Support as of 2026-09-23: | Embedder | Component model async | | --- | --- | | Native Rust, Wasmtime 46 or later | Supported, on by default | | Rust guest, wit-bindgen 0.62 | Supported | | Node and browsers, jco 1.34 | Experimental, uses JSPI (Chrome 137, Firefox 153, Safari 27) | | Python, wasmtime-py 49 | Not supported (bytecodealliance/wasmtime#13705) | ```ts // sketch: TypeScript wrapper import { Session } from "@finos/morphir-host"; using session = await Session.open(processGuest("morphir-elm"), peer); const result = await session.compile(request); ``` ## 5. The MEP contract ### 5.1 One contract, two bindings (checkpoint 7) ```mermaid flowchart TB M["MEP contract
methods, capabilities, handshake"] M --> J["JSON-RPC binding
stdio or HTTP"] M --> W["WIT binding
morphir:mep world"] ``` ```wit // sketch package morphir:mep@0.1.0; interface frontend { use types.{compile-request, compile-result, diagnostic}; compile: func(request: compile-request) -> result>; } interface host { log: func(level: log-level, message: string); read-file: func(path: string) -> result; } world frontend-guest { import host; export lifecycle; // initialize, describe export frontend; } ``` The envelope style of `morphir:ext@0.1.0` is not the component binding of MEP. ### 5.2 Versioning (checkpoint 8) Before 1.0.0: - A breaking change bumps the minor version (`0.2.x` to `0.3.0`). - An additive, backward-compatible change bumps the patch version. `@since` marks new WIT items. - The JSON-RPC handshake sends the canonical version, for example `"0.2"`. The WIT package carries the full version, for example `morphir:mep@0.2.3`. - `SUPPORTED_MEP_VERSIONS` lists canonical versions. - Published contracts carry no prerelease tags. The component model never splits a prerelease version, so each draft would need an exact match. After 1.0.0, MEP uses standard SemVer. ### 5.3 Source of truth (checkpoint 9) ```mermaid flowchart LR G["mep.gleam"] -->|"morphir-gleam frontend
works now"| IR["Morphir IR"] IR -->|"new backend"| WIT["WIT world"] IR -->|"morphir-openapi json-schema
needs fixes"| JS["JSON Schema"] IR -->|"morphir-rust, works now"| RS["Rust types"] IR -->|"backend to choose"| TS["TypeScript types"] IR -->|"morphir-python, needs List, Maybe, generics"| PY["Python types"] ``` ```gleam // sketch: mep.gleam import gleam/option.{type Option} pub type Diagnostic { Diagnostic(severity: Severity, message: String, path: Option(String)) } pub type CompileRequest { CompileRequest(language_id: String, sources: List(Source), package: CompilePackage) } pub type Frontend { Frontend(compile: fn(CompileRequest) -> Result(CompileResult, List(Diagnostic))) } ``` - Contract records use labelled fields. - WIT has no recursive types. The WIT backend rejects them, or encodes them the way `morphir:ir` `encoded-ast` does. - The generated files are committed, and CI checks them for drift. The contract never depends on a guest that it defines. ### 5.4 IR payloads (checkpoint 13) ```gleam // sketch pub type IrLayout { Classic DocumentTree } pub type IrPayload { IrPayload(media_type: String, layout: IrLayout, data: BitArray) } ``` - Guest capabilities list the IR formats the guest accepts and produces. - The host sends the format on disk when the guest accepts it. Otherwise the host converts the IR one time. - JSON-RPC carries JSON IR inline, Ion text as a string, and Ion binary as base64. WIT carries `list`. - `CompileResult.ir` and `GenerateRequest.ir` change from `serde_json::Value` to `IrPayload`. - This depends on the Ion codec work in finos/morphir-rust#233 and finos/morphir#951. ## 6. Where the contract lives and how it travels ### 6.1 Folder (checkpoints 11 and 15) ```text spec/mep/ README.md what MEP is, the versioning rule contract/ Gleam project, the source of truth gleam.toml src/mep.gleam generated/ committed, CI drift check in the umbrella mep.ir.json json-schema/ wit/morphir-mep/ mck/ host and guest conformance suites ``` The root `wit/` folder splits by subject: - `morphir:extension`, `morphir:frontend`, `morphir:backend`, `morphir:component`, and `morphir:vfs` get a README that marks them superseded. They are deleted when the first generated `morphir:mep` WIT lands. Their incremental, streaming, and vfs ideas become candidate capabilities for `mep.gleam` first. - `morphir:ir` moves to `spec/ir/wit/`. The kb mirror in morphir-scala updates its mapping. ### 6.2 Publishing (checkpoint 12) ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph U["finos/morphir"] C["mep.gleam"] -->|"compile"| IR["Library IR"] IR -->|"pack + publish (to build)"| REG[("model registry")] K["spec/mep/mck"] -->|"mck kit, suite mep"| KIT["conformance kit"] end REG -->|"morphir package resolve / restore"| LR["language repo
restored IR"] LR -->|"morphir generate"| T["types and bindings, committed"] KIT -->|"mck kit vendor"| LR2["language repo
MEP conformance tests"] ``` - The contract is a Morphir Library package, for example `finos.org/morphir/mep@0.2.3` with IR package `morphir/mep`. - Consumers derive WIT, JSON Schema, and language types from the IR. - The conformance cases travel as an MCK suite named `mep`. - Until `publish` exists, each language repo commits a copy of the IR from an exact umbrella commit, with source and digest. When `publish` exists, that copy becomes `morphir package restore`. Package format requirements that MEP adds: 1. A package can be a zip archive. 2. A package can carry document-tree IR. 3. A package supports Amazon Ion text and Ion binary. The default between them is still open. ## 7. Error handling - A failed handshake or version mismatch fails `Session::open` with the guest's supported versions and the host's list. - RPC errors map to typed Rust errors in `JsonRpcConnection`. `-32014` (lifecycle refusal) keeps its meaning. - The pool evicts a session whose guest stopped, opens a new one, and retries the request one time. A second loss fails the request and clears the pool entry. A guest rejection fails the request and keeps the session. These are the rules in `sessions.rs` today. - A guest that does not accept the IR format on disk and cannot take a conversion fails with a capability error before the call. - Probe keeps today's provenance rules: `statementSource` probed or declared, and `probeSource` describe or session fallback. ## 8. Testing - **Sans-IO core.** Feed events in and compare the actions that come out. No runtime. - **Session and pool.** Use a fake `GuestConnection` with typed values. Port the five `sessions.rs` tests: shared session, reuse across compile and generate, evict and retry once, a retry that also loses its session fails and clears the entry, and a rejection keeps the session. - **Codec.** Use a fake `Channel` with golden JSON messages, including the legacy `documents` shape. - **Contract.** CI compiles `mep.gleam` and fails on drift in `spec/mep/generated/`. - **Conformance.** The `mep` MCK suite has host cases (a scripted guest, the messages the host must send, and how it must react) and guest cases. The Rust host, the TypeScript wrapper, and the Python wrapper all run the host suite. - **Released guests.** Before merging a CLI change, run the CLI tests and the real released providers (Elm 0.3.1, scala-elm M08), as for the capability-statements work. ## 9. Work breakdown Each item is a candidate issue. Items in the same group can run in parallel. **A. Host library in the CLI (first slice)** 1. Create the `morphir-host` crate with the sans-IO `SessionCore`: handshake, version negotiation, client-supplied peer. (finos/morphir-rust) 2. Add `GuestConnection`, `Channel`, `HostServices`, `JsonRpcConnection`, a process stdio channel, and a native connection. Add `Session` and the one-shot helpers. (finos/morphir-rust) 3. Add `Registry` and `GuestSource`. (finos/morphir-rust) 4. Move CLI compile, generate, and probe onto `morphir-host`. Remove `host_initialize_params`. (finos/morphir) 5. Add `Pool`, and move the web workbench off `sessions.rs`. (finos/morphir-rust, finos/morphir) 6. Make `morphir-daemon` a client of `morphir-host`, and move the process and Extism transports out of it. (finos/morphir-rust) **B. The MEP contract as a model** 7. Create `spec/mep/` with `README.md` and `contract/mep.gleam`, modelled on today's Rust protocol types. Add the drift check. (finos/morphir) 8. Generate the Rust protocol types from the IR with `morphir-rust`, and commit the IR copy in finos/morphir-rust. (finos/morphir-rust) 9. Fix the JSON Schema backend: single-constructor types as plain objects, and generic declarations. (finos/morphir-rust) 10. Add a Morphir to WIT backend. (finos/morphir-rust) 11. Close the Python backend gaps: `List`, `Maybe`, and generics. (finos/morphir-rust) 12. Add `BitArray` or an SDK `Bytes` type to the Gleam frontend. (finos/morphir-rust) 13. Add the `mep` MCK suite, with host cases and guest cases. (finos/morphir) 14. Split the root `wit/` folder and list the candidate capabilities. (finos/morphir) **C. Formats and packages** 15. Add `IrPayload` and IR format capabilities to MEP. Depends on the Ion codec. (finos/morphir, finos/morphir-rust) 16. Package format: zip archive, document-tree IR, and Ion. Link to the existing package work (`morphir-uhk3`). (finos/morphir) 17. Publish the MEP contract as a model package when `pack` and `publish` exist. (finos/morphir) **D. Component model and ports** 18. Add `ComponentConnection` over Wasmtime. (finos/morphir-rust) 19. Compile `morphir-host` to a component with the `morphir:host` and `morphir:host-sync` worlds. (finos/morphir-rust) 20. Add the TypeScript host wrapper with jco. (finos/morphir-typescript) 21. Add the Python host wrapper with wasmtime-py. (finos/morphir-python) ## 10. Risks and open items - jco P3 is experimental. The TypeScript wrapper may start on `morphir:host-sync`. - wasmtime-py has no async. Python stays on `morphir:host-sync` until it does. - No `pack` or `publish` command exists yet. The IR copy bridges the gap. - The Gleam frontend has no `BitArray` today. - The default Ion form, text or binary, is still open. - No TypeScript types backend exists in the new toolchain. Item 20 needs a choice of generator.

**Goal.** One extension SDK for guests and hosts across runtimes. This epic builds the portable host library (`morphir-host`, wasm32-clean, with `morphir-host-native` for processes, Extism and HTTP) and the MEP contract as a Morphir model, then ports the host to the component model with TypeScript and Python wrappers.

title: Design portable V3/V4 node addresses, index, and URIs
description: Define a typed semantic NodeAddress and version-aware node index for addressable V3 and V4 IR nodes. Specify a portable Morphir URI serialization independent of JSON, YAML, document-tree layout, and host. Support convenient unpinned URIs that resolve against a supplied current artifact with explicit stale or ambiguous target diagnostics, plus optional revision-pinned permalinks that resolve only against the identified immutable artifact revision. Browser URLs derive from the Morphir URI. Reconcile legacy V3 decorator NodeIDs and existing V4 document URIs/cursors without inheriting their gaps. Keep exact wire syntax in draft until reviewed; this task defines the shared address contract needed by V3/V4 sidecars and later native metadata.
design: Draft design in finos/morphir#957: typed semantic address and V3/V4 indexes; portable URI independent of serialization; unpinned current-artifact resolution with explicit stale/ambiguous outcomes; optional exact immutable revision pin; derived browser links. Pending review of artifact/revision namespace, guarded positional steps, URI grammar, and legacy key translation before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed artifact scope, root node kind/name, typed child path, IR version and optional revision model; URI parse/render and resolver contract; fixed V3/V4 positive and negative fixtures for nested nodes, JSON/YAML/tree layouts, escaping, stale and ambiguous targets, revision/version mismatch and sidecar key compatibility; index proves target existence and uniqueness with no silent retargeting; browser-link derivation specified; V4 native metadata migration boundary remains open.
notes:
Expanded finos/morphir#957 with a V4 type/field excerpt, typed NodeAddress and candidate URI snippets, V3 NodeID translation, node-kind and serialization-layout tables, and current-versus-pinned resolution cases. URI spelling and digest/guard algorithms remain draft pending design review.
finos/morphir#957 now shows proposed same-file versioned V3 and V4 sidecar JSON, seven V3 NodeID-to-semantic-URI cases, and an explicit shape-aware migration algorithm. Historical fixture /type and /value spellings are handled as tested compatibility inputs; all-or-nothing migration, collisions and invalid targets are covered. Draft envelope and URI grammar await review.
Draft spec and 49 reference-only cases are in finos/morphir#973 (branch feat/ir-node-addresses-957). Independent review corrected the canonical V4 Public wrapper and V3 TypeID custom-type exception. Issue #957 now links the PR. Open before closing: exhaustive V3/V4 child-role grammar and cases, custom constructor argument mapping, canonical guard/revision digest vectors, and executable adapter/index roundtrips. PR remains draft; no MCK compatibility claim.
Decision 2026-09-24: unpinned indexed URIs use a semantic node fingerprint of each ordered-step role, index, and selected child, not a whole-artifact revision guard. Unrelated artifact edits and later sibling appends retain the link; changed selected children or shifted indexed lineage become stale when distinguishable. Recorded in #957 and draft PR #973 with three new reference cases (52 total). Canonical cross-format digest encoding and vectors remain open.

title: Add golden file and span assertions to morphir itest
description: Extend the existing real-CLI scenario driver with golden-style assertions for complete file contents and selected spans. Support both notebook and Markdown authoring, fixed expected fixtures or inline expected text, useful mismatch diagnostics, and existing Rego/native evaluator architecture. Decide span selection and authoring contract before implementation, then drive it with failing integration scenarios and regression checks.
design: Proposed first increment: first-class golden assertions shared by Markdown and notebooks, with authored expected text kept on disk or supplied inline. Exact UTF-8 whole-file comparison by default; optional explicit line-range or marker-delimited selection, pending user preference. Preserve whitespace and final-newline significance; any line-ending normalization must be explicit. Load expected content before CLI commands and capture actual output immediately after its referenced command. Missing files, invalid/out-of-range spans and missing/ambiguous markers fail. Render unified diffs with source path/selected range; keep artifacts under --keep-temp. Preserve the existing real-CLI and morphir eval provider boundary, lowering golden equality into the same evaluator request rather than introducing a second external runner. Alternatives considered: raw Rego comparisons are already possible but require boilerplate and lack focused diagnostics; separate snapshot runner duplicates the scenario pipeline. No automatic blessing/update mode in the first increment. Add red/green CLI regressions for both formats, adopted golden example, developer/KB/skill documentation. Authoring syntax and span-selection scope are awaiting design review; no implementation edits yet.
acceptance_criteria: Both scenario formats can compare full generated files and selected spans against authored expectations. Mismatches fail with readable diffs; missing files, invalid selectors and ambiguous marker matches cannot pass. Expected content is independent of generated output. Existing assertions remain compatible. Documentation, example coverage and local skill explain authoring and diagnostics.

title: Design ecosystem-wide Morphir package distribution
description: Synthesize the package research and designs in finos/morphir and morphir-scala, compare relevant ecosystem package systems, and define a coherent package format, identity, dependency resolution, repository, transport, trust, workspace, and CLI design for Morphir model packages. This design prepares the vertical slice tracked by morphir-uhk3.
acceptance_criteria: The reviewed design defines canonical domain terms and invariants; reconciles existing umbrella and Scala proposals; evaluates 2-3 architectural approaches; specifies package identity, immutable content, manifests, dependency constraints and locks, source descriptors, repository/index behavior, trust and integrity, offline and workspace flows, CLI operations, interoperability, migrations, errors, testing, and staged delivery; records unresolved choices explicitly; and stays local under .dev until approved for publication.
notes:
Context mapped. User decisions: (1) model packages, executable extensions, and installable tools remain distinct artifact domains, with semantic reuse only; (2) published model packages are IR-first, with canonical versioned Morphir IR and optional source/provenance. Root CONTEXT.md now distinguishes Morphir package from immutable package release. Identity research: the earlier PURL-vs-PackagePath question was premature. JSR/Deno separates scoped package release from exported entrypoint; Gleam separates package dependency from imported module and supports registry/path/pinned-Git sources; Go uses authority-bearing module paths, package subpaths, one version per module path, /vN identity for incompatible majors, and replace for source redirection; Cargo fully qualifies packages by source+name+version and lets code use aliases/crate/module names, allowing multiple versions and sources. PURL standardizes cross-ecosystem package coordinates and physical subpaths but does not define name ownership, dependency solving, public exports, source substitution, or version coexistence. PackagePath+SemVer is sufficient for a release only after package-path ownership is defined; the system still needs PackageRequirement, ModuleReference, SourceDescriptor, digest/provenance, and coexistence rules. Teaching reference written locally at .dev/.sdlc/morphir-package-identity/. Next decision: global, authority-bearing, or repository-qualified package-name ownership.
Distribution history added from finos/morphir discussions. #55 says Distribution was introduced above Package to carry the package name, was expected to encompass multiple versioned packages, and deliberately deferred version semantics to package management. #146 frames publishing/versioning/reuse of Morphir IR as package-manager user stories. #160 distinguishes unresolved Library references from loading/linking the transitive implementation closure and raises version-conflict handling. #211 proposes Bundle as a fat IR; its discussion reframes that as Library versus bottom-of-graph Application and explicitly raises multiple-version support. #218 supersedes Bundle with standalone Application plus entry points, full dependency definitions, SDK inclusion/tree shaking, and equivalence/compatibility. #203/#214/#289 distinguish the semantic distribution from its single-file or granular document-tree serialization and treat a distribution as a virtual tree with one or many files. Proposed reconciliation: package release is repository identity/lifecycle; Distribution is typed IR content (Library/Specs/Application); encoding/layout is storage representation; package bundle/archive is the transport envelope. A reusable release requires a normative Library distribution; Specs is a projection; Application is a linked build/deployment artifact. Manifest requirements and lock entries remain distinct from dependency specs/definitions embedded in IR, with consistency validation between them.
Approved distribution boundary after reviewing finos/morphir discussions #55, #88, #146, #160, #203, #211, #214, #218, and #289. A reusable Morphir package release has one normative Library distribution; Specs is a projection sharing the release identity; Application is a versioned linked standalone IR artifact that may be stored/distributed but is not a dependency. Distribution is semantic IR independent of single-file/document-tree encoding. Package bundle is the physical transport envelope. Manifest requirements, lock entries, and embedded distribution dependency snapshots are distinct but must agree. CONTEXT.md updated with these terms.
Approved package identity: canonical PackageReleaseId = authority-bearing PackagePath + exact SemVer. The authority prefix establishes namespace ownership; registry, mirror, workspace, Git, and vendored locations remain SourceDescriptors and do not alter identity. Local dependency/import aliases are non-canonical. PURL may be an external representation after Morphir type registration, not the domain identity model itself. CONTEXT.md updated with Package path and Package release ID.
Version-coexistence research: MoonBit main at 94521dbd (2026-09-04) avoids Go /vN paths. Its MVS groups one module name into compatibility sets: all versions below 2.0 form one set, and each major >=2 is a separate set. It selects one version per set and retains multiple incompatible versions of the same module simultaneously. The resolved graph identifies nodes by ModuleSource (name+version+source), gives each a ModuleId, and binds each dependent edge to an exact node. PackageFQN internally contains ModuleSource/version although display/import syntax omits it; imports support local aliases. This is strong precedent for contextual, edge-scoped resolution. For Morphir, source should remain outside canonical identity per the approved model, so graph nodes would use PackageReleaseId (PackagePath+SemVer), with SourceDescriptor/digest in the lock. Supporting this requires Application distributions and downstream traversal to key definitions/references by release instance or graph context; current PackagePath-keyed dependency maps are insufficient. MoonBit currently has no dependency graph lockfile; .moon-lock is an operation mutex, so Morphir should not copy that omission.
Approved coexistence model: no Go-style major version suffixes. Keep PackagePath stable across majors; unify compatible requirements where possible; allow incompatible PackageReleaseIds for the same path to coexist as exact nodes in the resolved graph; require distinct dependency slots/aliases when one package directly uses multiple versions. Published Library IR resolves references through its owning release dependency slots; the lock binds slots to exact ReleaseIds; Application distributions carry the exact graph and implementations. This requires evolving current PackagePath-keyed distribution dependency structures. CONTEXT.md updated with Dependency slot and Resolved dependency edge.
Approved requirement and selection semantics: PackageRequirement uses an explicit SemVer constraint; prereleases require explicit admission. Normal builds consume the exact complete PackageLock. Initial resolution and intentional update prefer the highest stable version satisfying applicable constraints, unifying overlapping requirements where possible and retaining separate release nodes for disjoint constraints. CONTEXT.md updated with revised Package requirement and Package lock.
Approved module exposure model: convention-generated export paths by default, derived canonically from public Morphir ModulePaths rather than physical filesystem layout. Packages may exclude convention exports and add aliases, or select explicit mode for a curated surface. Publication validates and expands configuration into a complete immutable PackageExportTable carried by the release and Library/Specs metadata; consumers never regenerate it. Direct filesystem/module conventions are not repository identity. CONTEXT.md updated with Package export path/table.
Approved physical packaging model: define one canonical logical PackageBundle containing manifest, exact build lock, normative Library distribution, optional Specs/source/provenance/SBOM/attestations, and integrity metadata. Permit directory, deterministic archive, OCI, and repository-specific transport encodings. PackageContentDigest hashes a canonical sorted content manifest/file digests and stays stable across repacking; TransportDigest verifies a particular archive/blob. No transport technology becomes package semantics. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved repository architecture: RegistryIndex metadata is separate from package content and supports list-versions/read-release/source-descriptor capabilities. Resolver works through that capability rather than storage-specific APIs. Initial reference backends are local directory plus static Git/HTTPS per-package histories; OCI and hosted APIs are adapters over the same model. Content acquisition verifies package and transport digests. PackageCatalog search is separate and non-authoritative. CONTEXT.md updated with Registry index, Package registry, and Package catalog.
Approved authority/trust discovery: authority-bearing prefix may expose a well-known HTTPS metadata document; signed versioned delegations bind namespace prefixes to registry indexes and publication keys. Explicit configuration can pin authority metadata and redirect to approved mirrors. Mirrors may serve identical metadata/content but cannot create valid releases. Locks retain delegation digest, index snapshot, content digest, and exact source for offline reproduction. CONTEXT.md updated with Package authority, Authority delegation, and Package mirror.
Approved release lifecycle: PackagePath+version is permanently bound to one PackageContentDigest; republishing different content is rejected. Mutable signed status is separate: yank excludes from new range resolution while locks/exact requirements may remain eligible; revocation can warn or block even locked use under policy; tombstone durably records exceptional unavailability and prevents identity reuse. Mutable channels point to immutable releases. CONTEXT.md updated with lifecycle terms.
Approved development overrides: path/workspace/modified-vendor/pinned-Git inputs compile into explicit immutable IR-first UnpublishedPackageSnapshots with declared PackagePath, source/tree revision, compiler provenance, and content digest. They do not claim a published PackageReleaseId. Overrides are root-only policy and never propagate. Branch selectors resolve to commits in locks. Byte-identical vendored published bundles remain published releases with alternate SourceDescriptors. Applications may link snapshots with provenance; publishing a reusable Library release requires all dependency edges to resolve to published releases. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved document boundary: existing morphir.toml/morphir.yaml configuration remains the sole human-authored package intent and may include non-publishable workspace/task/toolchain/source/credential settings; morphir.lock is resolver-generated complete exact graph; publication emits a normalized immutable machine-facing PackageReleaseManifest containing only portable identity, requirements, expanded exports, content references, compatibility, and integrity metadata. Package consumers never evaluate authoring configuration. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved publication-time SemVer enforcement for stable releases. Patch/minor publication must pass structural backward-compatibility analysis over normalized export tables and Specs distributions; major releases may break. Implementation-only changes may be patch releases. Publisher emits a machine-readable PackageCompatibilityReport stored by the registry with comparison provenance. Behavioral equivalence is not generally provable and remains attested/additional analysis. Indeterminate structural results fail by default or require an authority-approved exception. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved name and release refinement: use ContractRelease rather than InterfaceRelease. LibraryRelease has normative Library distribution plus derived Specs; ContractRelease has normative Specs and no Morphir implementation claim. Runtime/extension providers bind to exact Contract PackageReleaseId and Specs digest. This is operationally analogous to .NET contract/reference assemblies and semantically analogous to ML module signatures, while avoiding overloaded signature/reference/interface terminology. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved application/binding boundary: ApplicationDistribution is portable and contains the exact model graph, Library implementations, ContractRelease requirements, and entry points. Target-specific ApplicationBinding separately maps every required ContractReleaseId+SpecsDigest to a compatible executable provider/artifact digest. Execution requires a complete binding; analysis/codegen may consume the portable Application. Changing platform bindings does not change model identity, and provider artifacts remain outside the model package graph. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved trust policy: public/private registry publication requires a PackageReleaseStatement signed by a key authorized through the PackageAuthority delegation chain, covering exact ReleaseId, normalized manifest, and PackageContentDigest. RegistryStatusStatements separately sign snapshots and yank/revoke/tombstone state. Optional build/SBOM provenance attestations are evidence, not publication authority. Transport TLS/digests do not substitute for release signatures; mirrors need no publishing keys. Unsigned snapshots are permitted only by explicit local-development policy and are marked in locks. Reuse standard TUF-style delegation and DSSE/in-toto-style statement machinery where semantics fit, with domain-specific manifests. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved CLI boundary: model packages use morphir package lifecycle commands distinct from morphir extension and morphir tool. Shared internals are limited to acquisition/cache/verification/trust semantics. Package workflow covers add/remove, explicit resolve/update, sync, tree/why, build snapshot, check, pack, verify, publish, vendor, inspect, yank, revoke. Ordinary builds validate and consume an existing lock, fetch missing content, and never silently re-resolve; missing/invalid locks require explicit resolution. Higher-level build orchestration delegates to this lifecycle.
Approved migration model: package-layer format evolves independently from Morphir IR format. New bundles may carry supported legacy Library IR with explicit payload format metadata. Legacy versionless distributions become UnpublishedPackageSnapshots; non-authority names remain migration metadata until explicitly mapped; localDependencies become workspace overrides; generated slots/exports adapt what is representable. No authority/version is invented and legacy IR is not silently rewritten. Graph-aware features such as multiversion Application linking, Contract releases, and binding metadata declare capabilities and produce clear errors in unsupported consumers. A package migrate workflow emits config plus a migration/capability report. CONTEXT.md updated with Legacy package adapter.
Approved PURL role: native PackageReleaseId remains normative domain identity. A future registered morphir PURL type is the reversible standardized external representation of an exact release for SBOM/provenance/catalog/vulnerability/generic repository interop. PURL does not represent ranges, dependency slots, exports, graph edges, sources, or unpublished snapshots; subpath is physical content and must not encode logical exports. Package manager v1 does not block on registration; define/test proposed mapping now, register upstream after a working format/registry, emit as standardized metadata only after registration. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved diagnostics contract: define a stable versioned PackageDiagnostic ADT/schema with code, severity, operation, subject, dependency path, structured details, causal diagnostics, and guidance. Share codes/payloads across CLI JSON, WIT, daemon APIs, and language libraries while allowing local human renderers. Cover identity/authority, solving, lock state, legacy capability, exports/slots, contract bindings, acquisition/offline, digests/signatures, immutable collision, compatibility, and archive safety. Integrity/authority errors fail closed; authorized mirrors may be retried for availability but never trigger silent trust fallback or re-resolution. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved normative PackageConformanceCorpus alongside schemas/specification. Language-neutral cases define inputs, normalized values, serialized outputs, digests, diagnostics, and capability requirements for identity/SemVer/PURL, exports, manifests/content hashes, solver/locks, contracts/bindings, compatibility, trust/signing, mirrors/offline/corruption, archive attacks/case collisions, and legacy adaptation. All implementations run the same corpus; no implementation is normative. Property/fuzz/performance tests remain supplemental. CONTEXT.md updated.
Approved staged delivery: Stage 0 specification foundation; Stage 1 local Library steel thread; Stage 2 signed distributed registry; Stage 3 graph-aware packages, contracts, applications, and bindings; Stage 4 ecosystem adoption and interoperability. Consolidated design published for ecosystem review as finos/morphir#800, labeled enhancement/spec/draft. The issue preserves all 16 open Stage 0 decisions.

title: Decide the v4 value node member vocabulary and where attributes may appear
description: Schema, Rust encoder (serde_v4.rs), morphir-ui decoder and the spec examples use four overlapping vocabularies: attrs vs attributes; thenBranch/elseBranch vs then/else; arg/result vs argumentType/returnType; subject/fieldName vs target/name; valueName/valueDefinition/inValue vs name/definition/in; Constructor and Tuple expanded forms with attributes that the schema forbids. Only LiteralValue and LiteralPattern accept attributes today. Choose one table of member names and one rule for attributes, and add Hole, Native and External to the Value oneOf in the same change.

title: Rust v4 type decoder reads a bare array as a parameterized Reference instead of a Tuple
description: ecosystem/morphir-rust/crates/morphir-core/src/ir/v4/serde_tagged.rs visit_seq: when the first element contains : and # it returns Type::Reference with the remaining elements as type arguments. There is no branch that decodes a bare array as Tuple. The schema (TupleType, ReferenceType), document-tree-files.md and closed bead morphir-j442 all say a bare array is a Tuple and a parameterized reference always carries the Reference wrapper. So ["morphir/SDK:basics#int", "morphir/SDK:string#string"] means (Int, String) per spec and List-of-String-applied-to-Int in Rust.
acceptance_criteria: visit_seq decodes a bare array of types as Tuple; {"Reference": [fq, args...]} and {"Reference": {fqname, args}} decode as Reference; a bare array whose first element is an FQName is a Tuple whose first element is a no-arg reference; regression tests cover all three; migrate_acceptance still passes.
