title: Make YAML the primary migrate output format
description: Specify and implement YAML as a native persisted serialization of the concrete Morphir IR, with v4 as the primary target and v3 compatibility where the concrete model permits it. YAML is an equal IR storage format, not a frontend language, generated projection, or documentation view. The migrate command should default v3-to-v4 output to YAML, infer single-file encoding from the destination extension, support document-tree output, and convert stored IR bidirectionally between JSON and YAML. Update v4 so JSON Schema is clearly a bootstrap definition mechanism rather than a restriction of IR storage to JSON.
acceptance_criteria:
EARS acceptance requirements:
AC-01 ubiquitous: The IR codec system shall provide an explicit YAML representation for every valid concrete v3 and v4 IR node.
AC-02 event-driven: When the YAML decoder reads an explicit or preferred readable form, it shall normalize that form into exactly one versioned semantic IR value.
AC-03 event-driven: When the YAML encoder writes an IR value, it shall emit the specified deterministic readable form where one exists and the explicit structural form otherwise.
AC-04 event-driven: When JSON is converted to YAML to JSON without a version transform, the result shall be semantically equal to the original IR.
AC-05 event-driven: When YAML is converted to JSON to YAML without a version transform, the result shall be semantically equal to the original IR.
AC-06 ubiquitous: The codec system shall retain JSON input and output support for every previously supported IR version.
AC-07 unwanted: If YAML contains ambiguous shorthand, duplicate keys, unsupported tags, unsafe aliases, lossy numbers, or invalid coercions, then the decoder shall reject it with a located diagnostic.
AC-08 event-driven: When v3 is migrated to v4 without a selected format or recognized output extension, the command shall emit canonical YAML.
AC-09 event-driven: When resolving single-file output, the command shall apply explicit output format, recognized extension, then YAML default.
AC-10 unwanted: If output format conflicts with a recognized extension, then the command shall diagnose the conflict and shall not publish.
AC-11 event-driven: When resolving single-file input, the command shall apply explicit input format, recognized extension, then bounded JSON-first detection.
AC-12 event-driven: When --json is used without an output path, the command shall write migrated JSON IR to stdout.
AC-13 event-driven: When --json is used with an output path, the command shall write the artifact and emit JSON status and diagnostics to stdout.
AC-14 event-driven: When writing a YAML document tree, the command shall use manifest.yaml, module.yaml, *.type.yaml, and *.value.yaml.
AC-15 ubiquitous: A generated document tree shall use one serialization profile.
AC-16 unwanted: If discovery finds multiple supported manifests, then the reader shall diagnose ambiguity and shall not choose implicitly.
AC-17 event-driven: When a single file is converted to a document tree and back without version change, the result shall be semantically equal.
AC-18 event-driven: When a JSON document tree is converted to YAML and back, the result shall be semantically equal.
AC-19 ubiquitous: Each transform shall declare event, definition, module, or distribution retention.
AC-20 state-driven: While all transforms are event-local, definition-local, or module-local, the pipeline shall retain no more than the largest declared scope plus bounded codec buffers.
AC-21 unwanted: If a transform needs a whole distribution, then the pipeline shall report that requirement before processing.
AC-22 event-driven: When LCR v3 is migrated to v4 YAML as a file or tree, the pipeline shall use its streaming path without retaining the complete distribution.
AC-23 ubiquitous: The pipeline shall carry semantic IR events rather than JSON or YAML value trees.
AC-24 ubiquitous: Public codec options shall keep IR version, layout, format, vocabulary, normalization, and publication independent.
AC-25 event-driven: When a new codec is registered, existing migration transforms and codec callers shall compile unchanged.
AC-26 optional: Where YAML style selection is later exposed, the system shall use existing codec options without changing the semantic model.
AC-27 unwanted: If any pipeline or publication stage fails, then existing output shall remain unchanged.
AC-28 optional: Where --allow-partial is enabled, migration shall recover only through target-version incompleteness constructs.
AC-29 unwanted: If serialization would drop, coerce, or ambiguously reinterpret IR, then --allow-partial shall not permit publication.
AC-30 ubiquitous: Each diagnostic shall include stable code, stage, severity, cursor, guidance, and source location when available.
AC-31 ubiquitous: The v4 specification shall separate the semantic model, JSON profile, YAML profile, and document-tree layout.
AC-32 ubiquitous: The v4 specification shall define logical document identities without physical serialization extensions.
AC-33 event-driven: When a normative YAML example round-trips through normalized IR and JSON, the result shall be semantically equal.
notes:
Design approved and written locally at .dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-native-yaml-ir-storage-design.md. Native YAML and JSON normalize to versioned semantic IR. Semantic equivalence defines losslessness. Canonical YAML uses deterministic readable shorthand with explicit structural fallback. Current CLI phase adds --input-format and --output-format for JSON/YAML; YAML style selection remains a compatible follow-up. Output resolution is explicit flag, known extension, then YAML default. Input uses explicit flag, known extension, then bounded JSON-first detection. Preserve the legacy context-dependent --json behavior. Homogeneous document trees default to YAML and use manifest.yaml, module.yaml, *.type.yaml, and *.value.yaml. Approved pipeline uses semantic cursor events, composable transforms, declared event/definition/module/distribution buffering, format encoders, layout sinks, and atomic publication. Open codec identifiers leave room for TOML, Markdown, Jupyter, and other adapters without implementing them now. Approved strict diagnostics keep --allow-partial from weakening serialization correctness. Approved v4 spec split: serialization-neutral semantic model, JSON profile, YAML profile, and document-tree profile. JSON Schema remains a bootstrap definition for JSON, not a persistence restriction. Logical identities omit physical extensions; resolve format versus manifest in favor of manifest. V3 semantics remain stable with complete explicit YAML coverage; v4 schema changes are allowed with documented migration behavior. Verification uses TDD, local quality gates, real morphir-elm and morphir-scala fixtures, semantic round-trips, single-file and document-tree acceptance paths, and instrumented bounded-scope LCR streaming. Implementation will use small commits pushed at completed sectional boundaries.

All seven verified Codex review findings were fixed and answered in their threads: JSON object-order independence, quoted YAML scalars, encoder ordering, rustdoc example, Cucumber/TestDriver coverage, YAML module split, and changelog. Dependency local gates passed: check:fmt, Rust/YAML lint, unit, integration, and docs. Parent PR finos/morphir#732 is at b424b288f896c164ef175e98aaac2a0768507e1c. Two automated review findings were independently verified and fixed with regressions: post-publication backup cleanup now warns without misreporting failure, and bounded YAML version detection accepts quoted root keys and flow mappings. Local fmt-check, Clippy with warnings denied, full workspace tests (including LCR streaming), and release workspace build pass. Preserve the unrelated unstaged website/static/validation-inline.worker.js change.

title: Design validated typestate MEP sessions
description: Separate untrusted MEP wire DTOs from validated application state, then assess a generic typestate session controller shared by Extism, spawned-process, and connected-daemon transports. The current session enum prevents some field combinations but still admits identity and capability drift, duplicate capability kinds, stringly typed operation calls, invalid JSON-RPC response envelopes, and uncertain lifecycle outcomes after cancellation or transport failure.
design: Recommended direction from the dedicated review: define an object-safe MepTransport that only exchanges wire requests and responses; put validation and lifecycle rules in Session<T, Loaded|Ready|Indeterminate|Stopped>; expose typed compile, generate, validate, and transform operations on Ready; use a ManagedSession enum only where registries or actors need runtime state erasure. Keep wire::InitializeResult deserializable even when peers disagree, then validate it into NegotiatedSession. Do not silently merge discovery and initialization claims.
acceptance_criteria: Document wire DTO versus validated domain boundaries; decide identity and capability drift policy; cover response JSON-RPC version, request ID correlation, and exactly-one-of-result-or-error validation; represent uncertain lifecycle outcomes explicitly; provide compile-fail tests for invalid state transitions; define migration from the object-safe ExtensionSession API without duplicating state machines across transports.
notes:
Rebased PR #93 onto connected-daemon main commit 6351b3e. New head 294991c integrates ConnectedDaemonTransport with MepTransport and migrates real HTTP conformance, 64 MiB payload, refusal, and timeout tests to Session typestates. Refusal and request timeout now retain Indeterminate because HTTP cannot prove remote state; acknowledged shutdown proves Stopped. Local connected/process/Extism/unit/doc/clippy checks pass. Replacement CI pending.
PR #93 head eee6cf2 boxes the state-bearing Session values in FailedSession, with a concrete ConnectedDaemonTransport size regression capped at 128 bytes. Replacement morphir-rust CI run 33122001751 passed every job, including integration, native process, connected daemon, WASM/Extism, lint, docs, coverage, and EasyCLA. Umbrella PR #707 commit 89481932 pins this head; its replacement run 33122067259 passed the previously failing morphir CLI consumer job plus all aggregate checks. PR #93 is CLEAN and MERGEABLE, all five review threads are resolved, and a final Codex review of eee6cf2 is pending. Leave the bead in progress until #93 is explicitly authorized, squash-merged, and #707 is repinned to the permanent main commit.
Final Codex review of head eee6cf2 posted two P2 findings: Session::loaded can wrap a SpawnedProcessSession already advanced through the compatibility API and reset lifecycle/request IDs; failure abort can still wait the full request timeout while collecting a stderr pipe inherited by a descendant. Both were assigned to the dedicated typestate worktree for TDD fixes. PR #93 remains open and must rerun morphir-rust and umbrella consumer verification after its head changes.
PR #93 head fcb9364 addresses the two final-review P2s. title: [UPDATED] Implement DirectRuntime for direct execution mode
description:
Implement DirectRuntime in morphir-ext for direct execution without actors or IPC, supporting CLI, Morphir-Live, and browser/WASM environments.

## PREREQUISITE: Gherkin Acceptance Tests Required

**BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION**: Prepare comprehensive Gherkin acceptance tests and present to user for approval/iteration. Implementation may NOT proceed without user verification of tests.

Gherkin tests must cover:
- DirectRuntime construction with ExtismRuntime
- execute() method with various function names and envelopes
- TEA lifecycle: init(), update(), subscriptions()
- Design-time operations: backend_generate(), frontend_compile()
- Error handling (WASM errors, envelope errors, missing functions)
- No dependency on Kameo or daemon infrastructure
- Works in WASM context (no_std compatible if needed)

## Background
DirectRuntime provides in-process extension execution without daemon/actor overhead. All clients (CLI, Morphir-Live, browser/WASM) can use DirectRuntime for embedded execution.

## Architecture

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Client Layer                           │
│  (CLI, Morphir-Live, Browser/WASM, IDE)                   │
└──────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                       │
                       │ Choice: Direct or Daemon
                       │
            ┌──────────┴──────────┐
            │                     │
            ▼                     ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────┐
  │  DirectRuntime   │   │  DaemonClient   │
  │  (morphir-ext)   │   │  (morphir-ext)  │
  └────────┬─────────┘   └────────┬────────┘
           │                      │
           │ No IPC               │ IPC (JSON-RPC)
           │                      │
           ▼                      ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────┐
  │ ExtismRuntime    │   │  Daemon Service │
  │ (morphir-ext)    │   │  with actors    │
  └────────┬─────────┘   └─────────────────┘
           │
           │ Loads WASM
           ▼
  ┌──────────────────┐
  │  Extension       │
  │  (WASM module)   │
  └──────────────────┘

DirectRuntime Flow:
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Client
  │
  └─> DirectRuntime::new(ExtismRuntime)
        │
        └─> execute("backend_generate", envelope)
              │
              └─> ExtismRuntime::call_envelope()
                    │
                    └─> Extism loads WASM
                          │
                          └─> Calls backend_generate()
                                │
                                └─> Returns envelope
```

## Implementation Location
- **File**: `morphir-ext/src/direct.rs`
- **Depends on**: `morphir-ext/src/runtime.rs` (ExtensionRuntime trait)
- **Uses**: `morphir-ext/src/extism_runtime.rs` (ExtismRuntime)

## Tasks

### 0. **FIRST: Create Gherkin acceptance tests and get user approval**
- [ ] Write Gherkin scenarios for DirectRuntime usage
- [ ] Include all execution modes (TEA + design-time)
- [ ] Present to user for review/iteration
- [ ] Get explicit approval before proceeding

### 1. Core Implementation
- [ ] Create `morphir-ext/src/direct.rs` module
- [ ] Implement DirectRuntime struct
- [ ] Wrap ExtensionInstance (which wraps ExtensionRuntime)
- [ ] Simple execute() API: `execute(func_name, input) -> Result<Envelope>`
- [ ] No actor infrastructure, no IPC
- [ ] No state management initially (stateless calls)

### 2. TEA Support
- [ ] Add init() helper method
- [ ] Add update() helper method
- [ ] Add subscriptions() helper method
- [ ] Maintain model state if needed

### 3. Design-Time Support
- [ ] Support backend_generate() calls
- [ ] Support frontend_compile() calls
- [ ] Support get_capabilities() calls

### 4. Error Handling
- [ ] Map ExtismRuntime errors to DirectRuntime errors
- [ ] Provide clear error messages
- [ ] Handle missing functions gracefully
- [ ] Handle envelope encoding/decoding errors

### 5. Testing
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios pass
- [ ] Unit tests with mock ExtensionRuntime
- [ ] Integration tests with real WASM (morphir-builtins migrate)
- [ ] Test in no_std context if targeting WASM
- [ ] Test error paths

### 6. Documentation
- [ ] API documentation
- [ ] Usage examples (native and WASM contexts)
- [ ] Comparison with DaemonClient

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Gherkin tests approved by user before implementation**
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios pass
- [ ] DirectRuntime compiles for native and wasm32-unknown-unknown
- [ ] Can execute migrate builtin in native mode
- [ ] TEA lifecycle methods work

- [ ] Clean error handling
- [ ] Documented with examples

│           ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐                   │
│           │                             │                    │
│  ┌────────┴────────┐         ┌─────────┴────────┐          │
│  │ MigrateExtension│         │ Future: TS Backend│          │
│  │ - Native impl   │         │ - Native impl     │          │
│  │ - WASM exports  │         │ - WASM exports    │          │
│  └─────────────────┘         └───────────────────┘          │
│           ▲                                                   │
│           │                                                   │
│  ┌────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┐          │
│  │         BuiltinRegistry                        │          │
│  │  - new() -> Self                               │          │
│  │  - get(id) -> Option<&dyn BuiltinExtension>   │          │
│  │  - list() -> Vec<BuiltinInfo>                 │          │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────┘          │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

title: Morphir x WebAssembly Component Model Interactive Guide
description:
Build an interactive, self-guided tutorial that explains the WebAssembly Component Model ABI (canonical ABI, lifting/lowering) while being extremely aware of Morphir IR.

## Goals
1. Map Morphir IR programs and types to WebAssembly (core Wasm level)
2. Evaluate whether Morphir IR could serve as a practical replacement for WIT
3. Identify gaps preventing this substitution (semantic/ABI/tooling mismatches)
4. Determine how Morphir could be enhanced to support this use case

## Modules (Progressive)
- Core Wasm boundary constraints (i32/i64/f32/f64, linear memory)
- Canonical ABI: lifting and lowering
- Scalars (bool/int/float)
- Strings and byte sequences (ptr/len, encoding)
- Lists, records/structs, tuples
- Variants/enums, option/result
- Functions, multi-arg/multi-return, flattening rules
- Resources/handles (ownership, borrowing patterns)
- Error handling and traps vs typed errors
- Versioning and evolution patterns
- Performance considerations (copies, allocations, alignment)

## Deliverables per Module
- Conceptual explanation with ASCII diagrams
- Code snippets in F#, Scala, Go
- Morphir IR examples (types + functions)
- Core Wasm function signature and memory layout
- WIT replacement check (what Morphir has, what's missing, candidate enhancements)
- Confidence check questions

## Key Questions
- Can Morphir IR act as an IDL/interface definition layer analogous to WIT?
- Can we derive canonical ABI lowering/lifting rules from Morphir IR types?
- What semantics does WIT have that Morphir IR lacks?
- What additions would make Morphir IR more suitable?

title: Create reusable TUI framework for interactive morphir commands
description:
Build a shared TUI framework that provides consistent interactive experiences across morphir commands.

## Overview
Create a reusable TUI component in `cmd/morphir/internal/tui` that can be used by:
- `morphir` (main interactive mode)
- `morphir validate --tui`
- Future commands like `morphir explore`, `morphir inspect`, etc.

## Architecture
```
cmd/morphir/internal/tui/
├── app.go           # Main TUI application shell
├── layout.go        # Flexible layout manager (sidebar + main)
├── components/
│   ├── sidebar.go   # Collapsible sidebar with tree/list
│   ├── viewer.go    # Markdown/content viewer with paging
│   ├── statusbar.go # Bottom status/help bar
│   └── searchbar.go # Search/filter input
├── styles/
│   └── theme.go     # Consistent lipgloss styling
└── keymap/
    └── vim.go       # Vim-style keybindings
```

## Core Components

### AppShell
Main application container that manages:
- Layout (sidebar width, visibility)
- Focus management between panels
- Global keybindings (quit, help, toggle sidebar)
- Resize handling

### SidebarPanel
- Tree view for hierarchical content
- List view for flat content  
- Collapsible (toggle with `b` or `Ctrl+b`)
- Filterable

### ViewerPanel
- Glamour-rendered markdown
- Viewport with vim navigation (j/k, gg/G, Ctrl+d/u)
- Search within content (/)
- Line numbers (optional)

### StatusBar
- Current mode indicator
- Keybinding hints
- File/position info

## Usage Pattern
```go
// In validate command
app := tui.NewApp(
    tui.WithSidebar(fileList),
    tui.WithViewer(markdownContent),
    tui.WithTitle("Validation Report"),
)
return app.Run()

// In main morphir command
app := tui.NewApp(
    tui.WithSidebar(commandList),
    tui.WithViewer(welcomeContent),
    tui.WithTitle("Morphir"),
)
return app.Run()
```

## Keybindings (Vim-style)
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| j/k | Scroll down/up |
| h/l | Switch panels |
| gg/G | Go to top/bottom |
| Ctrl+d/u | Page down/up |
| / | Search |
| n/N | Next/prev search result |
| b | Toggle sidebar |
| q | Quit |
| ? | Show help |

## Libraries
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Components
- `github.com/charmbracelet/glamour` - Markdown
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling

## Blocked By
None - this is a foundational component

## Blocks
- morphir-tol (TUI validate command)

title: Expose supported Workbench languages and generation backends
description:
Expose already-supported input/compiler and generation-backend choices in the shared browser/Proton Workbench instead of its current hard-coded local Scheme-only catalog and worker dispatch. This UI integration can proceed independently of the next output/outcome admission contract slice.

Register/use the pure MoonBit Boolean source frontend, explicitly label its moonbit-model-bool-v1 supported subset, retain Scheme, and route selected languages through real worker compilation without silent fallback. Preserve rich IR metadata and provenance from source units. Reuse model inspection and typed Explorer evaluation for admitted public entries; do not assume every source function is the Scheme main entry.

Expose real generation capabilities, initially existing Scheme and MoonBit library generation plus suitable IR representations. MoonBit generation returns multiple source/manifest and binary metadata artifacts, so provide artifact selection and lossless export rather than flattening the bundle into one source string. Preserve per-language drafts, CodeMirror highlighting, appropriate examples and separate compile/generate/evaluate availability. Reject unavailable language/backend combinations explicitly.

Connected mode already reads the host frontend/target catalog and has real Rust v1 Gleam acceptance; retain host negotiation and capability checks. Distinguish a generation backend such as MoonBit from generated execution targets such as JS, Wasm GC, native or LLVM. CLI/provider execution acceptance does not establish browser execution: native Proton IPC and standalone generated-code embedding remain separate pending work. No new connected evaluation method or full MoonBit language support is claimed by this slice.
design:
07

Delivery & proof

Reconciled on 02 October 2026 against merged main 40587e6. E1 generation landed in PR #31; E2 Tasks 1–3 in PR #32, lifecycle Task 4 in PR #34 and independent conformance Task 5 in PR #35. PR #36 merged structured results, typed fields/JSON/Ion inputs, live Rust v1 acceptance and portable CLI parsing after incorporating both execution phases. All 16 final-head checks, full local checks and explicit conformance acceptance passed. The upstream profile now has merged decode/declared-value contracts and published invocation admission in PRs #1035/#44. Output/outcome admission is the next contract slice, followed by broader semantic coverage and host adoption.

Completion checklist

Checked boxes indicate completed work within the stated scope. Unchecked boxes indicate remaining work, including work in progress. A local implementation can be complete while its merge remains pending. These read-only indicators reflect evidence in the shared tracker, not editable task state.

Completed

Pending and in progress

Typed invocation is local commit d850944, after structured results at 722a126. Both continuations landed in PR #36 at fd4026e. The public manifest governs admitted entries; tagged arguments use morphir-invocations-v1, and the shared bounded Scheme evaluator returns canonical typed values. Exact Int/Decimal, signed-zero Float64 bits, UTF-16 units, Maybe/Result, records and custom ownership have focused acceptance. Browser and packaged CEF import the pricing fixture. Typed convenience controls are complete and merged in PR #36 in morphir-ukvn.5.17. Generated-code execution and connected transport remain pending. Local IR text is retained across the JavaScript boundary for exact large-integer evaluation, inspection and export.

Stage / statusNext deliverableEvidence to proceed
Retain the shared shell, explorer, generated inputs, editor components, local Scheme worker and Proton package. Keep the result-view continuation identified separately.Existing browser/CEF workflows remain green; drafts, selection, sidebar context, cancellation, stale results and exact numbers survive integration.
Local worker mode now uses ValueType/public manifests, a reusable typed-input component, custom registry, Suite/Value codecs and the portable Scheme evaluator. Typed fields and JSON share a canonical document; Ion converts through the published codec without changing exact values. Invalid conversions retain the original draft. Dynamic Scheme/worksheet remains available. Native and connected adapters remain separate pending stages.Exact Int/Decimal, Float64 bits, UTF-16 units, Maybe/Result and constructor ownership round-trip. Generated-only restrictions remain visible without hiding inspectable declarations. The private 500-node result tree never becomes a normative wire codec.
Update morphir-etg2 around adoption of existing invocation/outcome profiles. Specify revision handles, jobs/cancellation, worksheet source maps, transport limits and artifact semantics; retain the real Rust v1 acceptance regression completed in morphir-ukvn.5.20.Normative finos/morphir contribution and language-neutral fixtures; coordinated Rust/TypeScript/MoonBit adoption. New operations stay unavailable until negotiated. Current v1 methods preserve their shapes.
Use engine plan/run and host-owned provider sessions through Proton IPC. Reuse compiler acquisition/pins and generated drivers. A standalone generated-code browser lane needs an explicit provider backed by verified browser embedding.Selected capabilities and dependency snapshots match the host; no target substitution. Browser workers never import the Node/native process provider. LLVM requires its separate tested nightly/core pin and verified host. Existing Proton worker mode stays supported.
Reuse Engine::list_projects, plan boundaries, IRUnit codecs, host grants and artifact reports. Keep source/model snapshots alongside display projections. Wait for E2 lifecycle/publication acceptance before offering verification-backed publication.Ion metadata and identities survive processing; Morphir JSON remains supported through explicit loss-aware boundaries. Generated, validated, invoked, compared, cleaned-up and committed output have separate evidence. Failure preserves prior output.
Run the same versioned fixture intersection through standalone, native and connected adapters; add recovery, persistence and platform package checks.E2 Tasks 4–6 are complete and merged, including lifecycle, independent conformance, installed/debug-release CI and native OTLP HTTP/JSON collector acceptance on Linux/macOS. Shared-SDK Scheme agreement is identified accurately; cross-host adoption and other telemetry protocols remain separate. Connected durability/replay is proved separately.

Integration rules from the merges

  • Reuse the public invocation manifest as the generated execution authority. Local generic aliases and dynamic Scheme values may remain available through their own runtime capability even when the generator rejects them.
  • Separate 200-node input forms and 500-node result display limits from execution budgets. Preserve full semantic values and Ion metadata; report unsupported or omitted presentation explicitly.
  • Exact comparison is the default. Approximate comparison requires an explicit policy and finite tolerances. Display selected target, evaluator profile and evidence; do not label shared-SDK agreement independent conformance.
  • Host-injected observations carry timing and correlation outside model/call identity. Required results bypass telemetry queues. Payload capture stays opt-in with a redactor; dropped observations cannot change a job outcome.
  • Model Result.Err, enumerated SDK model errors, validation failures, provider failures, cancellation and cleanup failures need distinct presentation. Preserve primary and cleanup causes once the E2 lifecycle contract lands.

Acceptance checklist

Build and assets

Build the UI for JavaScript, stage its CSS and worker assets, then consume that distribution from the static web deployment, daemon asset server, and Proton package. Bundle required assets locally for standalone and installed use.

Proton's CLI/runtime/framework versions stay aligned. Match embedded compiler and dependency interfaces to the repository's pinned toolchain. Verify packages on each supported OS.

Focused verification

Use MoonBit checks and formatting for package boundaries and target support. Run contract scenarios against each adapter. Browser checks verify the real workflow, responsiveness, focus, and cancellation.

For desktop, include installed-package smoke checks for asset lookup, the native bridge, workspace grants, and platform editing shortcuts. Timing numbers are measured during the slice, not assumed in this design.

Merge readiness and current main

The maintainer approved squash merges of parent PR #1033 and MoonBit PR #42 when checks are green, including an administrator bypass where policy requires it. Main now contains PR #40 at 32f2033; merge 7e3fd35 integrates its rich MoonBit source units into this continuation. The engine/CLI explicitly registers the bounded Boolean source frontend. PR #41 subsequently landed at b1a0298 with all 19 CI contexts successful. It adds installed MoonBit source lowering to Ion and independent Boolean truth-table comparison through original source, Scheme and generated execution across required targets in debug/release. The fresh DamianReeves/workbench-invocation-admission continuation starts from merged main 40587e6 and includes both frontend phases. The local Workbench still compiles Scheme, so exposing MoonBit source selection in the browser/Proton worker remains a separate follow-up. No new connected capabilities are advertised.

Combined local verification passes. Parent PR #1033 merged at 95c1aecb after all 17 final-head contexts completed successfully, skipped or neutral. MoonBit PR #42 merged at 40587e6 after all 20 final-head contexts passed on 7e3fd35. No unresolved review threads remained. The approved admin bypass was used for the parent required-review rule; MoonBit merged normally. Both PR watchers observed MERGED and stopped.

Full architecture, protocol inventory, Mermaid/SVG diagrams and implementation screenshots remain in the local workbench HTML design, Revision 30. Live Rust v1 acceptance is complete and merged in PR #36 in morphir-ukvn.5.20. Normative upstream profile publication remains morphir-etg2; evaluation, jobs and cancellation extensions still require upstream adoption.

CLI argparse portability check

Main 1f8c9ad adds the shared-worktree beads database check and requires new or changed task automation to use portable MoonBit scripts. It is incorporated into this continuation at merge 775f704; mise run beads:check passes. The existing browser/desktop UI is unaffected.

A local CLI experiment, preserved in .dev/argparse-spike.patch, replaced handwritten argument loops with moonbitlang/core/argparse command definitions. Contextual help, global output flags, declared repeated values, duplicate/arity checks and the opaque child-argument segment are covered. Five focused parser tests pass per JavaScript, native, Wasm and Wasm GC. Native/JS workspace flows, the installed npm package and real execute/verify through native/Node/npm hosts pass on JS, Wasm GC and native execution targets.

The actual standalone WASI artifact fails the existing import gate. Core Command::parse retains its optional default-argv branch, which links __moonbit_fs_unstable argument and external-string imports even when the application supplies argv explicitly. The WASI contract currently permits only wasi_snapshot_preview1 imports. Unit tests under MoonBit runtime do not establish WASI embedding compatibility.

That core-argparse experiment was restored after failing the standalone WASI import gate. The adopted Yoorkin/ArgParser integration, documented below, preserves the existing WASI-only contract and now passes full CLI acceptance. Future core-argparse adoption still requires a pure explicit-argv API that passes the same gate. Keep JSON/JSON-lines help and error envelopes, exact values, pipeline last-value overrides and child --help/--json/empty/Unicode arguments in either implementation. The official argparse quickstart demonstrates explicit argv for native CLIs; the artifact-level portability finding comes from local builds.

Alternative parser comparison

Target support is the acceptance requirement. Candidate probes use the repository-pinned MoonBit toolchain and explicit argv. Yoorkin/ArgParser has now passed the full CLI integration described below; other candidates retain only their stated probe evidence.

title: Qualify public-entry and invocation admission through shared Workbench MCK
description: Add exact Workbench MCK draft.3 validate-invocations for a frozen JSON/Ion morphir-invocations-v1 suite against a supplied bounded public-entry manifest. Extract portable entry/arity/type validation from the engine into morphir-execution and preserve engine diagnostics. Admit all manifest input/output and registry descriptors with complete reference closure before suite decoding. Parent authors independent goldens and validates ordered canonical suite observations/report operation inventory. Preserve draft.1/.2 artifacts and negotiation; no execution/provider/SDK/output-value/connected extension claim.
design:
Public-entry and invocation admission

Implementation validated after merged parent PR #1033 / 95c1aecb and MoonBit PR #42 / 40587e6. MoonBit main includes rich source-unit PR #40 and installed source execution PR #41. This slice extends the shared offline MCK contract to exact 0.1.0-draft.3.

Completion checklist

Boundary

The operation validate-invocations takes exactly {suite,manifest}. The suite uses the existing morphir-invocations-v1 JSON object or one Ion text string. The JSON manifest is exactly {entries,definitions}; entries are exactly {name,inputs,output}. Listed entries are the authoritative public/supported allowlist. Missing entries return the existing generic rejection. This tests supplied manifest membership, not correspondence with a model or hidden declaration visibility.

The portable execution package gains a public entry descriptor and shared invocation validation extracted from the engine. The engine continues to preserve its trusted unsupported-boundary diagnostics. The adapter admits every input/output/unused declaration before decoding data; the shared validator reuses Suite.validate and validate_as.

Limits and evidence

The whole compact input remains at most 1 MiB. The manifest admits at most 1,000 unique entry names of 1–1,024 UTF-16 units and 64 inputs each. Entry nodes share the 10,000-node declaration budget. Draft.2 depth, registry and descriptor limits remain. All output types require supported closed declarations even though this slice validates arguments alone.

Suite limits remain 1–1,000 unique calls, 128-unit call IDs, 1,024-unit entry identities, 64 arguments and 100,000 value/UTF-16 nodes per call. JSON extension bytes survive exactly. Ion text extension fixtures test only their specified binary projections; general binary/reverse encoding remains separate work. Reports preserve call/argument order, sort only record fields and reject model-error arguments.

Qualification uses parent-owned goldens through the existing Rust runner, with exact draft/operation negotiation and independent saved-report rechecking. Draft.1/.2 artifacts remain byte-identical and are replayed. No function execution, output value admission, SDK comparison, provider acquisition or new connected RPC is included. Connected protocol v1 and frozen payload identifiers remain unchanged.

Validation receipts

The 242-case draft.3 corpus qualifies and independently report-rechecks on Node/native debug/release. The final runner also replays all 64 draft.1 and 162 draft.2 cases on those lanes. Twenty-three pure adapter tests pass JS, native, Wasm and Wasm GC. Parent gates pass 33 focused Rust tests, five CLI subprocess tests, 176 structural schema tests and all three corpus documents, plus Clippy with denied warnings and formatting. Independent semantic review found no defect; report-forgery probes reject altered capabilities, operation claims, model-error arguments, extension bytes and call/argument ordering.

Full MoonBit mise run check and required validation pass. Parent commit 1497292e and MoonBit commit 30e9974 contain this implementation. Paired draft PRs finos/morphir #1035 and MoonBit #44 are published. Shared bead morphir-etg2.5 records the completed implementation; broader morphir-etg2 remains in progress. Evidence remains local under .dev/workbench-invocation/. Background CI/review monitors are running; merge remains pending.

Planned reachability policies

Current exact draft.3 remains strict and unchanged. Both follow-ups need explicit supported-policy and compatibility evidence. Output/outcome admission is the next technical slice in the existing upstream profile plan.

Shared entry validator is used by engine and adapter, preserving selected-entry diagnostics and validation-before-provider behavior. Whole declarations close all dormant types; suite identity/arity/type/extension limits pass focused regressions. Draft.1/.2 schemas, fixtures and kits are unchanged and replayed. Required checks, review, HTML checkbox evidence and beads sync pass.

design:
Declared-value admission qualification

The new validate-value operation accepts a JSON or Ion text value together with JSON type descriptors and constructor definitions. The adapter admits a bounded closed declaration graph, rejects duplicates, unresolved names and dormant function types, permits named recursion, then calls the shipped value codec and validate_as. title: Elm Backend Implementation Plan
description:
# Elm Backend Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add the `elm` generation backend: current Morphir IR in, a buildable Elm package project out, printed by the
krueger 0.4.0 printer.

**Architecture:** A new MoonBit module `finos/morphir-elm` with one package, `finos/morphir-elm/backend`, lowers IR
to the krueger elm-syntax AST and prints it with `@printer.print_file`. It has no engine or host imports. The engine
gets per-backend options (`[backends.<name>]`) and registers `elm` as a generation backend. A Node script checks the
generated projects with `elm make`.

**Tech Stack:** MoonBit 0.10.14 (pinned by mise), `moonrockz/krueger@0.4.0`, `finos/morphir-ir@0.1.0`, Node 24 and
the npm `elm` package (0.19.1) for acceptance only.

**Spec:** design of beads epic `morphir-ukvn.5.22.1` (render with
`mise run beads:plan -- spec morphir-ukvn.5.22.1 --render`, file `.dev/beads-specs/morphir-ukvn.5.22.1.md`).
Section "Spec amendments" below lists where this plan is more exact than the spec. The spec carries the same list.

## Global Constraints

- Module `finos/morphir-elm`, version `0.1.0`, license `Apache-2.0`, path `pkgs/morphir-elm`, member of `moon.work`.
- Dependencies of the backend package: `finos/morphir-ir@0.1.0` and `moonrockz/krueger@0.4.0` only (plus
  `moonbitlang/core` packages). No engine, host, filesystem, process or network imports.
- The backend must build and test on all four targets: `wasm`, `wasm-gc`, `js`, `native`.
- Error codes start with `elm.` (`elm.tuple_arity`, `elm.derived_type`, `elm.decimal_literal`, `elm.placeholder`,
  `elm.invalid_mapping`, `elm.print`, plus the codes in the amendments).
- Profiles: `model` (default) and `literal`. Placeholders: `refuse` (default) and `debug-todo`. Width default `120`.
- Default Elm SDK package: `finos/morphir-elm` version `22.0.2` (published on package.elm-lang.org, checked
  2026-10-02).
- The same input and options give the same output bytes.
- Commits use Conventional Commits in plain English, with no AI attribution and no `Co-Authored-By` lines. End each
  commit message with the line `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01D1669zmcEmkqP5VqAFRFh7`.
- Run `moon fmt` and `moon info` before each commit (the repository's pre-push checks are in `.github/AGENTS.md`).

## Spec amendments

These come from facts found while planning. Each one is in the spec's "Amendments" section.

1. **Package-type `elm.json`.** An application `elm.json` must list every indirect dependency with an exact version,
   which needs a solver. A package `elm.json` takes version ranges, so the generator writes `"type": "package"`.
   Because of this, `[backends.elm.packages]` entries take only `{ package = "author/name 1.2.3" }`. The
   source-directory form is a follow-on.
2. **Option key spelling.** `elm_package`, not `elm-package`, to match the snake_case keys in the rest of the
   configuration (`source_directory`, `out_dir`).
3. **Doc-comment attributes follow the krueger grammar.** An attribute name is `lower ("." lower)*` and its value is
   Elm data. The generator writes an `attributes` code block with `@morphir.entry { kind = "main", name = "..." }`,
   `@morphir.annotation { fqname = "...", ... }` and `@morphir.external { platform = "...", name = "..." }`.
4. **Constraint attribute.** Key `typeclass` in `TypeAttributes.constraints`. The value is `Text` or `Array` of
   `Text`. `["appendable", "comparable"]` becomes `compappend`. Any other set is `elm.unsupported_constraint`.
5. **More error codes.** `elm.int_literal` (lexeme outside Int64), `elm.document_literal`, `elm.literal_pattern`
   (float or decimal pattern, which Elm rejects), `elm.unsupported_constraint`, `elm.name_collision` (two IR names
   give one Elm name in a module), `elm.invalid_option`, `elm.cancelled`.
6. **Generation backend contract.** `GenerationBackend` gets `validate_options : (Json) -> Unit raise` and
   `targets : Array[String]`. A generator with no targets defaults to `pipeline.validation = "source-only"`, and
   `"required"` is refused with `build.unsupported_target`. The MoonBit generator declares
   `["wasm", "wasm-gc", "js", "native"]` and keeps its behavior.
7. **Built-in mapping source.** The table is generated from `pkgs/morphir-sdk/conformance/bindings.json`: every
   binding whose `semanticSource` is `elm/core 1.0.5` maps to the elm/core function of the same name, plus a
   hand-written list of types, constructors and operators. Other SDK references stay qualified.
8. **`elm.print` node path.** The path names the IR declaration whose AST did not print. The generator finds it by
   printing each declaration alone after `print_file` fails.
9. **No signatures on `let` functions.** Elm reads type variables in a `let` annotation as new rigid variables, so
   generated `let` functions have no signature.
10. **No shadowing.** Elm rejects a local name that shadows another name in scope. The lowering renames such names
    (`x` becomes `x_1`).
11. **Existing fixture corpus in engine tests.** The `finos/morphir-moonbit/fixtures` IR builders are already a
    dependency of `finos/morphir-engine` tests. The engine tests run the `elm` generator over them, so the Elm module
    does not depend on `finos/morphir-moonbit`.

## Review Focus

- **Shadowed local names** (`let x = 1 in let x = x + 1 in x`, or a lambda argument with the name of a top-level
  value): the Elm output must rename them so that `elm make` accepts it. Test in Task 5.
- **Documentation that contains `-}`**: the doc comment must not end early. The generator writes `- }`. Test in
  Task 6.
- **A module with no public members**: Elm rejects an empty exposing list, so the module exposes `(..)`. Test in
  Task 6.
- **Integer lexemes that are negative, or outside Int64**: negative values print as negation; values outside Int64
  give `elm.int_literal`, not a crash. Test in Task 5.
- **Two IR names that give the same Elm name in one module** (for example values `x-BC` and `x-B-C`, which both
  print as `xBC`): refuse with `elm.name_collision`, not silently overwrite. Test in Task 6.

---

## File structure

```
pkgs/morphir-elm/
  moon.mod                         module manifest
  README.md                        usage, profiles, options, limits
  backend/
    moon.pkg
    names.mbt                      Name/Path/FQName -> Elm identifiers; reserved words; type-variable prefixes
    names_wbtest.mbt
    errors.mbt                     Problem, ElmGenerationError, refuse
    mapping.mbt                    MappingEntry, Mapping, overrides, JSON entry parsing
    mapping_builtin.mbt            GENERATED built-in table (do not edit)
    mapping_wbtest.mbt
    options.mbt                    Profile, Placeholders, ElmPackageRef, Options, from_json, validate_options
    options_test.mbt
    context.mbt                    Ctx: imports, scopes, fresh names, resolution of FQNames
    lower_types.mbt                types and type declarations
    lower_types_wbtest.mbt
    lower_values.mbt               literals, patterns, values
    lower_values_wbtest.mbt
    module.mbt                     value declarations, docs, attributes, exposing, File, printing
    module_wbtest.mbt
    generate.mbt                   GeneratedFile, Output, generate, elm.json, morphir.json
    generate_test.mbt
  fixtures/
    moon.pkg
    fixtures.mbt                   IR builders used by tests and acceptance
  acceptance/
    moon.pkg                       executable
    main.mbt                       prints generated projects as JSON
  scripts/
    generate-builtin-mapping.py    writes backend/mapping_builtin.mbt
    test-elm-make.mjs              runs elm make on acceptance output
    package.json, package-lock.json   pins npm elm
pkgs/morphir-engine/
  generation.mbt                   GenerationBackend fields, elm_generation
  plan.mbt                         options lookup and validation default
  types.mbt                        registers elm
  config/config.mbt                Document::json, backends section validation
  elm_generation_test.mbt          engine tests for elm
  moon.mod, moon.pkg               depend on finos/morphir-elm
pkgs/morphir-host/library_build_test.mbt   new GenerationBackend fields
.config/mise/tasks/test/elm, elm.ps1       acceptance task
.github/workflows/ci.yml                   acceptance step
moon.work                                  new member
```

---

title: Elm backend: Morphir IR to Elm with krueger printer

design:
# Elm backend with krueger: design

Date: 2026-10-02. Status: approved 2026-10-02. Amended during planning (section 9).

## 1. Purpose and context

This is sub-project 1 of the Elm initiative (see the umbrella epic). The initiative gives finos/morphir-moonbit an Elm
frontend and an Elm backend that use [moonrockz/krueger](https://github.com/moonrockz/krueger). The order is:

1. Elm backend (this spec): current Morphir IR to Elm source.
2. IR type inference: a language-neutral Hindley-Milner pass over Morphir IR.
3. Elm frontend: Elm source to typed Morphir IR, with parity against `morphir-elm make`.
4. Wiring: `morphir.json` project discovery, CLI and workbench.

The backend comes first. It gives a visible result quickly, it does not need type inference, and its output is the
round-trip harness for sub-projects 2 and 3.

krueger 0.4.0 parses Elm 0.19.1 into the elm-syntax 7.3.9 AST and prints an AST as Elm in the elm-format 0.8.7
layout (`print_file`, width 120 by default). The printer raises `PrintError` with a `NodePath` when an AST cannot
print as valid Elm. It prints doc comments but not regular comments.

### Success criteria

- `pipeline.backend = "elm"` generates an Elm project from current IR through `Engine::plan` and `Engine::execute`.
- In the `model` profile, `elm make` accepts the generated project for every fixture in the golden corpus that
  contains no refused construct.
- Every generated file parses with `krueger.parse_module` with no diagnostics, in both profiles.
- The same input gives the same output bytes.

## 2. Architecture

### Package

New workspace member `pkgs/morphir-elm`, module `finos/morphir-elm`. It depends on `finos/morphir-ir` and
`moonrockz/krueger@0.4.0`. Like `finos/morphir-moonbit`, it has no engine, host, filesystem, process or network
imports. This sub-project adds only `backend/`. Sub-project 3 adds `frontend/` beside it.

| Unit | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/names` | Morphir `Name`, `Path` and `FQName` to Elm identifiers and module names. The Elm module name is the package path followed by the module path. Reserved words get the suffix `_`. Constrained type variables get their Elm prefix. |
| `backend/mapping` | The `Mapping` table from `FQName` to `Operator`, `Function` or `Type`, each with an optional import. It holds the built-in partial SDK table, merges overrides and removes entries. |
| `backend/lower` | Current IR types, values, patterns and definitions to krueger AST. The profile decides how references resolve. |
| `backend/project` | One `.elm` file for each IR module, plus `elm.json` and `morphir.json`. |
| `backend/generate` | Entry point `generate(Input, Options) -> Output`. Calls `@printer.print_file` for each module. Raises `ElmGenerationError`. |

`Options` holds `profile`, `placeholders`, `width`, `elm_package`, `mapping` and `packages` (section 4).

### Engine changes

- `GenerationBackend.generate` gets a third parameter: the backend options table from `[backends.<name>]`.
- A generation backend supplies a schema for its table. The engine validates the table and reports unknown keys and
  bad values as configuration diagnostics, with the provenance from `config.Document`.
- The MoonBit generator accepts the new parameter and ignores it. Its behavior does not change.
- `Engine::new` registers the generation backend `elm` beside `moonbit`.

### Out of scope

The frontend, type inference, `morphir.json` discovery, CLI flags other than configuration, workbench UI, regular
comments, and the IR to Elm to IR round trip. The round trip comes with sub-project 3.

## 3. Profiles and SDK mapping

There are two profiles.

- `model` (default) generates a Morphir Elm model project. References with a mapping entry use idiomatic Elm, for
  example `+` for `morphir/SDK:basics#add` and `List.map` for `morphir/SDK:list#map`. This is the inverse of the
  morphir-elm frontend.
- `literal` ignores the mapping. Every reference stays fully qualified, for example
  `Morphir.SDK.Basics.add a b`. It is a debug view of the IR.

The `model` profile does not need a full mapping of the Morphir SDK. The built-in table covers only the references
that have a clear Elm idiom. A reference with no mapping entry stays a qualified reference with its `import`, for
example `Morphir.SDK.LocalDate.addDays`. The `finos/morphir-elm` Elm package supplies those modules, and
`backend/project` adds it to `elm.json` only when the generated code uses an unmapped `Morphir.SDK` reference. A
missing mapping entry never stops generation.

The mapping is data. Configuration can override or extend the built-in table for any `FQName`, not only SDK
references, so a user can map references in their own package to existing Elm code. An empty entry removes a built-in
entry, and the reference falls back to the qualified form.

## 4. Configuration

```toml
[pipeline]
backend = "elm"

[backends.elm]
profile = "model"            # "model" (default) | "literal"
placeholders = "refuse"      # "refuse" (default) | "debug-todo"
width = 120
elm-package = "finos/morphir-elm 22.0.2"

[backends.elm.mapping]
"morphir/SDK:basics#add" = { operator = "+" }
"morphir/SDK:list#map" = { function = "List.map" }
"morphir/SDK:decimal#decimal" = { type = "Decimal.Decimal", import = "MyCo.Decimal as Decimal" }
"morphir/SDK:basics#max" = {}

[backends.elm.packages]
"acme/common" = { package = "acme/common 1.0.0" }
"acme/local" = { source = "../acme-local/src" }
```

- `elm-package` is the Elm package and version for unmapped `Morphir.SDK` references. The default is the
  `finos/morphir-elm` version in that repository's `elm.json` (22.0.2 on 2026-10-02). The implementation plan
  confirms that the version is published on package.elm-lang.org before it becomes the default.
- A `mapping` key is an IR `FQName` in canonical text form. A value has exactly one of `operator`, `function` or
  `type`, and an optional `import`. A malformed key or value is the configuration diagnostic `invalid_mapping`.
- `packages` maps a Morphir dependency package to an Elm package with a version, or to a source directory, for
  `elm.json`. A dependency with no entry does not stop generation. The `elm make` check reports it.
- In the `literal` profile, a non-empty `mapping` gives a warning, not an error.

## 5. Lowering rules

### Distributions and modules

- `Library` and `Application` generate every module of the package. For `Application`, each entry point becomes the
  doc-comment attribute `@entryPoint <kind>` on its target value. krueger reads doc-comment attributes, so the
  frontend can restore entry points.
- `Specs` generate type declarations. Value specifications have no body, so they follow the placeholder policy.
- References into dependency packages stay qualified.
- Public types and values are exposed. Private ones are not. A custom type with private constructors is exposed as
  `T`, not `T(..)`.
- Module documentation becomes the module doc comment. Member documentation becomes the doc comment of the
  declaration.

### Types

- A `Reference` with a mapping entry uses it. Any other `Reference` is qualified.
- `Record`, `ExtensibleRecord`, `Function` and `Unit` map directly to their Elm forms.
- A `Tuple` with more than three elements is refused with `tuple_arity`. Elm 0.19 rejects such tuples.
- A type variable with a `constraints` entry in its `TypeAttributes` gets the Elm prefix of that constraint
  (`number`, `comparable`, `appendable` or `compappend`). An unconstrained variable whose name starts with one of
  these prefixes is renamed so that Elm does not read it as constrained.
- Type aliases stay aliases. Custom types keep their constructor order.
- Derived types are refused with `derived_type`. A follow-on bead covers them.

### Values

- A chain of `Apply` becomes one `Application`.
- A mapped operator with both arguments becomes an `OperatorApplication`. With fewer arguments it becomes a prefix
  operator, for example `(+) a`.
- `LetDefinition`, `LetRecursion` and `Destructure` merge into one `let` block where scoping allows.
- `FieldFunction` becomes `.field`.
- Elm requires a variable as the target of a record update. `UpdateRecord` with any other target binds the target to
  a fresh name in a `let` first.
- `Int` literals keep the exact lexeme. A value outside the Elm range is refused through the printer's
  `UnrepresentableInt`.
- `Decimal` literals are refused with `decimal_literal` until a construction mapping exists.
- Fresh names never capture names in scope.

### v4-only constructs

- `Annotation` becomes the doc-comment attribute `@<fqname> <arguments>`.
- `ExternalBody` with a fallback value emits the fallback, plus `@external <platform> <name>` for each binding.
- `Hole`, `IncompleteBody`, `NativeBody`, `ExternalBody` without a fallback, and `Specs` values follow the
  placeholder policy:
  - `placeholders = "refuse"` (default) raises `ElmGenerationError` with code `placeholder`.
  - `placeholders = "debug-todo"` emits `Debug.todo "<reason>"`. `elm make` accepts this, but
    `elm make --optimize` does not.

### Determinism

Declarations keep IR order. Imports are sorted. The same input and options give the same bytes.

## 6. Errors

`ElmGenerationError { code, node_path, detail }`, where `node_path` identifies the IR node. The codes are:

| Code | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `tuple_arity` | Tuple with more than three elements |
| `derived_type` | Derived type definition |
| `decimal_literal` | Decimal literal with no construction mapping |
| `placeholder` | Construct with no body while `placeholders = "refuse"` |
| `invalid_mapping` | Mapping entry that is not valid at generation time, for example an operator that krueger does not know |
| `print` | krueger `PrintError`, with the IR node path of the AST node that failed |

A `print` error means that the lowering made an AST that is not valid, so it is a backend defect. Tests treat any
`print` error as a failure.

Generation of a module stops at its first error. All modules are tried, so one run reports every failing module.

## 7. Testing

- **Unit tests**: `names` (case, reserved words, constraint prefixes), `mapping` (merge, override, removal) and each
  lowering rule in both profiles, as snapshot tests of the printed Elm.
- **Golden corpus**: the classic v3 reference models in `pkgs/morphir-ir/conformance/fixtures` and the SDK examples,
  migrated to current IR and generated in both profiles. Output snapshots must be stable.
- **Parse-back law**: every generated file parses with `krueger.parse_module` with no diagnostics. This runs on all
  MoonBit targets.
- **`elm make` acceptance**: `pkgs/morphir-elm/scripts/test-elm-make.mjs` runs `elm make` on the generated `model`
  projects, with the npm `elm` 0.19.1 package pinned in `package.json`. Mise task `test:elm` runs it, in the same
  pattern as `test:compiler`, and CI runs the task. `literal` output gets only the parse-back law.
- **Engine tests**: options table pass-through, schema validation and diagnostics, and `elm` registration through
  `Engine::plan` and `Engine::execute`. The MoonBit generator tests stay unchanged and must pass.

## 8. Follow-on work

- Derived types (`derived_type`) and decimal literal construction (`decimal_literal`).
- Sub-projects 2, 3 and 4 of the initiative.

## 9. Amendments

These come from facts found while writing the implementation plan (2026-10-02). Where this section and the sections above disagree, this section wins.

1. **Package-type `elm.json`.** An application `elm.json` must list every indirect dependency with an exact version,
   which needs a solver. A package `elm.json` takes version ranges, so the generator writes `"type": "package"`.
   Because of this, `[backends.elm.packages]` entries take only `{ package = "author/name 1.2.3" }`. The
   source-directory form is a follow-on.
2. **Option key spelling.** `elm_package`, not `elm-package`, to match the snake_case keys in the rest of the
   configuration (`source_directory`, `out_dir`).
3. **Doc-comment attributes follow the krueger grammar.** An attribute name is `lower ("." lower)*` and its value is
   Elm data. The generator writes an `attributes` code block with `@morphir.entry { kind = "main", name = "..." }`,
   `@morphir.annotation { fqname = "...", ... }` and `@morphir.external { platform = "...", name = "..." }`.
4. **Constraint attribute.** Key `typeclass` in `TypeAttributes.constraints`. The value is `Text` or `Array` of
   `Text`. `["appendable", "comparable"]` becomes `compappend`. Any other set is `elm.unsupported_constraint`.
5. **More error codes.** `elm.int_literal` (lexeme outside Int64), `elm.document_literal`, `elm.literal_pattern`
   (float or decimal pattern, which Elm rejects), `elm.unsupported_constraint`, `elm.name_collision` (two IR names
   give one Elm name in a module), `elm.invalid_option`, `elm.cancelled`.
6. **Generation backend contract.** `GenerationBackend` gets `validate_options : (Json) -> Unit raise` and
   `targets : Array[String]`. A generator with no targets defaults to `pipeline.validation = "source-only"`, and
   `"required"` is refused with `build.unsupported_target`. The MoonBit generator declares
   `["wasm", "wasm-gc", "js", "native"]` and keeps its behavior.
7. **Built-in mapping source.** The table is generated from `pkgs/morphir-sdk/conformance/bindings.json`: every
   binding whose `semanticSource` is `elm/core 1.0.5` maps to the elm/core function of the same name, plus a
   hand-written list of types, constructors and operators. Other SDK references stay qualified.
8. **`elm.print` node path.** The path names the IR declaration whose AST did not print. The generator finds it by
   printing each declaration alone after `print_file` fails.
9. **No signatures on `let` functions.** Elm reads type variables in a `let` annotation as new rigid variables, so
   generated `let` functions have no signature.
10. **No shadowing.** Elm rejects a local name that shadows another name in scope. The lowering renames such names
    (`x` becomes `x_1`).
11. **Existing fixture corpus in engine tests.** The `finos/morphir-moonbit/fixtures` IR builders are already a
    dependency of `finos/morphir-engine` tests. The engine tests run the `elm` generator over them, so the Elm module
    does not depend on `finos/morphir-moonbit`.

# Elm backend with krueger: design

Date: 2026-10-02. Status: approved in brainstorming, waiting for written-spec review.

## 1. Purpose and context

This is sub-project 1 of the Elm initiative (see the umbrella epic). The initiative gives finos/morphir-moonbit an Elm
frontend and an Elm backend that use [moonrockz/krueger](https://github.com/moonrockz/krueger). The order is:

1. Elm backend (this spec): current Morphir IR to Elm source.
2. IR type inference: a language-neutral Hindley-Milner pass over Morphir IR.
3. Elm frontend: Elm source to typed Morphir IR, with parity against `morphir-elm make`.
4. Wiring: `morphir.json` project discovery, CLI and workbench.

The backend comes first. It gives a visible result quickly, it does not need type inference, and its output is the
round-trip harness for sub-projects 2 and 3.

krueger 0.4.0 parses Elm 0.19.1 into the elm-syntax 7.3.9 AST and prints an AST as Elm in the elm-format 0.8.7
layout (`print_file`, width 120 by default). The printer raises `PrintError` with a `NodePath` when an AST cannot
print as valid Elm. It prints doc comments but not regular comments.

### Success criteria

- `pipeline.backend = "elm"` generates an Elm project from current IR through `Engine::plan` and `Engine::execute`.
- In the `model` profile, `elm make` accepts the generated project for every fixture in the golden corpus that
  contains no refused construct.
- Every generated file parses with `krueger.parse_module` with no diagnostics, in both profiles.
- The same input gives the same output bytes.

## 2. Architecture

### Package

New workspace member `pkgs/morphir-elm`, module `finos/morphir-elm`. It depends on `finos/morphir-ir` and
`moonrockz/krueger@0.4.0`. Like `finos/morphir-moonbit`, it has no engine, host, filesystem, process or network
imports. This sub-project adds only `backend/`. Sub-project 3 adds `frontend/` beside it.

| Unit | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/names` | Morphir `Name`, `Path` and `FQName` to Elm identifiers and module names. The Elm module name is the package path followed by the module path. Reserved words get the suffix `_`. Constrained type variables get their Elm prefix. |
| `backend/mapping` | The `Mapping` table from `FQName` to `Operator`, `Function` or `Type`, each with an optional import. It holds the built-in partial SDK table, merges overrides and removes entries. |
| `backend/lower` | Current IR types, values, patterns and definitions to krueger AST. The profile decides how references resolve. |
| `backend/project` | One `.elm` file for each IR module, plus `elm.json` and `morphir.json`. |
| `backend/generate` | Entry point `generate(Input, Options) -> Output`. Calls `@printer.print_file` for each module. Raises `ElmGenerationError`. |

`Options` holds `profile`, `placeholders`, `width`, `elm_package`, `mapping` and `packages` (section 4).

### Engine changes

- `GenerationBackend.generate` gets a third parameter: the backend options table from `[backends.<name>]`.
- A generation backend supplies a schema for its table. The engine validates the table and reports unknown keys and
  bad values as configuration diagnostics, with the provenance from `config.Document`.
- The MoonBit generator accepts the new parameter and ignores it. Its behavior does not change.
- `Engine::new` registers the generation backend `elm` beside `moonbit`.

### Out of scope

The frontend, type inference, `morphir.json` discovery, CLI flags other than configuration, workbench UI, regular
comments, and the IR to Elm to IR round trip. The round trip comes with sub-project 3.

## 3. Profiles and SDK mapping

There are two profiles.

- `model` (default) generates a Morphir Elm model project. References with a mapping entry use idiomatic Elm, for
  example `+` for `morphir/SDK:basics#add` and `List.map` for `morphir/SDK:list#map`. This is the inverse of the
  morphir-elm frontend.
- `literal` ignores the mapping. Every reference stays fully qualified, for example
  `Morphir.SDK.Basics.add a b`. It is a debug view of the IR.

The `model` profile does not need a full mapping of the Morphir SDK. The built-in table covers only the references
that have a clear Elm idiom. A reference with no mapping entry stays a qualified reference with its `import`, for
example `Morphir.SDK.LocalDate.addDays`. The `finos/morphir-elm` Elm package supplies those modules, and
`backend/project` adds it to `elm.json` only when the generated code uses an unmapped `Morphir.SDK` reference. A
missing mapping entry never stops generation.

The mapping is data. Configuration can override or extend the built-in table for any `FQName`, not only SDK
references, so a user can map references in their own package to existing Elm code. An empty entry removes a built-in
entry, and the reference falls back to the qualified form.

## 4. Configuration

```toml
[pipeline]
backend = "elm"

[backends.elm]
profile = "model"            # "model" (default) | "literal"
placeholders = "refuse"      # "refuse" (default) | "debug-todo"
width = 120
elm-package = "finos/morphir-elm 22.0.2"

[backends.elm.mapping]
"morphir/SDK:basics#add" = { operator = "+" }
"morphir/SDK:list#map" = { function = "List.map" }
"morphir/SDK:decimal#decimal" = { type = "Decimal.Decimal", import = "MyCo.Decimal as Decimal" }
"morphir/SDK:basics#max" = {}

[backends.elm.packages]
"acme/common" = { package = "acme/common 1.0.0" }
"acme/local" = { source = "../acme-local/src" }
```

- `elm-package` is the Elm package and version for unmapped `Morphir.SDK` references. The default is the
  `finos/morphir-elm` version in that repository's `elm.json` (22.0.2 on 2026-10-02). The implementation plan
  confirms that the version is published on package.elm-lang.org before it becomes the default.
- A `mapping` key is an IR `FQName` in canonical text form. A value has exactly one of `operator`, `function` or
  `type`, and an optional `import`. A malformed key or value is the configuration diagnostic `invalid_mapping`.
- `packages` maps a Morphir dependency package to an Elm package with a version, or to a source directory, for
  `elm.json`. A dependency with no entry does not stop generation. The `elm make` check reports it.
- In the `literal` profile, a non-empty `mapping` gives a warning, not an error.

## 5. Lowering rules

### Distributions and modules

- `Library` and `Application` generate every module of the package. For `Application`, each entry point becomes the
  doc-comment attribute `@entryPoint <kind>` on its target value. krueger reads doc-comment attributes, so the
  frontend can restore entry points.
- `Specs` generate type declarations. Value specifications have no body, so they follow the placeholder policy.
- References into dependency packages stay qualified.
- Public types and values are exposed. Private ones are not. A custom type with private constructors is exposed as
  `T`, not `T(..)`.
- Module documentation becomes the module doc comment. Member documentation becomes the doc comment of the
  declaration.

### Types

- A `Reference` with a mapping entry uses it. Any other `Reference` is qualified.
- `Record`, `ExtensibleRecord`, `Function` and `Unit` map directly to their Elm forms.
- A `Tuple` with more than three elements is refused with `tuple_arity`. Elm 0.19 rejects such tuples.
- A type variable with a `constraints` entry in its `TypeAttributes` gets the Elm prefix of that constraint
  (`number`, `comparable`, `appendable` or `compappend`). An unconstrained variable whose name starts with one of
  these prefixes is renamed so that Elm does not read it as constrained.
- Type aliases stay aliases. Custom types keep their constructor order.
- Derived types are refused with `derived_type`. A follow-on bead covers them.

### Values

- A chain of `Apply` becomes one `Application`.
- A mapped operator with both arguments becomes an `OperatorApplication`. With fewer arguments it becomes a prefix
  operator, for example `(+) a`.
- `LetDefinition`, `LetRecursion` and `Destructure` merge into one `let` block where scoping allows.
- `FieldFunction` becomes `.field`.
- Elm requires a variable as the target of a record update. `UpdateRecord` with any other target binds the target to
  a fresh name in a `let` first.
- `Int` literals keep the exact lexeme. A value outside the Elm range is refused through the printer's
  `UnrepresentableInt`.
- `Decimal` literals are refused with `decimal_literal` until a construction mapping exists.
- Fresh names never capture names in scope.

### v4-only constructs

- `Annotation` becomes the doc-comment attribute `@<fqname> <arguments>`.
- `ExternalBody` with a fallback value emits the fallback, plus `@external <platform> <name>` for each binding.
- `Hole`, `IncompleteBody`, `NativeBody`, `ExternalBody` without a fallback, and `Specs` values follow the
  placeholder policy:
  - `placeholders = "refuse"` (default) raises `ElmGenerationError` with code `placeholder`.
  - `placeholders = "debug-todo"` emits `Debug.todo "<reason>"`. `elm make` accepts this, but
    `elm make --optimize` does not.

### Determinism

Declarations keep IR order. Imports are sorted. The same input and options give the same bytes.

## 6. Errors

`ElmGenerationError { code, node_path, detail }`, where `node_path` identifies the IR node. The codes are:

| Code | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `tuple_arity` | Tuple with more than three elements |
| `derived_type` | Derived type definition |
| `decimal_literal` | Decimal literal with no construction mapping |
| `placeholder` | Construct with no body while `placeholders = "refuse"` |
| `invalid_mapping` | Mapping entry that is not valid at generation time, for example an operator that krueger does not know |
| `print` | krueger `PrintError`, with the IR node path of the AST node that failed |

A `print` error means that the lowering made an AST that is not valid, so it is a backend defect. Tests treat any
`print` error as a failure.

Generation of a module stops at its first error. All modules are tried, so one run reports every failing module.

## 7. Testing

- **Unit tests**: `names` (case, reserved words, constraint prefixes), `mapping` (merge, override, removal) and each
  lowering rule in both profiles, as snapshot tests of the printed Elm.
- **Golden corpus**: the classic v3 reference models in `pkgs/morphir-ir/conformance/fixtures` and the SDK examples,
  migrated to current IR and generated in both profiles. Output snapshots must be stable.
- **Parse-back law**: every generated file parses with `krueger.parse_module` with no diagnostics. This runs on all
  MoonBit targets.
- **`elm make` acceptance**: `pkgs/morphir-elm/scripts/test-elm-make.mjs` runs `elm make` on the generated `model`
  projects, with the npm `elm` 0.19.1 package pinned in `package.json`. Mise task `test:elm` runs it, in the same
  pattern as `test:compiler`, and CI runs the task. `literal` output gets only the parse-back law.
- **Engine tests**: options table pass-through, schema validation and diagnostics, and `elm` registration through
  `Engine::plan` and `Engine::execute`. The MoonBit generator tests stay unchanged and must pass.

## 8. Follow-on work

- Derived types (`derived_type`) and decimal literal construction (`decimal_literal`).
- Sub-projects 2, 3 and 4 of the initiative.

Delivery & proof

Reconciled on 02 October 2026 against merged main 40587e6. E1 generation landed in PR #31; E2 Tasks 1–3 in PR #32, lifecycle Task 4 in PR #34 and independent conformance Task 5 in PR #35. PR #36 merged structured results, typed fields/JSON/Ion inputs, live Rust v1 acceptance and portable CLI parsing after incorporating both execution phases. All 16 final-head checks, full local checks and explicit conformance acceptance passed. The upstream profile now has merged decode/declared-value contracts and published invocation admission in PRs #1035/#44. Output/outcome admission is the next contract slice, followed by broader semantic coverage and host adoption.

Completion checklist

Checked boxes indicate completed work within the stated scope. Unchecked boxes indicate remaining work, including work in progress. A local implementation can be complete while its merge remains pending. These read-only indicators reflect evidence in the shared tracker, not editable task state.

Completed

Pending and in progress

The public manifest governs admitted entries; tagged arguments use morphir-invocations-v1, and the shared bounded Scheme evaluator returns canonical typed values. Exact Int/Decimal, signed-zero Float64 bits, UTF-16 units, Maybe/Result, records and custom ownership have focused acceptance. Browser and packaged CEF import the pricing fixture. Typed convenience controls are complete and merged in PR #36 in morphir-ukvn.5.17. Generated-code execution and connected transport remain pending. Local IR text is retained across the JavaScript boundary for exact large-integer evaluation, inspection and export.

Stage / statusNext deliverableEvidence to proceed

Keep the result-view continuation identified separately.Existing browser/CEF workflows remain green; drafts, selection, sidebar context, cancellation, stale results and exact numbers survive integration.

New operations stay unavailable until negotiated. Current v1 methods preserve their shapes.
Use engine plan/run and host-owned provider sessions through Proton IPC. Reuse compiler acquisition/pins and generated drivers. A standalone generated-code browser lane needs an explicit provider backed by verified browser embedding.Selected capabilities and dependency snapshots match the host; no target substitution. Browser workers never import the Node/native process provider. LLVM requires its separate tested nightly/core pin and verified host. Existing Proton worker mode stays supported.
Reuse Engine::list_projects, plan boundaries, IRUnit codecs, host grants and artifact reports. Keep source/model snapshots alongside display projections. Wait for E2 lifecycle/publication acceptance before offering verification-backed publication.Ion metadata and identities survive processing; Morphir JSON remains supported through explicit loss-aware boundaries. Run the same versioned fixture intersection through standalone, native and connected adapters; add recovery, persistence and platform package checks.E2 Tasks 4–6 are complete and merged, including lifecycle, independent conformance, installed/debug-release CI and native OTLP HTTP/JSON collector acceptance on Linux/macOS. Shared-SDK Scheme agreement is identified accurately; cross-host adoption and other telemetry protocols remain separate. Connected durability/replay is proved separately.

Integration rules from the merges

  • Reuse the public invocation manifest as the generated execution authority. Local generic aliases and dynamic Scheme values may remain available through their own runtime capability even when the generator rejects them.
  • Separate 200-node input forms and 500-node result display limits from execution budgets. Preserve full semantic values and Ion metadata; report unsupported or omitted presentation explicitly.
  • Exact comparison is the default. Approximate comparison requires an explicit policy and finite tolerances. Display selected target, evaluator profile and evidence; do not label shared-SDK agreement independent conformance.
  • Host-injected observations carry timing and correlation outside model/call identity. Required results bypass telemetry queues. Payload capture stays opt-in with a redactor; dropped observations cannot change a job outcome.
  • Model Result.Err, enumerated SDK model errors, validation failures, provider failures, cancellation and cleanup failures need distinct presentation. Preserve primary and cleanup causes once the E2 lifecycle contract lands.

Acceptance checklist

Build and assets

Build the UI for JavaScript, stage its CSS and worker assets, then consume that distribution from the static web deployment, daemon asset server, and Proton package. Bundle required assets locally for standalone and installed use.

Proton's CLI/runtime/framework versions stay aligned. Match embedded compiler and dependency interfaces to the repository's pinned toolchain. Verify packages on each supported OS.

Focused verification

Use MoonBit checks and formatting for package boundaries and target support. Run contract scenarios against each adapter. Browser checks verify the real workflow, responsiveness, focus, and cancellation.

For desktop, include installed-package smoke checks for asset lookup, the native bridge, workspace grants, and platform editing shortcuts. Timing numbers are measured during the slice, not assumed in this design.

Main 1f8c9ad adds the shared-worktree beads database check and requires new or changed task automation to use portable MoonBit scripts. It is incorporated into this continuation at merge 775f704; mise run beads:check passes. The existing browser/desktop UI is unaffected.

The actual standalone WASI artifact fails the existing import gate. Core Command::parse retains its optional default-argv branch, which links __moonbit_fs_unstable argument and external-string imports even when the application supplies argv explicitly. The WASI contract currently permits only wasi_snapshot_preview1 imports. Unit tests under MoonBit runtime do not establish WASI embedding compatibility.

The adopted Yoorkin/ArgParser integration, documented below, preserves the existing WASI-only contract and now passes full CLI acceptance. Keep JSON/JSON-lines help and error envelopes, exact values, pipeline last-value overrides and child --help/--json/empty/Unicode arguments in either implementation. The official argparse quickstart demonstrates explicit argv for native CLIs; the artifact-level portability finding comes from local builds.

Alternative parser comparison

Target support is the acceptance requirement. Candidate probes use the repository-pinned MoonBit toolchain and explicit argv. Yoorkin/ArgParser has now passed the full CLI integration described below; other candidates retain only their stated probe evidence.
